The review of this unit re-measured it (quarry-rust-env:1, 20 cores, same lib binary): the full lib at default threads failed 2 of 12 runs (the 12 include one workspace run that passed), at `--test-threads=4` 1 of 10, at `--test-threads=2` 0 of 3 and at `--test-threads=1` 0 of 3; the module filter `scrape_challenge_tests` at default threads failed 35 of 43 runs and at `--test-threads=1` 0 of 15; the single-test filter 0 of 25. The failure is not a miscount: in the captured module failure the assertion at `pipeline.rs:2855` reported left 0 and right 1 with an empty event list, so the refusal happened (the `result.is_err()` assertion before it passed) and the test's `EventLog` received no event at all. Suspected mechanism, NOT verified by experiment: the callsites `quarry.challenge.scrape_refused` (`pipeline.rs:843`) and `would_refuse_scrape` (`pipeline.rs:859`) are first registered concurrently by other tests that have no subscriber, and tracing-core 0.1.36 can keep that stale never-interest after a concurrent `set_default`, which drops the event before dispatch. CI runs `cargo test --workspace`, so it can fail there. Not fixed: the test is outside this unit's paths; the fix is to isolate the log-capture assertions (an own integration-test binary, or one lock shared by every test that reaches those two callsites; `tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache()` right after `set_default` is an untested option that narrows the window but does not close it) and then confirm with about 50 module-only runs and 20 full-lib runs at default threads. **Superseded: fixed by `d711a1bb`** (round 4, see the B-T2 row; the mechanism was the suspected one, the fix keeps two `NoSubscriber` dispatchers alive and lives in the test module, and the module and the full lib then failed 0 of 20 runs each). |

### Errata: claims in commit messages that were false or inaccurate

Commits cannot be amended on this branch (and are not rewritten), so each claim that a later check disproved is listed here, one line each: the commit, what it said, what is true. Each was checked against `git show` or the code on 2026-10-19 (the round-4 entries on 2026-10-20); where a later commit already corrected it, that commit is named.

- `5f90ae3a`: said the "Scrape cleaning cost" RUNBOOKS section is "in the next commit". It first reached the branch in `37b7ebb0`.
- `37b7ebb0`: names only the WS3.F docs. The commit also carries the whole "Scrape cleaning cost" section of WS5.E (`git show --stat`: ERROR_REASONS.md +26, RUNBOOKS.md +35), because the shared file was staged as a whole.
- `c2b3d2e9`: said RUNBOOKS.md got "8 added lines and 0 removed". `git show --numstat` gives 11 and 3: it also carried three browser lines of WS3.F's uncommitted review round, which ran ahead of the code until `c8c31a26` (`329d2b98`, `b2db250e`).
- `2046644e`: said every agent action during a take-over gets 409 `USER_TOOK_OVER`. Tab select and close took no initiator and were admitted (finding F5-4); corrected by `7b2ad43f`, fixed by `486bbd28` and gateway `44450389`.
- `ff1be0f6`: said `durable_jobs` and `agent_persistent_profile` both cite the two enforced-refusal tests. `agent_persistent_profile` never cited the durable-jobs test (`264832dd`).
- `bb951ab5`: said a matrix table change that is not regenerated, or a hand-edited golden, fails the repo-level drift check. Only the second is true: the sync script reads only the committed golden bytes (a hand edit changes the digest), while a table change is caught by `quarry-core`'s `the_golden_and_markdown_are_what_the_table_generates`, and `contract-goldens.yml` had no path entry for the golden (`41b3a9cf`).
- `6b9c636a`, `89c67974`: regenerated the matrix golden without moving the digest pinned in `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`, so that script failed at HEAD from `6b9c636a` on (48 passed, 1 failed); fixed by `13c6f5ac`.
- `4e82894b`: said the classifier tests "replay recorded HTML". Every fixture is hand-written; nothing recorded exists (`de6c83f9`).
- `97186586`: said `sdks/.gitignore` keeps `src/`, `dist/` and the Python client out of the repository. That file does not exist; the rules are in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/.gitignore`.
- `a9a71f4e`: said the regenerated diff is the basis line in each of the three generated files. In the `.sha256` pin file the changed line is the digest.
- `0997b7c8`: said 14 tests in `grant/derive_test.go` and 7 in `server/derive_test.go`. At that commit the files hold 15 and 8 `func Test`.
- `6da7ffd8`: said a retried start cannot mint a second grant. Every start had a fresh `run_key`, so a retry was a second run with a second grant (`33a362f6`); it is true only for a keyed retry since `e4af12cb`.
- `df7feedf`, `1db86f58`: said the converted request-path failures "stay visible" to a ZDR caller and that 23 R2 sites were left in `quarry-runtime` and `quarry-browser`. Two converted warns still carried `url` or `host` and stayed invisible, `quarry-browser` had no site, and two of the 23 were outside `quarry-runtime` (`67cff1f3`). `df7feedf` alone also leaves `log_field_discipline` red until `1db86f58` (its own message says so).
- `67cff1f3`: said the log baseline went to total 48 and 21 keys. The figures are 44 and 18 (`89c67974`).
- `9a2bc002`: said four new `RUST_LOG` tests were red on the old registry-level wiring and named the level-filter test among them. Seven `zdr_log` tests failed, three of the four named; the level-filter test is a control that passes on both wirings (`3aac8a8a`).
- `2042c391`, `63b64619`: said `693 passed + 1 ignored (bin)`. That was the total over all gateway binaries; the bin alone was 676 passed, 1 ignored (`d8a9708d`).
- `77749d34`: said `110 passed, 4 ignored`. That was counted on a tree that already held the five live tests of `b86a32c8`; the tree of `77749d34` has 109 test functions, 105 passed (`c8c31a26`).
- `217fc548`: said 149 lib tests in `quarry-transform`. The tree at that commit had 144 (`4c4e4226`).
- `14eb0367`: said truncated streams are not counted and that images are not counted. A truncated stream counts the bytes it inflated, image-labelled streams have their own 384 MiB budget, and the scan was quadratic (`4c4e4226`); four spellings that lopdf reads were also invisible to it (`9f08f7e1`).
- `d8e62fa3`: said the scrape-path wall check runs "before extraction". It runs after the markdown conversion and the metadata pass, whose results are dropped; nothing stored or returned precedes it. It also made `enforce` the default; the default is `log` since `1b1a9810`.
- `e50046a9`: does not build on its own. Its `main.rs` hunk calls `slots::session_cap_warnings`, which `slots.rs` gained only in `0b86c8c6` (`git show e50046a9:` the file has no such function; the branch tip builds).
- `fd049304`: said "HEAD 9867a8be plus this change". Its parent is `3aac8a8a` (`9867a8be` is an ancestor).
- Trailers: the requested trailer is `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5`. 43 of the 152 commits in `bed81d16..13c6f5ac` carry `Claude Haiku 5.5` instead (all in the first two rounds, none after `fd049304`).
- `1c5f000a`: said its L1 test pins "no ephemeral flag in the base file". The guard's regex, `/^s+BROWSER_BROKER_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_DEVELOPMENT:/m`, matches the letter `s` and never whitespace, so it could not match an indented key and passed on any file (`git show 1c5f000a:scripts/tests/browser-grant-contract.test.mjs`, line 294). The base compose file has no such flag, so the conclusion held; the corrected regex, a self-test that it matches an indented key and a mutation run are in `b40242f7`.
- `1c5f000a`, `e25d9ec0`: said the separate database and role "keep the data apart (no direct database crossing)" and that `CONNECT` is revoked from PUBLIC "so no other role can open it". A superuser ignores that revoke, and every Quarry service connects as `ingestion_user`, the container's superuser (`POSTGRES_USER: ingestion_user` on the `postgres` service of `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml`), so Quarry itself can read and write `browser_grants`; only ordinary roles are kept out. The wording was corrected in the deploy note and, by `08d07ad2`, in the script header, the `init-databases.sql` comment and the migration comment; the commits cannot be.
- `e25d9ec0`: said the password is "never on a command line". The `--mint-if-missing` step wrote it into the env file with `sed -i -E "s|^KEY=...|KEY=${pw}...|"` (`git show e25d9ec0:"apps/Ingestion Plane/scripts/bootstrap_broker_db.sh"`, line 84), so a freshly generated password was on `sed`'s argv; only the SQL (stdin) and the `PGPASSWORD` hand-off (by name) avoided it. The fix is `08d07ad2` (shell builtins and `cat`; the test records the argv of every external command and the password is in none).
- `2aa92fbc`: said a 412 from the run-control endpoint means ZDR run controls are off, and closed the session on any 412 (`run_stop_outcome` mapped `PRECONDITION_FAILED` to `ControlsDisabled`). model-gateway also maps a gRPC `FailedPrecondition` of the cancel itself to 412, so a 412 for another reason closed the session while the run might still be going. Corrected by `137ba2ac`, which reads a 412 as "controls off" only when the owner's text starts with "ZDR browser-run controls are disabled".

## W1 build wave: closeout (2026-10-23)

W1 is built to the plan's scope and is NOT proven to the plan's evidence bar. 38 of the 39 W1 slices are built; WS3.J is built in this branch for its Quarry, gateway and SPA halves, and its Model Plane half (4 of its 6 days) is handed to the Model Plane session (branch `model-plane`, commit `e336de32`; its live proof is owed). That is 144.25 of 148.25 engineer-days built. Days verified at L2: 0. Days fully verified at rebuilt-image level: 6.0 (WS1.A0, WS4.K, WS5.C, all on images older than HEAD), 8.5 with WS4.F, whose DoD is a CI lint test. SC1 to SC7 are all NOT-RUN: none is PASS and none is FAIL by a run. No image of the final tree was built and no stack was run for evidence in the wave; that depth work was deferred on purpose by the user's build strategy of 2026-10-23 (build the wave first, depth later), not forgotten.

A wave test phase ran once at the end with the default features and the big suites skipped on purpose (live Chromium lane, Postgres and integration suites, quarry-browser, `--features grpc`, Model Plane crates): `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean; 2323 Rust tests pass in quarry-core, -transform, -security, -runtime and -edge; Go tests pass in browser-broker, quarry-orchestrator and quarry-control; node 138 and 23 pass; `zdr-contract-sync` 65; gateway `cargo test` 778; auth-core registry specs 101. Not green: 6 SPA vitest files never started (worker timeout), `tsc -b` shows the 33 baseline errors, `principal-registry-parity.test.sh` timed out at 1000 s after 21 ok. The runs were made on a shared tree that also held W2 units' uncommitted edits.

Where to read more (files in the worktree under `.plan-work/quarry-w1w2/`, which is not committed): `W1-closeout.md` (one row per slice: built with commits, reviewed, evidence level, what is left and of which kind; the numbers; the SC1 to SC7 table; the wave test phase) and `DEPTH-FINDINGS-W1.md` (87 rows: 16 high, 64 medium, 7 low themes, with a recommended order). ## Plan at a glance

1. **Goal.** Make Quarry v2 a Firecrawl-plus-Apify-class acquisition platform and make Verevon's in-app browser one governed browser that users and the Model share. The Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects; Firecrawl is a reference, never a runtime dependency; ZDR propagates through every content-persisting boundary.
2. **Workstreams.** 17 (WS1 to WS17), 166 slices in 15 lanes (the 162 of the first draft plus WS1.A0, the WS1.A split into WS1.A1 and WS1.A2, WS4.K and WS14.S0b, the hard Go CI job). Most missing capability is built-but-unwired code, so the plan wires before it builds.
3. **W1, unblock and make safe.** WS1 to WS5 plus the WS6.A crawl-bound hotfix: 148.25 engineer-days (132.25 core, 16 gated), 6.6 to 8.6 weeks at 6.5 engineers. The first draft counted 125.75 (113.75 core, 12 gated); the review re-estimated WS1.A (16 d), WS2.C (10 d), WS3.F (10 d) and WS6.A (3.5 d), added WS1.A0 (1.5 d) and WS4.K (0.5 d), and moved WS5.C (4 d) from optional to gated.
4. **W2, table-stakes parity.** WS6 to WS17 plus WS3.K (actionability): 510.5 engineer-days (447.5 core, 63 gated; WS14.S0b adds 0.5 d), 14 to 19 weeks at 12 engineers; beyond about 14 engineers the critical path binds.
5. **W3 to W5 as epics.** 21 W3 items (20 in epics E3.1 to E3.9; F-t2-046 is carried by WS6), 16 W4 items (E4.1 to E4.7), 12 W5 items (E5.1 to E5.3; F-t2-077 parked). None is estimated in the totals.
6. **Critical path.** The shared browser, 50 engineer-days: WS1.A1, WS1.B, WS8.F, WS8.H, WS8.I, WS8.J (13 to 18 weeks risk-adjusted). WS1.A2 (6 d) and WS1.A0 are off the path because WS1.B depends on WS1.A1 only, but production use of the shared browser waits for them (X-1). WS2.A is not on the path.
7. **First three PRs** (hunk-disjoint, not file-disjoint: PR 1 and PR 2 both edit `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/knowledge/quarry.rs` in non-overlapping regions, so PR 1 merges first; PR 2 needs the uncommitted baseline at position 0; stage hunks by hand): PR 1 WS4.A gateway result cache org scope and ZDR bypass, together with WS4.K (the Quarry `PageCache` org key); PR 2 WS6.A crawl bounds; PR 3 PRE-2 (production dev-bypass and artifact-backend gates made case-insensitive). WS2.A (deny raw page script `evaluate` on every agent entry point) is PR 4.
8. **Decisions that block.** X-1 (register `quarry-edge` as a read-only `browser-broker` principal) blocks the merge of WS1.A2 (not WS1.A1) and every production browser path; ADR-3 (shared human-plus-agent sessions) gates WS8.C, WS8.F, WS8.G and the whole critical path from W2; ADR-1 (policy of record) gates the org-layer slices of WS7. Alongside them sits one process action: commit or branch the uncommitted baseline (X-3).
9. **W1 exit gate.** PRE-1 (baseline committed) and PRE-2 done; WS1.A0, WS1.A1, WS1.A2, WS1.B and WS1.C with `BROWSER_GRANT_ENFORCEMENT=strict` on the production-overlay stack (the real `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml` [M] plus `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.production.yml` [C], with the test-only contract overlay allowed to set env and volumes only; WS3.A is a dependency of that L2 run), WS2.A to WS2.E, WS3.A to WS3.F, WS3.H, WS3.J, WS4.A to WS4.G and WS4.K with the cache purge recorded, WS5.A to WS5.H (WS5.C, moved from optional to gated, is the X-14 Q1 gate for the production default `DOC_ROUTING=on`), WS6.A (crawl bounds, counted in the W1 total); all deployed on rebuilt local images. Section 1.2 says which success criteria this gate closes.
10. **Rollout.** Every behaviour change ships behind a default-off or observe-mode flag. Production flags flip only after an L2 run (rebuilt images, running stack, verified end-to-end flow) is recorded in the PR; a deployment claim counts on no weaker evidence.
11. **Out of scope.** Channel Plane, Firecrawl as a dependency, stealth and anti-bot bypass, MCP exposure, per-session VMs, Space members driving another member's browser, unattended browser runs, credential vaulting in pages.
12. **Totals.** W1 plus W2 is roughly 5 to 7 months end to end: 167 to 228 risk-adjusted engineer-weeks (W1 34 to 44, W2 133 to 184; the first draft said 162 to 221).

## 1. Goal, success criteria and scope

Owners: workstream and decision owners are plane roles in this draft; naming individuals is open question OQ-owners in 7.1.

### 1.1 Goal

Verevon's web layer has two halves that must become one product. The first is an acquisition API (scrape, crawl, batch, search, monitors, schedules) at the level of Firecrawl and Apify. The second is a remote, leased Chromium that users and the Model share, at the level of the Codex in-app browser and Aside. This plan turns the audit's 77 recommendations (24 Priority, 35 Recommended, 18 Nice-to-have; none already done) into slices that can be built, reviewed and deployed.

Three constraints bind every slice.

- **The Model proposes; Quarry executes or rejects.** Quarry validates a grant before every action, takes one governed action per `/step`, and is the final enforcer of takeover, raw-script denial, budgets and policy. Nothing on the Model Plane side may widen what Quarry allows.
- **Firecrawl is not a runtime dependency.** It is a reference for parity only. No Firecrawl SDK, API or fire-engine call is added anywhere, and parity docs are corrected to what the code does.
- **ZDR propagates.** Zero data retention reaches every boundary that can persist content: gateway caches, logs, spans, receipts, artifacts, checkpoints, schedules, profiles and AI formats. A refusal that exists today is never loosened. The detail is decision ADR-4 and workstream WS4.

Plane ownership is unchanged (`apps/master-ownership-matrix.md` [C]). Control Plane owns identity, billing, entitlements and the principal registry; Model Plane owns the BrowserBroker, grants, runs and cost; Ingestion Plane (Quarry v2) owns acquisition and browser execution and persists knowledge only through Data Plane contracts; Frontend Plane owns the SPA and the same-origin gateway; Application Plane owns projections and notifications. No database is crossed between planes, and Space access may only narrow an owner-plane decision.

The audit's ten headline findings map to the workstreams as follows: no production browser path and no grants (WS1), cross-tenant gateway search cache and ZDR gaps (WS4), takeover and raw script ungated inside Quarry (WS2), budgets not enforced and unbounded crawl (WS6, WS14), crawl without scope or robots (WS14), thin scrape contract and empty ZDR scrape (WS5), half-built shared browser (WS8, WS9), secrets unmasked (WS12, WS17), one Chromium relaunching on viewport change (WS3). The remaining workstreams (WS7, WS10, WS11, WS13, WS15, WS16) deliver the parity features on top.

### 1.2 Measurable success criteria

Twelve criteria define done for W1 and W2; SC2 is stated in two parts so that each part can close at the exit that can prove it. The table after the criteria says which exit closes which. Evidence types: **CI** hermetic test in CI; **L2** live production-overlay stack run on rebuilt images, recorded in the PR; **LOG** log or artifact scan with a canary; **PROBE** scripted adversarial request.

| # | Criterion (pass condition) | Measured by | Workstreams |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC1 | **Prod-mode browser path works.** With `APP_ENV=production` quarry-edge, a signed-in user's UI session and an AI run both start, act and close with zero 401/403 and zero grant-less fallbacks; a revoked or expired grant is 403 `SECURITY_BLOCKED`, not a 5xx; gateway `BROWSER_GRANT_ENFORCEMENT=strict` is the production default; no service principal holds `browser:write`. The L2 stack is `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml` [M] plus `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.production.yml` [C] plus the contract overlay `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.grant-contract.yml` [NEW]; the overlay may only set env and volumes and never removes a production hardening key (read-only root, `cap_drop`, tmpfs set). WS1.A0 makes the production overlay boot quarry-edge, and WS3.A (sandbox on, writable Chromium root) is a dependency of the SC1 L2 run: the PR records `ps` on that stack showing zero `--no-sandbox` and a `navigate` step returning 200. | L2 (Playwright API legs A to E plus log-scan wrapper); CI L1 contract test | WS1, WS3.A |
| SC2a | **Raw script and takeover enforced inside Quarry (W1).** `AgentAction::Evaluate` on `/step` is 403 `raw_script_denied` for every principal. With `QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT=1` on the evidence stack, a user token labelled `initiated_by:"agent"` gets 409 `USER_TOOK_OVER` during a takeover and succeeds after give back; the refusal of a service principal is proved by the claims-injecting integration test, because a stack-level proof needs a service-principal token that exists only after the WS11 mapping. The flag ships `0` (observe) until WS11.D lands; the exit evidence names the value it ran with. | CI `admission_order_is_pinned`, contracts golden; L2 live takeover with the user token | WS2, WS13 |
| SC2b | **The Model Plane run pauses (W2).** An agent step during `HumanTakeover` returns 409 `USER_TOOK_OVER` and the Model Plane run pauses with its checkpoint rather than failing; `QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT` is set to `1` in the default stack once this holds. | L2 live takeover with a Model Plane run (WS11.D) | WS11 (mapping) |
| SC3 | **No leaked or runaway runs.** An abandoned run frees its Chromium context within its class idle TTL (agent 300 s, interactive 900 s) and keeps a resumable checkpoint; the (cap+1)th concurrent run of an org is 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` and `details.reason`; `close_run` releases the session even with a viewer attached; a run stuck behind a viewer still hits the 4 h backstop. | CI sweeper and registry tests; L2 RSS at 8, 16 and 32 contexts (the RSS runs set `QUARRY_BROWSER_MAX_SESSIONS=48` in the test env file, so that 32 run contexts plus the heavy lane and interactive sessions never meet the session cap while RSS is measured; the shipped defaults are 40 sessions against 32 runs, see R-26) | WS2, WS6 |
| SC4 | **Driver stability.** A viewport mismatch between two sessions does not kill the other's pages (relaunch counter stays 0); a hung CDP call returns typed `TIMEOUT` with `details.effect` within its deadline and never wedges the slot; the production overlay launches Chromium with the sandbox on; a challenge page is a block outcome with at most one recovery and no stealth code remains. | CI SlotBook and deadline tests; L2 two-session viewport probe, sandbox launch | WS3 |
| SC5 | **ZDR and tenant boundary.** Org B querying an org A cached search gets no hit; org B sending org A's page fingerprint as `prev_fingerprint` to `/v1/scrape` gets a miss from the Quarry `PageCache` (WS4.K); ZDR search is neither read nor written from the gateway cache; a ZDR scrape and ZDR agent step write zero log lines containing URL, title, host or query, with one canary per route family in the matrix or the row marked `log-unverified`; the published ZDR matrix is generated from the Rust `ROWS` table, whose completeness against the registered routes is enforced by a CI scan (axum has no route attributes), and every pinned gap row has a behavioural test; a ZDR scrape returns inline markdown and writes zero artifacts. | LOG canary scan across edge, gateway and orchestrator; CI `cache_admission_only`, `log_field_discipline`, `zdr_behavior`, `zdr_claim_floor`, `page_cache_is_not_readable_across_orgs`; PROBE cross-org (search cache and page fingerprint) | WS4 (A to G, K), WS5 |
| SC6 | **One strict scrape contract.** `/v1/scrape` returns the requested formats inline; PDF and DOCX URLs return extracted text; image and archive URLs are 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA`; unknown keys warn, then (after the strict date) 400 with `error.details.fields[]`; `GET /v1/scrape/{id}` is org-bound; a JSON Schema golden pins the contract. `DOC_ROUTING=on` is the production default only once WS5.C (the child-process parser, 4 d) has landed; WS5.C is part of the W1 exit gate for that reason (X-14 Q1), and until it lands the L2 PDF and DOCX proof runs with `DOC_ROUTING=on` on the evidence stack only. | CI schema golden, golden fixtures; L2 PDF and DOCX fixtures through the stack with `DOC_ROUTING=on` | WS5 (A to H, including WS5.C), WS13 |
| SC7 | **Budgets and capacity stop work.** A budget-exhausted agent run stops with 402 `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, partial results kept and the run resumable; a failed action still counts against attempts; a crawl request with `max_pages: 0` or no `max_pages` gets the finite default (1000) and the response shows `limits.max_pages.clamped_by:["default"]`, so every crawl has a finite page, depth and failure bound (the W1 pass condition, WS6.A); direct-to-edge `0` is refused with a 400 only after `QUARRY_EDGE__CRAWL_REQUEST_VALIDATION=strict` (WS14.G adds the flag, WS14.I flips it); manual (Interactive) sessions are never capped by agent budgets; every run response shows `constraints` and `clamped[]`; usage events exist for browser seconds, crawl pages and extraction. | CI; L2 budget exhaustion on the stack; billing metric codes confirmed | WS6, WS14, WS11 (token cap) |
| SC8 | **Crawl is scoped, polite and policy-bounded.** A crawl with an external link stays in scope by default; a robots-denied URL is not fetched and appears in the job's `denials` with a remedy; `Crawl-delay` feeds the scheduler; org policy can only tighten (a `RequestAsk` that widens is unrepresentable; the Model cannot set `ignore_robots_txt`); an override use writes an audit event before the job is acknowledged. | CI policy-meet property tests, `RobotsGate`; L2 fixture site with robots and an external link | WS14, WS7 |
| SC9 | **One shared browser.** A user browses past one host and past 120 s on a `human_browse` session; an AI run attaches to the user's visible tab, acts only in its pinned tab under the attach allow-list, and the user can Take over (agent gets `USER_TOOK_OVER`), Give back, Reveal and Stop; a Space member cannot attach to or view another user's session; the dock shows chat beside the page. | L2 attach flow and invariants I1 to I8; CI route-table scope test; Playwright (dock) | WS8, WS9, WS1, WS2 |
| SC10 | **Secrets never leave capture.** A seeded password and a seeded cookie value appear in no `/v1/*` JSON response, receipt, event, log line, planner prompt, stored artifact or stored screenshot (masked rectangles); the owner's live frame stream is explicitly excluded (X-19), and Space members receive receipts only. A PROBE asserts that the exclusion is exactly the `frames/stream` and `frames/ws` routes and nothing else; profiles are encrypted at rest with the DEK wrapped under an org KEK; a profile owned by user A is 404 to user B; service principals get 403 on `/v1/profiles*`; `GET /v1/profiles/:id` returns structure with `value: null`. | LOG and PROBE canary; CI `secret-shapes.v1.json` golden (both copies) and rule version; L2 | WS12, WS17 |
| SC11 | **Jobs have a lifecycle and schedules execute.** `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`, cancel, pause, resume, errors and a live tail work for scrape, crawl and batch with typed `timed_out`; a created schedule fires exactly once per window under Temporal and a skipped fire records a typed reason; a cross-tenant schedule id is 404; a ZDR org cannot create a schedule or monitor (after enforcement); the SPA hides what the backend cannot honour. | L2 Temporal schedule fire on the stack; CI; PROBE cross-tenant | WS15, WS14, WS4 |
| SC12 | **One canonical run trace and governed extraction.** A browser run's trace (receipts, egress decisions, artifacts, control changes) is readable from `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/trace` as `model_plane.v1.Event`s ordered by `producer_seq`, with a request id from SPA to Quarry and none for ZDR runs; `formats:[{type:"json",schema}]` returns schema-valid, verbatim-verified JSON through the governed model lane, with a typed refusal under ZDR and `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` when over budget. | L2 trace round trip and extraction on the stack; CI trace allowlist golden | WS10, WS16, WS11 |

## 2. Decisions first

Nothing in this plan waits for a decision to start. Every decision below has a recommended default that lets dependent slices be written and tested, and each record names what proceeds without it and what it gates (merge, production enablement or a default flip). Decisions are grouped by the first thing they block. Ids: `ADR-1..10` are the audit's section 9.3 topics; `OQ-1..15` are its section 10.2 open questions (those that restate an ADR point to it); `X-n` are decisions the designs raised that the audit does not list. Slice ids are the catalogue's letter ids (`WS7.H` is design D7's S7).

### 2.1 Decision summary table

"Blocks" says what the decision holds up: **W1 merge** (a W1 slice cannot merge), **W1 enable** (the slice merges, but a production default or flag flip waits), **W1 evidence** (a spike, not a ruling), **W2 merge**, **W2 enable**, **Later** (W3 and beyond). Blocking decisions come first. Where the architecture memo's gate list is stricter than the sequencing memo's `GATED` flags (WS1.A2, WS8.F, WS8.G, the WS5.B default, WS12.D, WS9.H, WS17.D), the stricter list is used.

The answer "ok" to a question accepts its recommended default.

### 2.2 Decision records

Each record states the question, the options, the recommendation, what it gates and what proceeds without it. Evidence was re-opened in the live tree for the citations that carry a tag; where a line range drifted, the corrected range is given. Confirmed in the live tree: production `quarry-edge` refuses to start without a BrowserBroker validator (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/main.rs` [M] 183-201; the architecture memo said 178-204); `Claims::zdr_floor` ignores service principals by design (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/auth.rs` [C] 105-123); the gateway search cache key has no org segment (`apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/search.rs` [C] 209-233, key built at 218-226; the memo said 211-229); `refuse_durable_job_under_zdr` covers only crawl and batch (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs` [M] 555-588); the viewport mismatch relaunch clears every page, receipt and dialog (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs` [C] `ensure_browser` 194-222); `stealth.rs` [C] has no caller (no `stealth::` reference exists in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates`), but the crate still declares it at `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs` [C] line 164 (`pub mod stealth;`), so deleting the file alone breaks the build; the resume owner check sits at `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs` [C] 1334-1341.

**Blocking W1 (merge)**

**X-1. Register `quarry-edge` as a read-only `browser-broker` principal (D1).**
- *Question.* How does production Quarry authenticate to the broker to validate grants? Without an answer no production run validates (the boot gate above bails when no validator is configured).
- *Options.* (a) Registry row `quarry-edge`, audience `browser-broker`, scope `browser:read` only, per-org token through the existing manifest machinery. (b) Forward the user's browser bearer to Quarry: fails for the AI path (execution-core calls Quarry with its own org-scoped service token; the user bearer lives 300 s against a 15 min grant). (c) Self-contained signed grants verified offline: loses revocation and changes the security model.
- *Recommendation.* (a). `browser:read` only validates; no service principal holds `browser:write` (a contract-spec assertion). Retention for this audience is `zdr` (the token carries no retained content). `apps/Control Plane/config/plane-service-principals.json` [C] holds `quarry-edge` with only the `data-plane` audience today.
- *Gates.* The merge of WS1.A2 (registry row, manifest row, Quarry service-token path, boot gates, L2 legs A to C); every browser item end to end. WS1.A1 does not wait: it carries no Control Plane edit. *Proceeds without.* WS1.A1 (broker Repository refactor, kinds, proto, model-gateway grant routes, L1 contract test, `browser-broker-ci.yml`, the `buf.yml` fix), WS1.A0 (production overlay boot), WS1.B, WS1.A2 up to its merge (written and tested against a dev-bypass Quarry), and leg A of the L2 run against a dev-bypass Quarry. Bundle the registry row with the other `quarry-edge` registry edits (R-13) so Control reviews once.
- *Decider.* Control Plane owner plus the user for the ledger entry.

**X-3. Merge governance (every design asks for it).**
- *Question.* Who arbitrates merge order, and who is the single editor of the hot files? `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs` [C] is edited by 9 workstreams, the broker files by 6, the execution-core browser files by D3, D6, D7, D8, D11 and sibling (b), `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs` by 5, and about 324 uncommitted entries sit under `main.rs`, `state.rs`, `config.rs`, `routes.rs`, `search_routes.rs`, `extract_routes.rs`, `zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`, `openapi.yaml` and session-core `0044/0045`.
- *Recommendation.* (1) Commit or branch the in-flight work as a baseline before W1 starts. (2) One arbiter for merge order. (3) Rules: broker files WS1 first; `agent_routes.rs` WS2.A, then the WS2.B split (two-working-day freeze), then WS2.C; `chromiumoxide.rs` one serial queue (R-31: WS3.C, WS3.D, WS3.F, WS3.K, WS3.G, WS8.E, WS12.B, WS13.C, WS12.F, WS17.E, WS17.G); the execution-core browser files have one editor (D11's proposal). (4) Migration, proto, event-number and registry allocations from section 2.3 are recorded in one ledger entry (`apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md` [C]). (5) The three copies of `quarry-token-claims.golden.json` are committed as a triple.
- *Gates.* WS2.B, WS1 broker work, every W2 slice in a hot file. *Proceeds without the baseline.* Slices that touch no uncommitted file: WS4.A, WS3.B, WS3.E, WS2.E, WS1.A1, and, with one hand-staged hunk each, WS2.A (text in `openapi.yaml` [M]) and WS4.K (the `PageCache` call sites in `routes.rs` [M]). Not on this list: WS5.A and WS5.B (they edit [M] files), WS3.A (it edits `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml` [M]) and WS6.A; these need position 0 (X-3 baseline). Day-0 slices are hunk-disjoint, not file-disjoint: several edit the same [M] files (`docker-compose.yml`, `openapi.yaml`, `routes.rs`, `main.rs`, `lib.rs`, `config.rs`, `domains/knowledge/quarry.rs`), so stage hunks by hand.
- *Decider.* The user or a delegate.

**Blocking W1 (production enablement or a default flip)**

**ADR-4 / OQ-4. ZDR semantics per feature.**
- *Question.* For monitors, schedules, durable crawls, URL caches, telemetry, profiles and AI formats, does ZDR mean refused, inline-only, hash-only or metadata-only?
- *Options (D4 section 3.3, a 24-row matrix).* Refused (today for durable crawl and batch; PageCache and SearchCache reads and writes skipped). Inline-only (scrape results returned in the response, nothing persisted). Hash-only: rejected by D4, since a hash of a known URL is a membership oracle and a hash-only cache serves nothing. Metadata-only (a tombstone with ids, outcome and counts, no URL). Correction to the audit text: schedules and monitors are not refused today, and a ZDR scrape logs URL and title at INFO.
- *Recommendation.* Adopt D4's table as the published default. Never loosen a refusal; refuse monitors, schedules, profile CRUD (except list and delete) and AI formats for ZDR orgs behind `QUARRY_EDGE__ZDR_REFUSE_DURABLE_RESOURCES` (observe one week, then enforce, customer notice first); scrape inline-only; captures refused until the inline path ships; log fields content-free; spans dropped at the sampler; tombstone only after counsel review. Generate the published matrix from the Rust `ROWS` table in WS4.G, not from hand-written JSON; axum has no route attributes, so completeness against the registered routes is enforced by a CI scan (`every_registered_route_has_a_matrix_row`). `QUARRY_EDGE__AI_FORMATS_ZDR` stays `refuse` until the owner records an ADR-4 amendment that allows ZDR extraction; the WS16 ZDR proof is a precondition of that amendment, not a switch.
- *Gates.* WS4.H (enforce), WS4.J (tombstone), the enforce steps of WS15.I, WS17.B and WS16.G, WS9.A (ZDR omnibox). *Proceeds without.* WS4.A to WS4.G and WS4.K (WS4.G documents and pins today's behaviour; WS4.K is a one-key tenant fix), every observe mode, log-field discipline, inline-only scrape in WS5.D. A plain "yes, as recommended" is enough.
- *Decider.* The user (product and legal); Control Plane for the org-posture signal (X-9).

**ADR-5 / OQ-5. Anti-bot posture.**
- *Question.* Is honest identity official, and which policy-gated escalation is allowed?
- *Options.* (a) Honest: a status is never an identity-change trigger; delete `stealth.rs`; proxy rotation on transport failure only; TLS-fingerprint fallback not a block reaction; rename the `stealth` preset with a one-release alias. (b) Keep shipped behaviour (rotation on bare 401/403/407/503, `prior_block_signals` forcing, Chrome-TLS fallback). (c) A policy-gated middle (tiers per org, F-t2-058).
- *Evidence.* Live rotation exists (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/egress_broker.rs` [C] 149, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/fallback_driver.rs` [C] 95-108, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/driver_plan.rs` [C] 40-46 per D3); WS3 centralises triggers in `escalation_allowed()` behind `QUARRY_BLOCK_ESCALATION=legacy|honest`.
- *Recommendation.* (a). The Chrome-TLS driver may stay registered for non-block reasons; profile restore does not replay the user agent (D16 Q5); the robots identity tokens stay `quarrybot`, `quarry` until F-t2-067.
- *Gates.* WS3.I default flip and preset rename; WS14.E robots posture and tokens; WS17.G UA replay. *Proceeds without.* WS3.E (delete stealth including the `pub mod stealth;` declaration at `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs` line 164 and any test or doc that names the module, `stealth_level`, `FingerprintRotator`, false doc claims), WS3.H (classification, one-recovery rule), WS3.I mechanism with the `legacy` default.
- *Decider.* The user (policy).

**X-2. ZDR browser grants memory-only on a single broker replica (D1).**
- *Question.* ZDR grants must not be persisted, so they die on broker restart and cannot span replicas. Acceptable?
- *Options.* (a) Memory only (`z_` id prefix routes to the memory repository), broker stays one replica (one container today). (b) Persist encrypted: violates "refused or ephemeral". (c) Refuse ZDR browser sessions whenever the broker has more than one replica.
- *Recommendation.* (a), written into the ledger, with an assertion that Postgres has no `zdr` column. model-gateway already refuses ZDR AI runs (`apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/browser_run.rs` [M] 307-315), so only ZDR human sessions rely on this.
- *Gates.* WS1.C production rollout; WS8 `human_browse` for ZDR users (a 4 h session on an in-memory broker dies on restart). *Proceeds without.* WS1.A0, WS1.A1, WS1.A2 (its merge still waits for X-1), WS1.B and the Postgres store for non-ZDR grants.
- *Decider.* The user (data governance); Model Plane owner for the replica constraint.

**X-14. Document parser isolation, skipped media, strict-validation date, scrape retention (D5 Q1 to Q4).**
- *Q1.* In-process parser with input and output caps, a 15 s deadline, 2 concurrent parses and a container memory limit (WS5.B), versus a child process with RLIMIT (WS5.C, 4 days). Evidence: `lopdf` 0.42.0 `decompress_zlib` has no output cap. Recommend ship WS5.B and keep `DOC_ROUTING=shadow/skip` as the default until WS5.C lands, then `on`. *Q2.* HTTP 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA` (non-retryable, counted in `pages_failed`) versus 200 with an empty body: recommend 415; WS5.A introduces the code under that default, and the answer should be in before WS5.G ships consumers. *Q3.* Lenient plus warnings for two releases, then strict. *Q4.* Scrape-record retention follows artifacts, armed by `QUARRY_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- *Gates.* Q1 blocks the production default `DOC_ROUTING=on`. Q3 and Q4 do not block. *Decider.* The user.

**X-16. Model Plane refusal catalogue keys (D4 S-9, D16 `browser_profile`).** Quarry adds four feature keys (plus `browser_profile`) to `apps/Model Plane/api/contracts/zdr-refusals.json` [U]; the Z-series that created `zdr_refusal.rs`, `zdr-refusals.ts` and the sync script is uncommitted. **OQ-10. Which claims need runtime confirmation first?**
- *Question.* AI-path 401/403 in production, viewport relaunch frequency, whether Chromium masks password values in the AX tree, whether same-host scrape sessions from different orgs share a session key.
- *Recommendation.* Reproduce first, as the first days of W1, each with a named owner and a recipe already in the designs: the WS1.A2 L2 legs A to C on the prod overlay (AI-path 401/403) and the WS1.A0 production-overlay boot (the Quarry prod-boot spike is a real fix, not only a check: the production overlay does not boot quarry-edge today, see WS1.A0); WS3.B plus the relaunch counter from WS3.C; D12 recipe D12-6 (AX password masking, which decides the WS12.B field-probe primary); WS13.A (same-host session sharing, fixed there regardless). Record results in each PR.
- *Proceeds without.* Everything: each fix is correct under either answer. *Decider.* Engineering; no ruling needed.

**OQ-3. Was the gateway search cache ever live outside a developer machine, and did a cross-org hit happen?**
- The cache key has no org segment and feeds org-scoped private-corpus providers. Stock compose does not set `GATEWAY_CACHE_REDIS_URL`; the e2e compose and a local `.env` do. Options: (a) fix only; (b) fix plus a forensic count of cross-org hits from Redis plus an incident record. Recommendation (b): WS4.A ships the fix first (3 days) and WS4.B runs the forensics and purge on every environment that ever set the variable. State the record as "reachable in production since <revision>" or "dev only" from deployment history, not from code.
- Gates only the incident record; WS9.A's omnibox search flag stays off until WS4.A merges. Everything proceeds. Decider: the user (classification), ops (deployment history).

**Blocking W2**

**ADR-3 / OQ-2 / OQ-12. Shared human-plus-agent sessions (D8, D9).**
- *Question.* How does a grant bind a session a human and a Model run both use; what navigation policy governs free human browsing; what replaces the 120 s run TTL; does a chat thread keep one long-lived Quarry run?
- *Options (D8 D8-1).* (1) Broker `human_browse` kind (open public web minus a broker deny-list, renewable by user presence) plus a run-bound `attach` child grant; a service principal attaches; a Quarry attach registry; per-tab control. (2) A delegation claim (RFC 8693 `acting_user_id`): authorises the service on every live session of that user and says nothing about hosts or TTL; kept only as optional hardening WS8.K. (2b) Forward the user's `aud=quarry` bearer: agent origin becomes client-asserted and a 300 s bearer cannot cover a run. (3) End and resume under a new grant: fails because `resume_run_id` requires owner equality (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs` [C] 1334-1341) and restores the URL only. D9 adds a fourth: an observe-only relay (WS9.J) before attach (WS9.K).
- *Recommendation.* Option 1, ratified as one package: kinds and invariants I1 to I8, open web minus a deny-list, 900 s idle interactive, 1800 s takeover idle, 4 h absolute, attach 900 s with 180 s idle release, keep-alive 300 s, implicit take-over on a non-passive human action. Agent idle stays 300 s (X-15). One long-lived user-owned run across chat turns, a Model Plane run attaches per run, agent-private browsing stays one run per Model Plane run. If ratified before W2 starts, skip D9's relay (WS9.J, saves 8 to 10 days); build it only as the fallback if ADR-3 is refused. Human seconds are metered, never capped.
- *Gates.* Merge of WS8.C, WS8.F, WS8.G; `human_browse` and `ATTACH` production enablement; WS9.H general availability, WS9.K, WS9.L; F-t2-012, 013 phase 2, 035, 054, 024, 038. *Proceeds without.* WS8.A, WS8.B, WS8.E, WS8.H; WS9.A to WS9.I (WS9.H behind its flag); F-t2-013 phase 1 (WS2.C).
- *Decider.* The user; Model Plane owner for grant kinds. Ratify in the first weeks of W1 so W2 can start.

**ADR-1 / OQ-1. Policy of record for web and browser capability.**
- *Question.* Does org web policy live in Control Plane org-core (signed claims) or Model Plane capability-core (grant fields), and how is it revoked mid-run when grants live 15 min?
- *Options (D7).* A: claims on user tokens only, grant fields for Model-driven runs (two resolution paths). B: capability-core owns, grant fields only: cannot reach `/v1/scrape`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/crawl` (no grant on those routes) and cannot store a proxy ceiling or robots mode. C: org-core owns; the claim rides on user tokens and on org-resolved service tokens (precedent only: `apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/interactive-retention-policy.ts` [C] 514-545, `resolveTenantServiceRetentionPosture`, resolves tenant-owned values at mint time but throws unless the principal's retention is `tenant`; the Quarry-facing rows `execution-core` and `model-gateway` carry `quarry: zdr` retention in `apps/Control Plane/config/plane-service-principals.json` [C], so WS7.I adds a second resolver for `zdr` and `persistent` service rows and must not change what those retention rows mean); the grant carries a snapshot.
- *Recommendation.* C. Revocation: claim staleness about 345 s by default (300 s audience TTL plus 45 s resolver cache), 105 s with `WEB_POLICY_TOKEN_TTL_CAP_SECONDS=60`, which is not applied by default. Riding sub-decisions: fail mode of the entitlement read is fail-to-floor (last good for 15 min, then the static floor); the budget claim minter is model-gateway (if capability-core wins later only the minter moves); fall back to A if Control declines the registry field `webPolicyByAudience`. The grant snapshot never overrides a tighter claim.
- *Gates.* WS7.A, WS7.H to WS7.K, WS7.M; WS6.D plan-aware clamps and fail mode; WS14.H; the claim channel of F-t2-032, 025, 046, 048. *Proceeds without.* WS7.B to WS7.G (owner-neutral `Option<PolicyLayer>`), WS6 static mode, WS11 interim env allowlist.
- *Decider.* The user, with Control Plane (registry field, token lifetime) and Model Plane (grant fields) sign-off.

**X-13. Human-browsing evidence, shared jar and take-over (D8-5, D8-6, D8-7).** D8-5: human steps on non-ZDR runs persist metadata-only receipts (typed text `[redacted]`, query and fragment dropped, no observation, checkpoint URL stripped); history is not stored in Verevon; a hard prerequisite to enabling `human_browse`, and a strict tightening WS8.B can ship now. D8-6: attach shares the user's logged-in jar (default) or opens an isolated context; recommend the shared jar with per-tab egress equal to the attach list, with F-t2-032 later replacing implicit consent. D8-7: implicit take-over (Codex lets the user interact at any time): recommend yes, one constant switches to an explicit button. Gates: D8-5 `human_browse` enablement, D8-6 `ATTACH` GA, D8-7 the WS8.F default. Decider: the user.

**X-12. Budget numbers and gate order (D6 Q1, Q6).** Shipped defaults and ceilings: agent 60 steps, 900 s, 1.00 USD; ceilings 300 steps, 3600 s, 20 USD; crawl 1000 pages depth 5, ceilings 5000 and 10; 3 concurrent jobs, backlog 200; estimator 0.00003 USD per browser second until the billing-core price table replaces it. Recommend accepting them as placeholders ratified before `on`, and the canonical gate order of R-7 (budget before sensitive approval, so a refusal never burns a single-use approval). Gates WS6.B and WS6.D leaving shadow or static. Decider: the user.

**X-7 / OQ-14. The Quarry-to-Model-Plane structured-extraction lane (DR-15.1) and the owner of DEF-QB-T17-PART2 (D15).**
- *Question.* Who owns the org-bound metered Model Plane path for services, and what is the grant shape?
- *Options.* G1: two registry audiences (`model-gateway: models:invoke`, `inference-core: inference:invoke, models:invoke`), retention `tenant`, two new manifest rows, `model-invoke`, stream and audio stay dark. G2: one audience plus a gateway-held inference principal (ambient authority, rejected). G3: no grant (interim Model-proposed route only). G4: status quo (refused in production). Owners: O1 Model Plane gateway owner; O2 Control registry owner; O3 Ingestion (violates ownership); O4 split with O1 accountable.
- *Recommendation.* G1 with O4 and O1 accountable (ownership matrix rows 62 and 88), written as the draft ledger entry in D15; ship the dark slices meanwhile. OQ-14 answer: the Model Plane gateway owner.
- *Gates.* WS16.C, WS16.G and any production use of AI formats; F-t2-030 phase 2, 037, 050, 065. *Proceeds without.* WS16.A, WS16.B, WS16.D to WS16.F, WS16.H, WS16.I (the interim route). *Decider.* The user names the owner; Control co-signs.

**X-9. Job-lifecycle decisions that are not audit topics (D14b).** (D9) Results source: events as a page index (`page_extracted` rows, excerpt only, capped) as phase 1; the alternative is to wait for F-t2-052 result sets. (D14) Trigger and backfill transport: a Temporal SDK client in quarry-control (second client, silent-success `NoopClient` hazard), pull-model `schedule_requests` rows claimed by the orchestrator every 2 s with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (recommended), or an orchestrator HTTP endpoint; backfill refused for crawl and batch, 24-window cap. (D15) ZDR for schedules: refuse at creation with D4's code and re-check posture at fire time through an edge preflight that reads org-core `retention-posture`; that needs a `quarry-edge` principal with `org:retention:read:any`, currently held only by auth-core (a documented one-holder invariant and two contract tests); fail closed as `skipped_posture_unknown`. (D17) Failure notices: Application Plane registers `quarry-control` as a notification-core caller (types `quarry.schedule_run_failed` and `quarry.schedule_run_skipped`, HMAC v2 delegation, content-free payload). Gates WS15.H, WS15.I enforcement and notices, WS15.J go-live (also needs WS14 scope and WS6.A deployed and one week of observe), WS15.K (D9). Proceeds without WS15.A to WS15.G (WS15.C org scoping closes a cross-tenant exposure; WS15.E ships flag-off). Decider: the user, Control and Application Plane owners.

**X-10. Crawl and robots decisions (D14a).** Robots when unreachable (5xx or timeout): disallow (RFC 9309, recommended; flaky robots endpoints will stop crawls, so soak first) versus allow (Firecrawl). Ignore-robots override: an audited Control Plane entitlement through D7's `robots.max_mode` ceiling, the audit event written by quarry-control before the job is acknowledged (fail closed); grantor platform operators only (default) versus org admins (OQ-11). Crawl under ZDR: keep the refusal (the alternative is an XL redesign across five retention surfaces). Default scope: same host with `www.` equivalence, whole host, page cap 1000; `max_pages: 0` is treated as absent and takes the WS6.A default at W1 (edge and orchestrator), and WS14.G turns it into a 400 `invalid_option` only when `QUARRY_EDGE__CRAWL_REQUEST_VALIDATION=strict` (the gateway keeps its existing 400; test `crawl_request_zero_pages_is_default_in_lenient_and_400_in_strict`); existing crawls lose off-site pages, so soak in `observe` first. Gates WS14.H and WS14.I; WS14.A to WS14.G proceed. Decider: the user.

**ADR-8 (parts 1 and 2), X-4, X-5, X-6. Run trace envelope and sharing (D10).**
- *Part 1.* Extend `model_plane.v1.Event` (fields 14-18 inside the range `apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/events.proto` [C] reserves as `reserved 14 to 20`; event types 150-159) versus a second envelope. Recommend extend; record the allocation in the ledger. Gates production use of WS10.B.
- *Part 2 (D10 D13).* A: coarse debounced Convex projection with an owner-checked read-through. B: full trace in Convex (rejected: write amplification, a second ACL). C: copy events into a Space (rejected: widens the ACL, violates matrix rule 10). D: no projection. Recommend A with owner-only reads in v1 until the resource-taxonomy ADR (F-t2-072). Gates WS10.G only.
- *X-4.* The cross-plane NATS credential: (a) a publish-only principal `quarry-trace-producer` on Model-nats, subject `mp.v1.trace.run.*`, no JetStream API rights; (b) a bridge service (an unowned service that keeps raw payloads on the Ingestion bus); (c) fold into the Ingestion bus with a filter. Recommend (a) after security review; gates WS10.E enablement outside dev. *X-5.* ZDR and the replay ring: an in-memory live-run ring (what the 256-slot broadcast channel already holds, freed at `close_run`) versus no replay; recommend allow, a one-line flip. *X-6.* Owner of the session-core consumer and `EventLog` server (about 10 engineer-days): sibling (b) after `0044/0045` are committed (recommended), this plan, or defer WS10.F and ship WS10.A to WS10.E (16.5 days of value without persistence). Proceeds without ADR-8: WS10.A, WS10.C, WS10.D, WS10.H. Decider: the user; Application Plane owner for WS10.G; security reviewer for X-4.

**X-8. Key management ownership (D16-3, D16-4, D16-7; proposed audit item 11).** Options: (a) org-core behind an interface (`internal/orgkeys`; hierarchy master, per-org KEK, per-profile DEK; cascade delete gives crypto-shred); (b) auth-core (wrong blast radius); (c) a new `key-core` service (XL). Master key from env first (loss destroys every profile; escrow runbook, boot canary, restore drill), KMS later. Owner model: `owner_user_id` set on insert, `user_private` owner-only, `org_shared` members read, a non-owner gets 404. Recommend (a), the env master as an explicit logged interim, observe-first owner enforcement, legacy `user_private` rows hidden not deleted. Gates WS17.D `REQUIRED=1`, WS17.F enforce, WS17.H, WS17.I; proceeds without WS17.A to WS17.G with the `env` provider. Decider: the user (ownership docs change) and Control Plane owner.

**X-11. Planner production enablement (D11 OD13, quota keys).** The route (stay on Balance or pin a subscription route with a guard), the quota-key convention for the interim org flag, and who edits the execution-core browser files. "OD13" is one open-decision bundle of `CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01`: D1 cites its "start host plus at most 8" clause, D8 its "user's aud=quarry bearer" clause, D11 its "pin Terra" clause; sibling (b) must answer them together. Recommend keeping Balance until Tier C numbers exist; org-core quota rows `browser_agent_llm_planner` (1 on, 2 off) and `browser_agent_max_tokens_per_run` as an interim carrier removed when ADR-1's carrier lands; one editor; run length about 4 minutes until bearer refresh exists. Gates WS11.F stage 3 (`default_on`) and production use of WS11.C. Proceeds without WS11.A, WS11.B, WS11.D, WS11.E, WS11.G, WS11.H and WS11.C for dev. Decider: the user and sibling (b); Control owner for quota keys.

**X-19. Redaction product decisions (D12 Q1 to Q5).** Receipt typed-text policy `sensitive` (keeps benign typed text, default) versus `all` (compiled procedures become replay-useless); accept the raw URL in the Live view but strip it everywhere durable; legacy rows masked on read only (default) versus a destructive rewrite (conflicts with append-only evidence); the owner's frame stream is unmasked (a limit of WS12.F), Space members get receipts only (recommended) or a later masked stream; cross-origin iframe fields in screenshots default to `allow` with counts, `mask` is a strict mode. Gates WS12.D merge. Decider: the user (product owner).

**X-20. Scrape actions and captures (D13).** Who may send `actions`: user principals when the flag is `user`, no service principal until granted `scrape:interact` (ADR-6). Fidelity under host-pinned egress: report what was denied (default) versus a third-party subresource allow-list (via D7 `BrowserEgressPolicy`). Inline-only ZDR capture with a size cap. Credential entry in `write` refused heuristically until ADR-2. Local driver only (Browserbase fails closed for every scrape today; a 501 elsewhere). One heavy action request per process (`QUARRY_SCRAPE_HEAVY_PERMITS=1`) and a 125 s router deadline; whether front proxies allow 125 s is [UNVERIFIED], otherwise cap total wait near 20 s. WS13.F ships dark either way. A Model-authored action list relayed by the gateway under the user's bearer is indistinguishable from a human list by principal kind alone, so WS13.F accepts a tighten-only `initiated_by` hint on `/v1/scrape` (an `actions` request labelled `agent` is 403 `scrape_interact_scope_required`; the gateway sets the label on every model-originated request; test `agent_labelled_user_token_cannot_send_actions`), and `QUARRY_EDGE__SCRAPE_ACTIONS=user` is dev-only until that test exists. Decider: the user.
*Ruling of 2026-10-28 (ADR-6 ratified, decision 3.8 of `.plan-work/quarry-w1w2/DECISIONS-ROUND-2026-10-27.md`). These gates replace the two weaker ones above ("`on` only after ADR-6" and "`user` in dev until the agent-label test exists"), which a yes to ADR-6 and a dev-bypass unit test would otherwise have met on paper:* (1) `on` (service principals with `scrape:interact`) needs a verified Model caller (D2-012, closed by decision: Quarry decides who the agent is from the verified token) **and** an approval gate; ratifying ADR-6 does not open it. (2) `user` outside the dev and evidence stack needs the live proof (`scrape_actions_live` and `make test-scrape-capture` passing on the evidence stack), a billing meter and a per-org entitlement; that is option C, a separate decision. (3) `user` on the dev and evidence stack only, against the fixture site or hosts we own, with the default "report denied" egress, and only after SC1 to SC7. (4) Production stays `off` (both compose files carry `${QUARRY_EDGE_SCRAPE_ACTIONS:-off}`, commit `675903067`). (5) Opening to the Model (option D) is a Model Plane session decision.

**X-18. Shared-browser frontend product choices (D9 D-3, D-4, D-11, Q1 to Q6).** In a ZDR verdict of "deny" the omnibox keeps no local history, no suggestions and no search-home recording (matches D4); a ZDR thread's dock is human-only. Org-scoped autocomplete: local history plus related queries only. Chat-per-tab default: keep the chat. Land WS9.A and WS9.H behind flags, off in production until WS8 removes the 12-step, first-host and 120 s limits. Classify `browser.observe`, `browser.act` and `browser.console` output as external browser content now (a security fix; sibling (b) edits execution-core). Decider: the user; production flags only.

**OQ-11. Robots exemption for manual browsing and the override grantor.** Recommend: human navigation in the browser pane is exempt from robots.txt (robots governs crawlers); agent-proposed navigation is not exempt (`RobotsGate::check` is the API `validate_navigation` can call, owned by sibling (b)); `domains.deny` applies to humans and agents alike; the override is platform-operator-only by default. Gates WS14.H. Decider: the user.

**OQ-13. Should `GET /v1/profiles/:id` ever return raw cookie values?** Options (D16-8): keep, owner-only audited, never (summary only), owner plus step-up approval. Recommend never: redacted structure only (name, domain, path, flags, `value_len`, `value: null`), no raw read route, service principals refused on all `/v1/profiles*`; a "show my cookies" feature is a separate audited DSAR export. Confirm no operator workflow needs raw values. Gates WS17.B. Decider: the user.

**Later (do not block W1 or W2 building)**

- **ADR-2 / OQ-7, secret custody.** Extend integration-corev2 (an at-rest token vault with a shared internal API key, not a user-secret store) versus a Control Plane secret service. Recommend OTP first through the existing sensitive-approval path, defer password references; every OTP read approved and shown with origin and connection. Gates F-t2-024 E3 and E5 (W3). WS12 proceeds in full: redaction precedes any `fill_secret`.
- **ADR-6 / OQ-9, script execution model.** Keep one governed action per call, or allow declarative capped action lists and a sandboxed runtime whose bindings are separate Quarry steps. D2 chose outright rejection of `Evaluate` (the broker has no script-hash scope and `/step` discards the return value, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/observation.rs` [C] 542-544); D13 ships a closed, declarative, capped action list for user principals with no `evaluate` in its wire enum. Recommend declarative lists and profiles; code mode (F-t2-063) only as a slice of the Model Plane's code-mode; a future read-only evaluator is a new action variant, never a relaxed `Evaluate`. Record D2's choice as the ledger default now. Gates WS13.F opening to the Model, F-t2-063, F-t2-065. **Ratified by the owner on 2026-10-28:** closed, declarative, capped action lists, no `Evaluate`; a future read-only evaluator is a new action type, never a relaxed `Evaluate`. The X-20 gates were rewritten in the same ruling (see X-20).
- **ADR-7 / OQ-6, external MCP exposure.** REST only, or an audience-bound MCP front outside Quarry with customer API keys. Recommend the OpenAPI-from-types slice now (WS5.H); the rest waits for an owner decision (it reverses `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md` [C] line 30). Gates F-t2-064, F-t2-042.
- **ADR-9, automation owner.** Quarry schedules stay acquisition-only; unattended browser runs are draft-only through W2 and cannot borrow a human's bearer; agent routines wait for pause and resume (sibling F-t3-018). Gates F-t2-031 phase 2, F-t2-061.
- **ADR-10 / OQ-8, browser execution substrate.** One Chromium with caps (K=1), a K-process pool (crash containment, no tenant isolation claim), per-session container or microVM (F-t2-060), remote providers (F-t2-059), the user's own Chrome (F-t2-077, parked). The pinned egress proxy type is loopback-only (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs` [C] 331-360), so remote or containerised Chromium needs a sidecar proxy or a reviewed relaxation. Recommend per-page emulation and sandbox default now (WS3.A, WS3.C), K=1 with slot bookkeeping (WS3.F), a pool (WS3.G) only after a measured memory budget; no per-session VM; a sidecar proxy is not accepted until a reviewed relaxation exists.
- **X-17, Prometheus rules and an Alertmanager.** Infrastructure rules in the Control Plane Prometheus `rule_files` and user-facing alerts through App Plane notifications, or per-plane Alertmanagers. Recommend the first (none exists today). Gates WS6 L3 alerts.
- **OQ-15, stale docs.** Recommend yes: each PR corrects the stale statement it disproves and adds a line to `apps/STALE_DOC_DELETION_REGISTER.md` [C] (WS1.A1 and WS1.A2 the grant-issuance COMPLETE claims, WS5 the "formats done" claim, WS6 "budgets enforced", WS3 the `/ready` browser block and stealth claims, WS8 the `BROWSER_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md` co-browsing, WS12 `SECRET_REDACTION.md`). "Docs corrected" is part of each slice's definition of done.

## 3. Workstreams

How to read this section. Each workstream (WS) is one design (D1 to D17) cut into slices; a slice is one PR-sized change with its own tests and deployment evidence. Slice ids are `WS<n>.<letter>`: the letter is the architecture memo's slice id (arch-B 1), and the design's own slice name is given in brackets, for example `WS3.C [D3 S2]`. Where the reconciliation list in arch-A section 2 (R-n) or a decision record (X-n, ADR-n, OQ-n) overrides a design, the override is used and named in one clause. Wave 1 workstreams are WS1 to WS5; later workstreams are cut the same way by the other section 3 parts.

Path tags come from `tools/provenance.sh` run on 2026-10-15 against the live tree (afb83928 plus about 324 uncommitted entries): `[C]` committed and unchanged, `[M]` committed but modified in the live tree (in-flight hunks exist: rebase, never merge blind), `[U]` untracked (exists only as uncommitted work), `[NEW]` created by this plan. Paths in section 3 are written in full, relative to the repo root. Line numbers are live-tree numbers read by the design agents and re-checked where stated; they drift once earlier slices land, so re-read before editing. Test commands that build Quarry Rust run inside the `rust:1` container with the `quarry-cargo`, `quarry-go`, `quarry-target` volumes and `bash -c` (a full `-p quarry-core -p quarry-runtime -p quarry-edge` run exceeds 10 minutes), because the Windows host cannot build the crates natively. Every "Deployment evidence" item means rebuilt local images, a running stack and a verified flow with a stated observable assertion; the evidence stack recipes are in arch-B 7.3 (the edge listens on `127.0.0.1:8082` in the Ingestion compose and `127.0.0.1:38080` in the standalone compose, not the `:8080` the Quarry smoke scripts default to). Baseline for every slice: the PRE-1 commit of the in-flight work (arch-B 2.1) is done first, and the regression guards in arch-A section 7 stay green.

### 3.1 Wave 1: unblock and make safe

Wave 1 closes the two data-exposure holes (gateway cache, raw script), makes the production browser path possible at all (grants), puts run control and driver safety inside Quarry, and fixes the scrape contract. It is 132.25 engineer-days core plus 16 gated and 6 optional (arch-B 5.2 counted 113.75, 12 and 10; the review re-estimated WS1.A to 16 d and added the 1.5 d boot gate WS1.A0, re-estimated WS2.C to 10 d, WS3.F to 10 d and WS6.A to 3.5 d, added WS4.K at 0.5 d, and moved WS5.C, 4 d, from optional to gated; WS6.A, the crawl bounds, is counted in the core figure). W1 exit gate: WS1.A0, WS1.A1, WS1.A2, WS1.B and WS1.C with `BROWSER_GRANT_ENFORCEMENT=strict` on the production-overlay stack (the production overlay itself plus the contract overlay, which may only add env and volumes; see SC1 and WS1.A0); WS2.A to WS2.E; WS3.A to WS3.F, WS3.H, WS3.J; WS4.A to WS4.G and WS4.K with the purge recorded; WS5.A to WS5.H (WS5.C is the X-14 Q1 gate for the production default of `DOC_ROUTING=on`); WS6.A (crawl bounds); PRE-1 and PRE-2 committed.

#### WS1. Production BrowserBroker grants and delegated browser bearer  (Wave 1; owner: Model Plane browser-broker + model-gateway, with Frontend gateway, Ingestion quarry-edge and Control Plane registry hunks; effort: L, about 33.5 engineer-days (A0 1.5, A1 10, A2 6, B 10, C 6; WS1.A re-estimated from 10 to 16 d and split in two, K1-11, K1-16); lane: L1 GRANTS-BROKER)

**Resolves:** F-t2-001 (all three phases: A, B, C). **Depends on:** none to start (WS1.A0 and WS1.A1 depend on nothing); only WS1.A2 waits for the Control Plane sign-off (X-1), and its Quarry stream needs WS2.B merged (it edits `agent_routes.rs`) and WS1.A0 merged (the production overlay must boot first); the SC1 L2 run on the production overlay also needs WS3.A (sandbox default and writable Chromium root, proven by `ps` and a `navigate` 200 on the same stack). **Gated by:** X-1 (register `quarry-edge` as a read-only `browser-broker` principal, `browser:read` only; blocks the merge of WS1.A2, the Quarry credential and every end-to-end browser item, but not WS1.A1); X-2 (ZDR browser sessions use memory-only grants on one broker replica; blocks WS1.C production rollout only); X-3 (merge governance and the allocation ledger); X-15 (L2 gate runner is a manual pre-merge evidence run with L1 in CI; broker database is the shared `session_core` database now); OQ-10 (L2 legs A to C are the runtime spike for the AI-path 401/403 and the Quarry prod-boot claims). Soft: ADR-1 (the `PolicyResolver` hook ships with a static default), ADR-3 (no `human_browse` kind in WS1).

**State of the code (verified 2026-10-14, live tree):**

*Risks.* Shared `session_core` database and the `postgres` superuser (precedent, not ideal): `browser_` prefix, nothing else reads the table, dedicated database and role is a hardening follow-up. DDL re-applied each start: idempotent DDL only, later migrations use `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; the gap between `0001` and WS7's reserved `0002` is acceptable: gaps are tolerated (the entrypoint copied from `sandbox-manager` globs `/app/migrations/*.up.sql` and re-applies every file on each start, so each statement must stay idempotent). Run grants outlive a stopped AI run (no revoke-on-stop; bounded by TTL, deferred to F-t2-036 with a run-to-grant map).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** Model Plane owns all grant authority (only the broker creates a record; model-gateway binds org and user from verified claims; the Verevon gateway only forwards the user's own bearer and a session grant id and can never mint, derive or widen; Quarry only validates, and the legacy Quarry `acquire` is deleted so this is structural); no direct database crossing (`browser_grants` is read only by the broker).
ZDR is OR-ed from request and verified token and can never be lowered; ZDR grants are memory-only with `z_` ids and no column; run grants inherit the parent's ZDR and a posture change fails closed; no domain lists in broker, model-gateway or gateway logs or metrics; Quarry refuses a non-ZDR run under a ZDR grant; the residual (ZDR grants lost on broker restart, single replica) is X-2.
The AI never chooses domains (the run grant is derived server-side and the optional request list can only narrow); every action still passes execution-core's allow-list, the HITL risk gates (`CrossDomainNavigation` does not read the grant) and Quarry's per-step `ValidateGrant` and domain check.

**Cross-session:** B1 grant issuance, derivation, renewal: this plan owns the broker `Repository`, kinds, model-gateway routes and `DeriveRunGrant`; sibling (b) owns the execution-core consumer and must not build a second grant API (F-t3-008's grant half is WS1; only Do-loop dispatch and the browser subagent step stay with (b)); any new model-gateway grant route updates the L1 single-minting-path test.
B2 delegated bearer: the user's `aud=browser-broker` bearer is used for the mint, a service principal for Quarry calls; sibling (b) forwards on chat routes (this plan adds the parameter and wrappers in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/chat/shared.rs`, (b) wires chat call sites and the `purpose` list, for example `chat_turn`, a one-line addition in `Derive`).
S1 (a) Space: no `space_id`, `team_id` or shared flag in any grant API; a Space-hosted agent derives from the acting user's session grant; `space_ref` is attribution at run start only.
Shared files with one editor: `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs` and `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/chat/shared.rs` (WS8, sibling (b)); the registry PR (R-13) and `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` (append-only rows, R-14).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** Quarry consumes Auth Core's `principal_type` and `service_id` claims (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/auth.rs` 99-103, 148-174) and defines no identity; the caps are infrastructure safety limits in the plane that owns the browser lifecycle, set by env, not entitlements (plan-aware values arrive with F-t2-022/025); receipts and checkpoints stay in Quarry's own Postgres, no cross-plane database.
Enforcement is independent of persistence, so a ZDR run is gated identically; epoch and mode live in memory, receipts, timeline events, checkpoint epoch and the Skipped receipt are skipped under `entry.zdr.is_active()`; the denial logs the action name only, never the script; `agent.expired` carries no URL and goes through `emit_for_zdr`; `RegistryStats` labels are class and reason only.
Every WS2 slice is Quarry rejecting (the admission pipeline decides, not the planner); the caller-asserted `initiated_by` can only make a request stricter; the one-shot sensitive approval path is untouched and still needs a broker grant.

*Files.* `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/deadlines.rs` [NEW] (`Op` enum: `Launch, TabAttach, Navigate, Content, AxSnapshot, Screenshot, Pdf, Evaluate, Input, NativeAction, WaitForPoll, WaitFor, PageClose, ContextClose, HealthProbe, ProfileCapture, DownloadBegin, DownloadComplete, ...`; `const fn deadline(op)`; `cdp_err(op, CdpError)`; `with_deadline(op, effectful, fut)`; `read_with_retry(op, f)`; `is_context_destroyed`); `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs` [C] `mod deadlines;` near 153-164; `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs` [C]: builder 226-262 `.request_timeout(15 s).launch_timeout(20 s)` and `Browser::launch` (256) in `with_deadline(Op::Launch, ..)` (25 s outer); `open_tab_page` attach sequence in `with_deadline(Op::TabAttach, ..)` with an `AttachGuard` closing the page and disposing a context this call created, and the `browser` mutex no longer held across the function (379); wrap `goto` 2001, `content` 2019 and `native_page_projection` 2681-2730 (`read_with_retry`), `screenshot` 2398, `pdf` 2440, `evaluate` 3009, input dispatches (`click_point` 2883-2894, `mouse_wheel` 2977, `press` 2996, `type_text` 2913), `execute_native_target_action` 1267/1345 (`Op::NativeAction`, effectful), `wait_for` 2810 (poll 2 s, loop `min(timeout_ms, 30 s)`), `release` and `close_tab` closes (1952, 1963, 2568-2578, best effort); constants `DOWNLOAD_BEGIN_TIMEOUT`/`DOWNLOAD_COMPLETE_TIMEOUT` (76-77) and the literal 5 s at 685 move into the table unchanged; debug log `browser_op_duration_ms op=<name> ms=<n>` per wrapped call.

*Contracts, flag.* No new `ErrorCode` (R-10); `ErrorCode::Timeout` (504) gains `details {op, deadline_ms, effect: none|unknown}`; effectful ops set `retryable = false`; details never copy a URL, selector or page text (`cdp_err` must not copy the `url`/`selector` details that existing `DriverFailed` sites carry). Starting table: launch 20 s (outer 25 s), tab attach 15 s, navigate 30 s, content 15 s, AX snapshot 10 s, screenshot 10 s, pdf 30 s, evaluate 15 s, input 5 s, native action 10 s, page and context close 5 s each, probe 3 s, profile capture 5 s, download begin 10 s and complete 30 s. Retry once after 100 ms only for destroyed-context signatures (`Cannot find context with specified id`, `Execution context was destroyed`, `Inspected target navigated or closed`) and only for the three read helpers; never retry navigate, click, type, select, press, upload, download, respond_dialog or ref/coordinate actions. `QUARRY_BROWSER_DEADLINE_SCALE` (float in (0,2], default 1.0) multiplies the table; step-level 50 s budget around `ObservationRunner::execute` is recommended to WS2/runtime so the typed `Timeout` beats the 60 s router `TimeoutLayer`.

*Tests.* Unit `every_op_has_a_positive_deadline_below_the_router_cap`, `timeout_error_names_the_op_and_is_not_retryable_for_effectful_ops`, `read_ops_timeout_is_retryable`, `context_destroyed_matcher_accepts_known_signatures_only`, `read_with_retry_retries_once_then_surfaces`, `with_deadline_uses_tokio_paused_time` (`start_paused = true`); live `navigation_during_content_read_is_retried_once`, `attach_timeout_cleans_up_partial_context`. Commands `cargo test -p quarry-browser --features chromiumoxide`; `cargo check -p quarry-edge`. DoD: no `page.execute/evaluate/...` call lacks a `with_deadline` wrapper or an explicit comment that the library `request_timeout` is the bound; `grep -n "DriverFailed.*timed out"` finds nothing that should be a `Timeout`; the table is the only place durations are written.

*Deployment evidence.* Rebuilt edge with `QUARRY_BROWSER_DEADLINE_SCALE=0.02`: a `navigate` to a slow public URL returns HTTP 504 `error.code = "TIMEOUT"` with `error.details.op = "navigate"` within the scaled deadline, the next `/step` is accepted immediately (run lock free), `docker logs quarry-edge | grep browser_op_duration_ms` shows durations (collect a week before tightening any value). Risks: deadlines too tight (scale env, calibration log), effect unknown on an effectful timeout (`effect:"unknown"` plus `retryable:false`), changed attach lock scope can reorder concurrent attaches (WS3.C live test stays green); land as one mechanical PR right after WS3.C.

[CLAIM-FALSE] "only `click_point` dispatches trusted mouse events": selector `click` (2828-2839) and `press` (2989-3001) already use trusted chromiumoxide `Element::click`/`press_key`; and [CLAIM-FALSE] "upload and download reuse the same native click helper": only download does.

DoD: with the flag on, a click on a ref covered by an overlay fails `TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED` with `details.reason = "target_covered"` and a tag, succeeds after dismissal, `event.isTrusted` is true, governed downloads and uploads unchanged, the failure rate per reason is logged. Evidence: rebuilt edge with `QUARRY_BROWSER_TRUSTED_INPUT=on`, the start response shows `driver_capabilities.trusted_input = true`; on a public page with a modal over a link an agent run clicks the link's ref and gets 409 `target_covered`, clicking the modal's close ref returns 200 and the link click then returns 200 with a changed `url`; repeat with the flag off [UNVERIFIED] stable public test page (else fixtures back the claim). Risks: a modal dialog can stall the input acknowledgement (handled as success when the dialog collector holds a pending dialog); cross-process iframes are not hit-tested (explicit synthetic fallback); trusted input can trigger default browser behaviours (default-off flag and soak); the covered tag is a tag name only. Sibling (b) owns the planner sentence telling the Model to dismiss the overlay or scroll and re-observe.

**Slice WS3.L (unscheduled)**: cross-process iframe hit-testing, `press` with modifiers, drag, `select_text`, paste, per-key typing, file-chooser interception; each needs its own design and a Model Plane contract change first (`browser.act` is a closed list at `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs` [M] 3479-3508; `AgentAction::Press` carries only a key string, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/contracts.rs` 699). Owner for the contract: sibling (b).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** every slice is inside the Ingestion Plane except WS3.J's Model Plane, gateway and SPA halves, which consume additive Quarry fields through their own contracts; no database and no migration (next free quarry-runtime number `0010` is WS2's); the admission cap is a host-resource guard, not a quota (plan caps stay with Control and WS6).
No new persistence: block episodes and host counters are in memory (ZDR runs count by reason only, never the host); health and slot data are content-free; new error details carry operation, deadline, reason and tag name only; the reaper never persists a profile; retirement and crash cleanup remove each launch's directories; the per-session live-frame cache (250 ms TTL) is cleared on `release` and reaping so frames cannot outlive a ZDR session; the probe context uses the pinned proxy with a deny-all policy; `--disable-quic`, the per-context proxy and `<-loopback>` bypass override stay for every launch and `PinnedEgressProxyEndpoint::parse` stays loopback-only.
Quarry enforces the single recovery by counting and rejecting (it never reloads on its own); WS3.K rejects covered, disabled or unstable targets with typed reasons instead of clicking blindly; WS3.F busy, WS3.D timeouts and WS3.H `ChallengeDetected` are Quarry rejections; the health prober never touches a session or navigates.

**Cross-session:** B3 `browser.*` tool schema and closed action list: sibling (b) implements the closed `browser.act` schema (WS3.L and R-12), WS3 specifies; `browser.observe/act/console` output classified as external browser content (WS9 3c) changes both copies of `classify` together. B6 typed-error mapping for `TIMEOUT` (effect), `TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED` reasons, `RATE_LIMITED` driver reasons and `CHALLENGE_DETECTED`: sibling (b) via WS11 `parse_typed_error` (planner text for `target_covered` is theirs). Edits to `BrowserChrome.tsx`, `browser-client.ts`, `action-registry.ts` for the blocked state: single editor to be named (WS9 owns `src/features/browser/*`; sibling (a) S7 reuses the controller, no fork). Sibling (a): Space agent browsers share the one `agent_driver`, so `QUARRY_BROWSER_MAX_SESSIONS` is sized for UI plus Model plus Space sessions together.
