*Contracts, flag.* No HTTP change. The Redis key shape changes, so every existing `quarry:page:{fingerprint}` entry becomes unreachable and ages out by TTL (a one-time cold cache). No flag: the fix must not be switchable, and a rollback is a revert that re-opens the hole.

*Tests.* `page_cache_is_not_readable_across_orgs` in `tests/cache_policy.rs` (needs Redis: org A scrapes and writes; org B sends org A's fingerprint as `prev_fingerprint` and gets a miss that reaches the origin once; org A with its own fingerprint still gets the hit) and the unit test `page_cache_key_includes_the_org` in `cache.rs` (two orgs, one fingerprint, two keys; an empty org is not a key). Commands `cd "apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2" && cargo test -p quarry-edge --test cache_policy` (Redis required) and `cargo test -p quarry-edge cache::`.

*Definition of done.* Org B with org A's fingerprint gets a miss; both tests green; the SC5 assertion "org B with org A's fingerprint gets a miss" passes.

*Deployment evidence.* Rebuilt edge with Redis: as org A `POST /v1/scrape` for a public URL and note `data.fingerprint`; as org B `POST /v1/scrape` for a different public URL with `prev_fingerprint` set to that value: the response is org B's own fresh scrape (it does not carry org A's `final_url` or title), `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'quarry:page:<orgA>:*'` returns the one key and nothing sits under org B for that fingerprint; the same request as org A for its own URL returns the cached output.

*Risks.* One cold-cache period after deploy; ZDR is unaffected (the cache is skipped under ZDR); the other Quarry cache namespaces (`quarry:search:{org}:...`) are already org-keyed; the URL-keyed cache stays with F-t2-048.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** Control Plane identity, orgs and entitlements are only read (org ZDR posture through the existing org-core call in `zdr.rs`; the org-erasure event `gdpr_nats.rs`), nothing stored; the tombstone lives in quarry-control's own Postgres and the Control retention input would be an API read; no Data Plane contact (ingest stays refused under ZDR); the catalogue is Model Plane's and Quarry vendors a sha-pinned golden, adding keys only by a PR into that contract.
Every persistence boundary is stated: gateway caches (fixed, fail closed), Quarry caches (correct, protected), logs (WS4.D to WS4.F), usage meter (scrape site stripped here, F-t2-046 the rest), schedules, monitors and profile CRUD (WS4.H, ADR-4), run history and artifacts (already withheld), tombstone (the only deliberate retention, metadata-only by allowlist).
Every matrix refusal is enforced inside Quarry's own handlers whatever the Model proposed; model-gateway refusals stay the first line, Quarry the last; no new Model-facing capability is added.

*Contracts.* HTTP 415 with the standard envelope, `error.code "UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA"`, `error.details {"reason":"unsupported_media","kind":"image","subtype":"png","content_type":"image/png","bytes":48213,"source":"magic","supported":[...]}`; `data.metadata.content_kind` (`"html"`, `"pdf"`, ...) and `content_kind_source`; `page_fetched.payload.content_kind`. 415 (not 501, which orchestrators retry; not a 200 with an empty body) maps to the orchestrator's non-retryable `CategoryClient4xx` and counts as `pages_failed` without failing a crawl (X-14 Q2). Field errors: 400 `BAD_REQUEST` with `details.fields[] {path, code, message}` (for example `unsupported_format` with `supported`), so a Model that proposed bad options can correct itself. Inline caps: over cap without ZDR the field is omitted and listed in `omitted` with the `formats.*` ref as fallback; over cap under ZDR it is truncated at a char boundary and listed in `truncated`; under ZDR with no `formats` the default is `["markdown"]` inline. - *API:* `POST /v1/crawl` response `data.limits {max_pages{requested, effective, clamped_by[]}, max_depth{...}}`, `clamped_by` in `default|hard`; job `params.max_pages` becomes the effective value, `params.max_pages_requested` added. A request with `max_pages: 0` or no `max_pages` gets the finite default (1000) and the response shows `limits.max_pages.clamped_by:["default"]` (0 is absent, never unlimited and never a 400 at the edge in W1); a direct-to-edge `0` is refused only after `QUARRY_EDGE__CRAWL_REQUEST_VALIDATION=strict` (WS14.I). No SQL, no proto.
- *Flag and rollout:* env `QUARRY_CRAWL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES` 1000, `QUARRY_CRAWL_HARD_MAX_PAGES` 5000 (ceiling pending the owner ruling; env-overridable), `QUARRY_CRAWL_DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH` 5, `QUARRY_CRAWL_HARD_MAX_DEPTH` 10; `0` on a default disables the default, never the hard ceiling (rollback). Deploy orchestrator and edge together (either alone is safe). `GetVersion` protects in-flight workflows.
- *Tests:* Go workflow `TestCrawlJobWF_ZeroMaxPagesFallsBackToCap`, `TestCrawlJobWF_FailuresCountTowardCap`, `TestCrawlJobWF_ZeroMaxDepthFallsBackToDepthCap`, `TestCrawlJobWF_OldVersionHistoryKeepsLegacyBehaviour` (`OnGetVersion` hook availability in the pinned Temporal SDK is [UNVERIFIED]; else a `WorkflowReplayer` run on a recorded history); jobs `TestResolve_ZeroUsesDefault`, `TestResolve_ClampsToHardAndReports`, `TestResolve_DefaultZeroDisablesDefaultNotHard`; Rust `zero_is_absent_and_takes_default`, `above_hard_is_clamped_and_reported`, `depth_resolves_like_pages`, `from_env_rejects_unparsable_naming_the_variable`; integration `crawl_limits` (axum stub as control; a ZDR caller is still refused at `routes.rs:555-588`); gateway `start_crawl_exposes_upstream_limits`. Commands: `cd "apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-orchestrator" && go test ./...`; `cd "apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2" && cargo test -p quarry-edge crawl_limits limits`; `cargo test --manifest-path "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/Cargo.toml" quarry`. The Go tests, including the `GetVersion` replay guard, run in CI only in the report-only `go-coverage` job (`continue-on-error: true`, `quarry-v2-ci.yml:306-309`) until WS14.S0b adds the hard `go-test` job; until then the PR attaches the local `go test ./...` output. The lenient-versus-strict pair `crawl_request_zero_pages_is_default_in_lenient_and_400_in_strict` belongs to WS14.I; WS6.A owns only the lenient half.
- *Definition of done:* no path starts a crawl without a finite page, failure and depth bound; ack and stored job carry requested and effective values; old histories replay; docs corrected.
- *Deployment evidence:* rebuild edge and orchestrator (`make up` with the deploy-recipe env chain); test-only `QUARRY_CRAWL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES=7`. (1) Gateway `POST /api/v1/knowledge/crawl` with only `url` of a public site with more than 7 internal links: `limits.max_pages.effective == 7`, `clamped_by == ["default"]`. (2) Direct to `127.0.0.1:8082` with `"max_pages": 0`: identical. (3) `/api/v1/knowledge/jobs/{id}/events` terminal `run.completed` shows `pages_visited == 7`. (4) control `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` shows `params.max_pages == 7`. (5) Pre-fix capture on the old image, cancelled manually after 7 pages. The off-site walk is closed by WS14, not here.
- *Risks:* workflow non-determinism if `GetVersion` is wrong (replay test); default 1000 changes behaviour for unbounded callers (equals the unused frontier default, and the response now says so); the 30-minute timeout still ends big crawls without a typed outcome (F-t2-017).

- *API:* `POST /v1/agent/runs` body optional `initiated_by:"agent"`; response `data.constraints {class, max_steps, max_runtime_s, max_cost_usd, estimated}` and `clamped[{field, requested, effective, by}]` (`by` in `default|ceiling|grant|org_default|entitlement`); step/interact success `meta.budget {class, steps, attempts, max_steps, max_attempts, elapsed_s, max_runtime_s, spent_usd, max_cost_usd, estimated, cost_source, exhausted}`; refusal 402 `error.code BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `details {dimension (steps|attempts|runtime|cost|org_allowance), limit, spent, unit, estimated, limit_source, resumable}`, `retryable false`; `DELETE` response `usage {spent_usd, steps, attempts, active_s, class, exhausted}`; event `agent.budget_exhausted {dimension, limit, spent, unit, estimated}` once per segment via `emit_for_zdr`; migration `0011`. Semantics: effective = min of present {request, grant claim, org default, entitlement remaining, Quarry ceiling}; absent/0 request takes the agent default, not unlimited; attempts allowance `max_steps x factor`; runtime clock excludes `HumanTakeover` pause; projected-cost check before execution; Interactive class is never capped; exhaustion latches; resume cannot refill.
- *Flag and rollout:* `QUARRY_EDGE__BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT=off|shadow|on` (`shadow` first deploy at least 24 h, review `would_exhaust` by class: a human session must never appear; then `on`; `off` is rollback), `AGENT_DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS/_RUNTIME_S/_COST_USD` 60/900/1.00, `AGENT_CEILING_...` 300/3600/20.00, `BUDGET_ATTEMPT_FACTOR` 2, `BUDGET_BROWSER_SECOND_USD` 0.00003 (placeholder; must come from the billing-core price table before `on`). Numbers are X-12 placeholders. Image rollback is safe (all persisted additions are defaulted or nullable).

- *Deployment evidence:* rebuild edge; test-only `BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT=on`, `AGENT_DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS=5`. (1) Human not capped: open a UI browser session, send 20 scripted actions through the gateway `run_action` route, all 200 (record the pre-slice baseline where the 13th returns 429); no `would_exhaust` for class `interactive`. (2) Agent capped: start an AI browser run from chat without a step limit; after the fifth completed action the edge answers 402 `dimension: steps`; `GET /v1/agent/runs/{id}/receipts` shows exactly 5 receipts each `cost_micro_usd > 0` and `cost_source: flat_table`; SSE shows one `agent.budget_exhausted`; `psql` on `quarry_agent_run_checkpoints` shows `state->>'budget_exhausted' = 'steps'` and status still `active`. (3) Service token with `max_cost_usd: 50`: `clamped` lists effective 20.0 `by: ceiling`. (4) Idle-expire run (2) then `POST /v1/agent/runs` with `resume_run_id`: first step refused at once. - *Risks:* false cap on a human session (class-keyed, shadow stage, named test); estimator error (labelled `estimated`, shadow compared to receipts, rate is env); plan fails on 402 until sibling (b) lands (agent default is generous); approval wait counts as runtime (documented, F-t2-033 decides); WS2 not landed (same code fits the monolith at higher merge cost).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Control Plane owns plan and org numbers (`quarry.cap.*`, allowance policies, per-run ceiling); Quarry enforces and never stores or computes entitlements, reads billing-core over one read-only principal and has no database access; the estimator rates are budget heuristics, not prices (prices stay in billing-core and Lago). Model Plane mints the grant claim and enforces the combined cap in execution-core; cost-core is not written in v1.
- ZDR: accumulators are memory-only and no checkpoint is written for ZDR; usage metadata under ZDR is an allowlist with no URL, host, title, fingerprint or query; metrics labels are closed sets; crawl and batch stay refused under ZDR so no ZDR backlog row exists (a test pins it); drain writes no ZDR checkpoint; a ZDR crash loses an in-memory segment (under-billing accepted).
- Quarry rejects: budgets, caps and clamps only tighten (`min`), `initiated_by` and class hints are tighten-only, and the budget gate runs before the single-use approval is consumed.

**Cross-session:** `LimitsResolver`, `meta.budget`, `clamped`, usage events and the 402 contract: WS6 (Quarry). `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` to resource-limit mapping, combined cap, `initiated_by:"agent"` on every call, `RATE_LIMITED` bounded retry, `RUNTIME_NOT_READY` backoff: sibling (b) (execution-core, model-gateway). Grant budget fields: WS1 (broker owner). Plan and capacity numbers and the `quarry-edge` billing credential: Control Plane. Space: runs started by a service principal are class `Agent` and budgeted, `space` is in the closed `surface` enum and only service tokens may set `x-verevon-surface`; sandbox-second metering (no `sandbox.second` event exists) is sibling (a)'s decision; per-Space limits do not exist and none are invented here.

#### WS7. Web policy and one tighten-only ResolvedPolicy  (Wave 2; owner: Ingestion Plane quarry-core/runtime/edge for the owner-neutral slices, Control Plane org-core and auth-core plus Model Plane browser-broker for the owner-dependent slices, sibling (b) for WS7.L; effort: L, 52.5 engineer-days (48.5 without the optional WS7.M); lane: L13 WEB-POLICY-QUARRY, with WS7.D in L2, WS7.H and WS7.I in L9, WS7.K in L1, WS7.L in L8)

**Resolves:** F-t2-022 in full; F-t2-032 only its typed-denial/action-class/carrier part (the E1 sub-line, absorbed here; per-origin consent and the settings hub stay the W3 epic E3.2). **Depends on:** WS2.A (`raw_script_denied`) before WS7.D, WS2.B/C (module split, `admit_action`, `StepInitiator`) soft for WS7.D, WS5.D (`ScrapeRequest` field) soft for WS7.C, WS1.A/B (and WS1.C for persistence) for WS7.K, WS14 and WS15 for WS7.G's durable-job snapshot (6b), sibling (b) for WS7.L. **Gated by:** ADR-1/OQ-1 (policy of record; recommendation outcome C: org-core owns, claim on user tokens and org-resolved service tokens, grant carries a snapshot, claim staleness about 345 s, fail-to-floor on the entitlement read), with the Control Plane owner's sign-off on registry field `webPolicyByAudience` and token lifetime, and the product input on entitlements and who may grant `robots.max_mode=ignore` (OQ-11, default platform operators only). Gates WS7.A, WS7.H, WS7.I, WS7.J, WS7.K, WS7.M. WS7.B to WS7.G (21.5 days) need no ruling. Not gated by ADR-3/4/5/6.

**How the ADR-1 outcome changes the slices:** under outcome A (user claims only) WS7.I drops the registry part and WS7.K becomes the mandatory Model-run carrier (WS1 a hard dependency, bound users 45 s, Model runs 15 min, WS7.M mandatory); under outcome B (capability-core owns) WS7.H is replaced by capability-core migration `apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/migrations/0016_org_web_policy.up.sql` [NEW] (outcome B only; next free after `0015`) with a parameter store beside `registry/scope_store.go`, there is no claim, user and SDK calls on the acquisition routes are unpinned and the Model Plane would own org entitlements (conflicts with CLAUDE.md, the reason B is not recommended). WS7.B to WS7.G and WS7.L are unchanged under every outcome because the org layer is an `Option<PolicyLayer>`. Epic E-032 (per-origin consent, settings hub) is the W3 epic E3.2: it reuses the typed-denial vocabulary, the action-class mapping, `RequestAsk` and the claim and grant carriers built here.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Control Plane owns org policy and entitlements (outcome C: org-core store and audit, auth-core issuer); Ingestion only enforces; the broker carries a snapshot derived from the verified bearer and accepts no caller-supplied policy; capability-core stays an allow/deny/ask engine, not a policy store.
- ZDR is never a key in `web_policy` and never part of the claim: `ResolvedPolicy.zdr` is the existing floor, existing refusals stay (`refuse_durable_job_under_zdr` `routes.rs:563-588`, `zdr_forbids_persistent_profile` `agent_routes.rs:527-533`, `allow_paid_providers && !zdr` `search_routes.rs:529`) with an equivalence test before any deletion; denial events carry capability and decision source only (via `emit_for_zdr`), org-core audit rows carry keys and `tightened`, never domains for a ZDR org; the 6b snapshot travels only on non-ZDR durable jobs.
- Every denial is produced by Quarry before an approval, budget or receipt is consumed; the Model influences policy only through a tighten-only `RequestAsk` (a Space restriction enters the same way) and a planner hint, so no Space or caller can widen an owner-plane ACL.

**Cross-session:** `RequestAsk` as the only way a Space restricts a browser or crawl, and the `policy.denied` event (`capability`, `decision_source`, `denied_action`, `policy_rev`, never a URL): contract WS7, Space settings storage Application Plane (sibling a). `browser.proto` field 20 and the `PolicyResolver` hook: contract WS7, code WS1 with sibling (b). `StartRunRequest.policy` and the `policy_denied` mapping in `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/quarry_agent.rs`, plus the vendored `RequestAsk` golden: sibling (b). Approvals: `policy_denied` is never approvable (sibling b). A Space-hosted run is under its owner's claim and grant, never the Space's.

#### WS8. Shared browser backend: human-browse grants, session-bound agent attach, per-tab control  (Wave 2; owner: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser/runtime/edge, Model Plane browser-broker, model-gateway and execution-core, Frontend gateway; effort: XL, 68 engineer-days (63 without the optional WS8.K); lane: L10 SHARED-BROWSER-QUARRY, with WS8.C in L1, WS8.D and WS8.I in L6, WS8.E in L3, WS8.G in L8)

**Resolves:** F-t2-011 backend half (WS8.B, C, D; the omnibox is WS9), F-t2-013 phase 2 (WS8.E to WS8.I; the audit's "L to XL" is XL because ownership is one of six independent blockers), F-t2-013 phase 3 (WS8.J), the ADR-3 spike and ledger entry (WS8.A), audit open question 12 (answered in the design, ratification below). **Depends on:** WS1.A and WS1.B (production grants, `Repository`, kinds, `Derive`, `owner_id`/`zdr` on validate, `absolute_expires_at`, projection `grantId`, `x-browser-authorization`), WS1.C (Postgres grant store) for production `human_browse`, WS2.B and WS2.C (module split, `admit_action`, `RunLive`, `StepInitiator`, `USER_TOOK_OVER`), WS2.D (registry, `Interactive` class idle semantics, sweeper) for the orphan sweep, WS3.C, WS3.D and WS3.F merged before WS8.E (same `chromiumoxide.rs` call sites; the full queue is the R-31 line in WS8.E). **Gated by:** ADR-3/OQ-2/OQ-12 ratified as one package (D8-1 kinds and invariants I1 to I8, D8-2 open web minus deny-list, D8-3 numbers 900 s idle, 1800 s takeover idle, 4 h absolute, attach 900 s with 180 s idle release, keep-alive 300 s, D8-7 implicit take-over, OQ-12 one long-lived user-owned run per visible session); X-13 (D8-5 metadata-only human evidence blocks `human_browse` enablement, D8-6 shared jar blocks `ATTACH` GA, D8-7 blocks the WS8.F default); X-2 (ZDR human sessions rely on a memory-only grant on a single broker replica); X-1 (quarry-edge as read-only `browser-broker` principal, otherwise no production run validates); ADR-1 only for the org override behind `PolicyResolver.ResolveHumanBrowse` (static default ships). Ratify ADR-3 in the first weeks of Wave 1 so Wave 2 can start; the observe-only relay of WS9.J is then dropped (saves 8 to 10 days).

**Can start without the decision:** WS8.A (spikes feed the ADR), WS8.B in full except production enablement (strict tightenings: open-web policy type, tolerant timeline decode, metadata-only human receipts, URL-stripped checkpoints, budget exemption, flag-gated `human_browse`), WS8.E (capability bits, no caller), WS8.H lane split (behaviour-neutral for runs without an attach), WS8.G client code against wiremock. **Blocked:** merge of WS8.C (wire-visible kinds, proto 50-59, `RenewGrant`), merge of WS8.F and WS8.G, `human_browse` in production (retention answer, WS1.C, evidence), `ATTACH` in production (WS8.H, evidence, jar and idle numbers), org-level deny list.

**State of the code (verified 2026-10-14, live tree; first five are the load-bearing ones):**
- Per-session driver state: one `SessionPages {active_tab_id, tabs, browser_context_id, download_dir}` per run id; every driver call resolves its page through `active_tab_page` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:346-356` [C], confirmed) and `open_tab_page` ends with `session_pages.active_tab_id = Some(tab_id.clone())` (`:555`, confirmed): every new tab steals the active slot (F2). Egress policy is per session (`egress_policies` 130, guard 747-756), collectors (`devtools_events` 2591, `egress_receipts` 2614, dialogs 137-142) read the whole session unfiltered (F4: a human tab's network URLs and console lines would reach a model observation). `BrowserSession` is built by struct literal in 13 places.
- Admission and ownership: `caller_owns_browser_run` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:474-482` [C], confirmed at 474) needs org and actor equality, so a service call on a user-owned run is a 404; `validate_run_grant` (314-338) demands exact equality of the broker domain list; `canonical_broker_domains` rejects empty or over-32 lists (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:59-77`), so no grant can say "any public host"; `enforce_step_budget` (446-451, confirmed) counts human and agent steps alike.
- The gateway creates every UI session with `max_steps 12`, `allowed_domains: [first host]`, `max_runtime_s 120` (`apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:483-494` [C], confirmed) and `run_action` pre-flips the whole session to `human_takeover` on any human action (715-731): incompatible with concurrent co-browsing (F5).
- Broker: `defaultGrantTTL = 15 * time.Minute` (`apps/Model Plane/go/services/browser-broker/internal/server/server.go:22` [C], confirmed); `AcquireGrantRequest.mode` already means `local|cloud` (`apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/browser.proto:30-33`) so a kind needs a new field; `Grant` has no kind, owner on validation, renewal or absolute cap until WS1.
- Receipts persist the post-action observation and typed text for every non-ZDR step and the checkpoint stores the full current URL (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/step_receipts.rs:183-210`, `0007_step_receipts.sql`, `0006_agent_run_checkpoints.sql`; written at `step` 2352-2366 and `execute_ws_action` 3155-3165): with free human browsing this is a browsing-history store (F1). The run mutex is held across each action (2248-2408) with one shared `ObservationContext` (F6); event idempotency keys use `{run_id}:action:{ctx.step}` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/observation.rs:392-393, 1010`) so two lanes would collide (F7).

Observable assertion: Quarry, not the gateway, refuses the agent after the user acts in its tab.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Phase A adds no claim, principal or scope in Control Plane; every authority (`human_browse`, `attach`, renew) is minted or renewed by the broker only from a verified user bearer and no service principal holds `browser:write` (asserted, extended to `RenewGrant`); Quarry keeps `browser:read` only; derive and renew use the user's own bearer. Phase B (WS8.K) is an explicit optional Control Plane decision.
- ZDR: attach is refused in three layers (model-gateway `browser_run.rs:307-315`, broker `ErrAttachZdrRefused`, Quarry `attach_zdr_refused`); ZDR human sessions hold a memory-only grant (X-2), persist nothing (no receipts, checkpoint or timeline) and keep-alive persists nothing; attach state, ledger and epochs are memory-only; `agent.attached`/`agent.detached` use `emit_for_zdr` and carry no URL or title; collectors are pin-filtered so a human tab's data never enters a model observation; non-ZDR human steps persist metadata-only receipts and URL-stripped checkpoints.
- Quarry executes or rejects every proposed step and `mark_tab` through one ordered admission chain (R-7); the model never chooses domains (the attach list comes from the user's narrowing request, validated by the broker, enforced per tab at the CDP Fetch guard); `initiated_by` sent by a service is ignored for delegates; SSRF layer untouched under open web (private, loopback, link-local and metadata targets stay blocked: `agent_navigation_blocks_private_targets_at_edge_boundary`, `quarry-browser/tests/ssrf.rs`, `quarry-runtime/tests/browser_egress_boundary.rs`).

**Cross-session:** broker grant kinds, derive purposes and proto 50-59: kinds and numbers WS8, broker repository WS1; sibling (b) must not add a second grant API or a purpose outside the one `Derive` allow-list. Quarry attach contract (`attach`, `release`, `tabs/{id}/control`, `mark`, `StepBody.grant_id`, `USER_TOOK_OVER` details): WS8; sibling (b) consumes it in execution-core, the MCP facade and the pause mapping, and must always send `initiated_by:"agent"` on a service principal. Delegated bearer forwarding (OD13): attach must use a service principal; recorded in the WS8.A ledger. `browser.mark_tab` schema registration: sibling (b). Approvals (F-t2-033): sensitive approvals use the attach grant as parent; the one-shot rule stays. Space (sibling a): a Space-hosted agent run attaches only to a session owned by the acting user; no `space_id` exists in any grant, attach body or `AttachState`; a member cannot watch or drive another member's session (new shared-session ACL is out of scope); presence renders `openedBy`, `holder`, `attach.state`, `tabEpoch` from Quarry's projection. WS9: the strip reads `tabs[].holder` when `tab_control` is advertised and keeps session control as "Pause all agents"; one state enum only (D8-10); wire `human`, SPA adapter `user`. F-t2-035 and F-t2-054 extend `RunLive` and `TabLedger` and add no parallel state enum.

#### WS9. Shared browser frontend: omnibox, chat dock, tab and control UI, run-evidence panels  (Wave 2; owner: Frontend Plane (SPA `src/features/browser/*` and gateway `browser_evidence.rs`) with Ingestion Plane quarry-edge/browser halves and sibling (b) for WS9.E; effort: L, 47 engineer-days scheduled (38 without the conditional WS9.J); lane: L6 SPA-GATEWAY, with WS9.E in L8)

**Resolves:** F-t2-011 frontend half (WS9.A omnibox, WS9.B reload and error page), F-t2-012 (WS9.F controller, WS9.G dock layouts, WS9.H interactive dock; WS9.J is the conditional observed-view binding), F-t2-013 UI step c1 (WS9.I control strip, markers, Reveal; the per-tab attach UI is WS8.I), F-t2-014 first UI slice (WS9.C, D, E). **Depends on:** WS2.C deployed (control epoch, `expected_epoch`, `initiatedBy`, `USER_TOOK_OVER`) for WS9.I; WS1 for the end-to-end evidence of WS9.E (the browser MCP tools need a broker-validated grant, `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/tool_bridge/mod.rs` 244-248); WS8.C/D (human-session budgets and cross-host policy) for general availability of WS9.A and WS9.H; soft: WS4.A (org in the gateway cache key) before the production omnibox flag, WS3.D (`chromiumoxide.rs` order) for WS9.B, WS2.B (`agent_routes.rs` split) for WS9.C and WS9.B. **Gated by:** ADR-3/OQ-12 (WS9.H GA, WS9.K and WS9.L; ratified early, so the observed-view fallback WS9.J is dropped and the attach UI is delivered inside WS8.I), ADR-4 (omnibox ZDR rule: no history, no suggestions under ZDR, matches WS4's "never loosen" default); X-18 product choices (org-scoped autocomplete, chat-per-tab default `keep`, ZDR thread dock is human-only). WS9.A, B, C, D, F, G start now (WS9.A and WS9.H merge behind flags that stay off in production until WS8 removes the 12-step, first-host, 120 s limits; WS9.I starts when WS2.C is deployed).

**Reconciliation overrides applied:** ADR-3 is ratified early and WS9.J (observed relay, 6a) is dropped unless ADR-3 is refused (R-17, saves 8 to 10 days); WS9.K (6b attach UI) is delivered inside WS8.I and `use-browser-session-controller.ts` (the controller hands the session id to every existing route because the run actor is then the user); the control strip reads `tabs[].holder` when `tab_control` is advertised and keeps session control as "Pause all agents"; one session state enum only (D8-10); `openedBy` is `human` on the wire and `user` in the SPA type through an adapter; `reload{ignore_cache}` is a human-only Quarry wire action: the Model Plane `browser.act` schema never auto-exposes a Quarry action and any new action (`reload`, tab control, `mark`) needs an explicit entry in WS3 S11's closed list (R-12, `AgentAction::Evaluate` is removed from `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/quarry_agent.rs:161` by sibling (b)); `BrowserChrome.tsx` takes wiring hunks only, new code lives in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/browser/*` (R-31, owner is WS9); the `browser.observe/act/console` external-content classification is a security fix that ships now, not with the console tool (X-18); new action ids get a dispatcher arm or `action-surface-contract.test.mjs` fails; every new gateway error code gets a `no`/`en` row in `shared/i18n/errors.ts`; production flags per R-29 (`VITE_BROWSER_OMNIBOX_SEARCH` waits for WS4.A, `VITE_CHAT_BROWSER_DOCK` interactive mode waits for WS8). The `BrowserChrome.tsx` file hunk order is WS9.A, WS9.B, WS3.J (error copy), WS9.D, WS9.I, WS8.D, WS8.I.

**Common rules for every WS9 slice.** Gates (from `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3`): `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (four `node --test` gateway scripts incl. `action-surface-contract.test.mjs`, then `vitest run`), `pnpm build`, and `cargo test --manifest-path apps/gateway/Cargo.toml --all-targets` (CI adds `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `verevonv3-ci.yml:132-141`). In a worktree `pnpm` prunes `pnpm-lock.yaml` (restore with `git checkout -- "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/pnpm-lock.yaml"` after the last pnpm call), `node_modules` is absent (`pnpm install --prefer-offline`), and `:5173` serves the main checkout (serve a worktree on `:5174` with `pnpm dev --port 5174 --strictPort`). Quarry changes run in the `rust:1` container recipe. Model Plane: `cd "apps/Model Plane/rust" && cargo test -p execution-core --lib <name>`. Playwright is not in CI: new specs are named `browser-workspace-*.spec.ts` and run in the `local` project (`pnpm exec playwright test --project=local tests/e2e/<spec>` against `LOCAL_E2E_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:5173`). CRLF files (`browser-omnibox.ts`, `KnowledgeComposer.tsx`) keep their line endings, no repo-wide formatter. Every new UI string goes through `useI18n().tr(no, en)`; do not mass-translate BrowserChrome (e2e selectors depend on its Bokmal literals). Deployment evidence for the SPA: `docker restart frontend-plane-verevonv3-frontend-1`, wait for HTTP 200 on `:5173`, then `await fetch('/src/styles/global.css',{cache:'reload'}); location.reload()`. Gateway: `docker build -t frontend-plane-verevonv3-gateway:latest -f "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/Dockerfile" "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway"` then `python3 C:/dev/tools/swap_gateway_image.py`. Quarry edge: `docker compose -p ingestion-plane <env-file chain> -f "apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml" up -d --no-deps --build quarry-edge`. Model Plane: `bash "apps/Model Plane/scripts/compose.sh" up -d --no-deps --build execution-core model-gateway`.

- *Behaviour:* Enter on free text opens Verevon search results in the frame stage (never a third-party engine); the dropdown has an explicit "Ask Verevon" row and a "Search the web" row; ZDR (retention verdict deny, temporary thread, or `session().zdr`) means no local history, no suggestions and no search-home recording, enforced client side and refused server side; until WS8 a cross-host result click returns 403 and the UI shows "This session is limited to {host}".
- *API/data:* no proto, no SQL, no Quarry change; new gateway error code; new action ids; one local-storage key. No OpenAPI change.
- *Flag:* build flag `VITE_BROWSER_OMNIBOX_SEARCH` (1 in dev and staging builds, 0 in production builds until WS4.A puts the org in the gateway cache key); off leaves URL navigation and local history and shows a "search is not enabled here" row. Rollback: flip the flag and restart the frontend container; the ZDR gate on suggestions only tightens.
- *Tests:* `cd "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3" && pnpm exec vitest run src/features/browser/omnibox src/features/dashboard/home/browser-omnibox.test.ts src/shared/session/home-local-content.test.ts src/shared/actions`: `omnibox-resolver.test.ts` (URL, host, query, demo, empty with fallback), `omnibox-history.test.ts` (per-identity key, retention-denied writes nothing, URL scrub keeps `?q=a` and drops `?token=x`, cap 200, corrupt record reads empty, purge through `clearHomeLocalContent`), `omnibox-suggestions.test.tsx` (debounce, abort, zero `fetch` calls and zero storage reads under `zdr()`), `OmniboxField.test.tsx` (keyboard model, Escape does not bubble, Shift+Delete), `BrowserSearchResults.test.tsx`; gateway `search_suggestions_empty_under_zdr_header`, `search_suggestions_empty_under_org_zdr` (wiremock org-core, pattern `browser.rs` 4174-4215), `forward_quarry_failure_maps_navigation_scope`; `action-surface-contract.test.mjs` proves registry and dispatcher parity; Playwright `tests/e2e/browser-workspace-omnibox.spec.ts` [NEW].
- *DoD:* free text never produces a google.com URL in any build; the demo build still returns no search (probe `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/scripts/probe-product-demo.mjs` [U]); URL input navigates; the dropdown works with keyboard only; ZDR issues zero history reads and zero suggestion requests (client and gateway); the two ids dispatch; `pnpm test` has the baseline failing set; `docs/BROWSER_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md` [C] gets a short omnibox section.
- *Deployment evidence:* rebuild and swap the gateway image, restart the frontend container (or serve the worktree on `:5174`). As `local@verevon.dev`: Home, Innhent, open `https://example.com`, type `norwegian salmon exports` in the address bar. Assert the dropdown shows the Search and Ask rows; Enter renders result cards in the frame stage; the network log shows `POST /api/v1/search/web` with that query and no request to `google.com`; the Quarry timeline (`GET /api/v1/browser/sessions/{id}/timeline`) has no new `navigate` item. Type `exam`: a history row for `example.com` appears. Toggle ZDR for the session and reopen the bar: no history rows and zero `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions` requests; `curl` the gateway with `x-zdr: 1` returns `{"data":{"suggestions":[]}}`. Click a result on another host: the "limited to example.com" row appears (the honest pre-WS8 state).
- *Risks:* `BrowserChrome.tsx` collisions (wiring-only hunks); cache without org key (production flag held for WS4.A); Escape collides with the global `dismiss` (field stops propagation, test pins it); org-scoped suggestions (X-18: recommend local history plus related queries only; the dashboard dropdown already shows colleagues' terms).

These are the epics E3.3 and E3.2 in wave 3.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Frontend Plane owns the omnibox, dock, strip, panels and the same-origin gateway normalisation (typed envelopes, no upstream secrets, no raw OAuth tokens, no forged scoping headers; the gateway derives org and user from `require_session` and `resolve_browser_run_owner`, never `x-verevon-org-id`, enforced by the fabrication guard); nothing is persisted in the Data Plane; omnibox history and dock state are local storage; receipts and procedures are read from Quarry over HTTP with the user's owner-scoped token; no cross-plane database access (the "admit org members to service-owned runs" variant is rejected).
- ZDR: no omnibox history, suggestions or search-home recording under ZDR (client and gateway); dock state is layout only and never server-side; evidence panels are unavailable under ZDR except the live-only egress read and nothing from panels is persisted in the SPA; free-text search under ZDR goes through the WS4-fixed gateway path (no cache, no `SearchIssued`); a ZDR thread's dock is a human-only browser (model-gateway already refuses ZDR browser runs).
- Every human action (navigate, reload, click, take over) is a request Quarry validates against the grant and domain list; `reload` is human-only and absent from the Model tool schemas; `browser.console` is read-only and grant-checked; page context never travels from the SPA to the Model (the Ask paths attach nothing).

**Cross-session:** `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/browser/*` is the single home for browser UI, owner WS9; Space reuses `useBrowserSessionController` and the panels and does not fork a controller (sibling a), and presence renders from Quarry's `controlEpoch` and `initiatedBy`/`openedBy`/`holder`, not a gateway cache; Space members cannot view a member's browser (`caller_owns_live_run` is owner-only). `browser.console`, the `TrustClass` fix and the `execution-core` edits: sibling (b) implements, WS9 specifies (both copies of `classify` change together). `initiated_by:"agent"` on every Model Plane Quarry call and `USER_TOOK_OVER` mapped to a paused run: sibling (b) (the dock's Take over relies on it). Chat controller edits (`use-chat-controller.ts`, `ChatPage.tsx`) and the floating composer: sibling (b) owns the controller, WS9 adds a 6-line dock hook and the edit order is agreed first. Local keys follow `verevon.<feature>.v1:{org}:{user}` and register their purge in `home-local-content.ts`. Chat-thread versus Quarry run lifetime (OQ-12) is decided with ADR-3.

*Contract:* optional request header and response header `x-request-id` on every Quarry and gateway response; no proto, migration or OpenAPI path change. The id is never an authorization, tenancy or idempotency key and is not unique across tenants (support lookups filter by `(org_id, request_id)`). *Flag/rollback:* always on; `QUARRY_EDGE__REQUEST_ID_ADOPT=0` always mints; the codemod PR reverts independently. *Tests:* unit in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/request_id.rs` [NEW]: `adopts_a_valid_inbound_id`, `mints_when_the_inbound_id_is_longer_than_128_bytes`, `mints_when_the_inbound_id_has_spaces_or_control_characters`, `never_returns_400_for_a_bad_id`, `echoes_the_header_on_success_and_error_responses`, `adopt_flag_off_always_mints`; router `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/tests/request_id.rs` [NEW] (uses `tests/support/mod.rs` `base_state`; run with `cargo test -p quarry-edge --test request_id`): `meta_request_id_equals_the_response_header`, `the_request_id_is_not_an_auth_or_tenancy_key`; Go `TestRequestIDRejectsOverlongAndForeignCharset`, `TestRequestIDAdoptsValid`; gateway `request_id::tests::*`, `browser_proxy_forwards_request_id_to_quarry`, `invalid_inbound_request_id_is_replaced_not_forwarded`. Commands: `cargo test -p quarry-edge request_id`; `cd services/quarry-control && go test ./internal/httpx/...`; `cd "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway" && cargo test request_id browser_proxy` (plus fmt and clippy `-D warnings`). *DoD:* `grep -rn "RequestKind::new()" "apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src"` returns only `request_id.rs`; CONTRACTS.md updated. *Evidence:* rebuild `quarry-edge`, `quarry-control`, gateway; `curl -i -H "x-request-id: e2e-d10-<uuid>"` through the gateway: header echoed, `docker logs quarry-edge` has `"request_id":"e2e-d10-<uuid>"`, a failing call's `meta.request_id` equals the header, a 300-char id yields a server-minted `req_` id. *Risks:* task-local lost across `tokio::spawn` (accepted); two layers on the same router line with WS4/WS2 (merge order stated); log cardinality (charset and cap bound it).

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run_trace_events (
    ingest_seq BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    event_id TEXT NOT NULL, run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (org_id <> ''), user_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    producer TEXT NOT NULL, producer_seq BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (producer_seq > 0),
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL, schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, received_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    resource_ref TEXT NOT NULL, correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', causation_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    request_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', agent_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', agent_role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    agent_parent_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK (origin IN ('','USER','AGENT','SCHEDULE','WEBHOOK','API')),
    payload JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb CHECK (octet_length(payload::text) <= 8192),
    CONSTRAINT run_trace_events_producer_seq_uq UNIQUE (run_id, producer, producer_seq),
    CONSTRAINT run_trace_events_event_id_uq UNIQUE (event_id));
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS run_trace_events_run_idx ON run_trace_events (org_id, run_id, ingest_seq);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS run_trace_events_received_idx ON run_trace_events (received_at);
```

Assertions: per-run `producer_seq` dense except the logged gap; zero duplicates in `run_trace_events`; rows = published minus `dropped`; consumer lag p99 under 2 s; Quarry step latency p99 within 5 percent with publisher on vs off; session-core CPU and Postgres write rate recorded. *Workstream deployment evidence:* all images rebuilt, stack up, non-ZDR user runs a chat browser turn over three pages (WS1 working, or the S4 stand-in) with `x-request-id: e2e-d10-<uuid>`: (1) `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/trace` returns Quarry events with that request id, `origin` `AGENT`, `agent.id`, dense `producer_seq`; (2) the Quarry SSE with a mid-run reconnect has no gap; (3) Convex `agentRuns.getByRunId` shows `browserActivity` (if ADR-8 part 2 ratified); (4) repeat as a ZDR user: SSE live, trace GET returns an empty page, `nats stream info` count unchanged, collector shows no spans, logs show no URL.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Ownership: Model Plane owns the run trace (contract, stream, `run_trace_events`, `EventLog`); Quarry only publishes over NATS with a publish-only principal and never writes Model Plane storage; identity comes only from the verified token, `trace.*` and `origin` are labels (session-core takes `org_id`/`user_id` from the run row); the gateway proxies and keeps no trace state; S7 only narrows access (matrix rule 10); no direct DB crossing.
- ZDR: publisher refuses ZDR at its door, `emit_for_zdr` keeps ZDR live-only, consumer requires explicit `"zdr": false` and also skips `runs.retention_class='zdr'`, no row/spans/Convex projection for ZDR, in-memory ring freed at `close_run` (X-5), logs carry only the non-content `request_id`; add the two WS4 matrix rows.
- Model proposes, Quarry executes: the trace carries consequences (receipts, egress decisions, artifacts, control changes), never a command channel or grant; `origin_is_not_authz` fails the build if admission or budget code reads `origin`; UIs must not read `origin=USER` as proof of human authority (WS2 `initiated_by` plus `control_epoch` is the control fact).

**Cross-session:** run trace read authorisation and Space sharing of a run: owner-only in v1, read-through with Control membership, sibling (a) with Control (F-t2-072); Application projection and presence chips: Application Plane, sibling (a) reads `browserActivity`; staffing of S6 (session-core consumer, `EventLog` server, routes, optional S6c) and `mp-telemetry` adoption: sibling (b) (X-6); start-run `trace` context and `x-request-id` forwarding plus the origin mapping function (chat/space/support/agent-run-console by a human = `USER`; capability-core cron and routines `0028_space_scoped_cron.sql` = `SCHEDULE`; background review/dreaming = `AGENT`; `mail_task` = `WEBHOOK`; direct service callers = `API`): sibling (b) in `EXC/quarry_agent.rs` `StartRunRequest` 180-192 via the R-22 contract PR; event numbering 150-159/fields 14-18 here, 160 for WS8's `BrowserAttachSharedJar` and 161+/21+ for others, pause and resume reuse 142/143 (ledger); live OrchestrationEvent tag 24 not built (client merges by `(producer, producer_seq)`, `ts`, `causation_id`); telemetry golden shared by contract, never code.

`PUT /orgs/<org>/quotas/browser_agent_max_tokens_per_run {"limit":3000}` then a multi-step task: `GET /v1/runs/<id>/events` ends in a resource-exhausted terminal state (not failed), usage line `planner_in + planner_out` at most 3,000 plus one call, `GET /v1/agent/runs/<qid>/receipts` matches the action count; session-core unit `cargo test -p session-core --bin session-core -- external_content`: `external_content_tool_list_is_pinned`, `mcp_prefixed_tools_are_external`, `org_internal_tools_are_not_external`; DB (`#[ignore]`, CI): `DATABASE_URL=postgres://session_core:session_core@localhost:5432/session_core_test REQUIRE_CONTRACT=1 cargo test -p session-core --bin session-core external_content -- --ignored --test-threads=1`: `external_content_marker_is_set_once_by_complete_step`, `external_content_marker_is_set_by_inline_reserve_tool_action`, `external_content_marker_reaches_the_parent_run`, `external_content_dreaming_skips_assistant_rows_in_the_window_and_ledgers_them`, `external_content_dreaming_keeps_user_rows_eligible`, `external_content_extractor_window_excludes_tainted_assistant_rows`, `external_content_zdr_run_stores_only_a_timestamp`, `external_content_thread_without_external_runs_is_unchanged`. *DoD:* all green; `0047` applies to empty and populated databases and reverts; the audit's `session_tool_audit_intents` derivation is deliberately replaced by the `CompleteStep` marker. *Evidence:* rebuild execution-core and session-core (`docker logs session-core` shows `0047` applied): (1) "search the web for <fixture topic> and remember the first result": `save_memory` shows the refusal, `SELECT external_content_at IS NOT NULL FROM runs WHERE id='<run>'` is true and `agent_memory` count for the thread is unchanged; (2) a new run in the same thread without web tools "remember that I prefer short answers" succeeds; (3) with `DREAMING_LLM_EXTRACTION=1` an assistant paraphrase inside the tainted window yields `dream_runs` `skipped_external_content` and no `agent_memory` row (baseline first: before the slice an `accepted` row is written); (4) a delegated child that calls `web_fetch` then the parent calls `save_memory`: refused; (5) an inline-loop chat turn after `web_search` sets `external_content_at` through `ReserveToolAction`. *Risks:* in-flight `dreaming.rs` and `agent.rs` hunks (land after Z-17 `0044`/`0045` committed, or rebase); over-blocking on research threads (message tells the model what to do, user rows eligible, quarantine/promotion is the later step B13); the 60 s window grace is a placeholder pinned by DB tests; protects durable memory, not the transcript.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Ownership: all code is Model Plane (execution-core, model-gateway, session-core) with no Quarry, Control, Data, Application or Frontend code change; the org flag and token ceiling are org-core quota rows written by an org admin through org-core's existing route and read with a service credential (interim, labelled, removed when ADR-1's carrier lands); the token meter is an in-process cap, not a ledger (cost-core is not written).
- ZDR: `PlannerPolicy::resolve` never selects the planner for ZDR and model-gateway refuses durable browser runs under ZDR (`apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/browser_run.rs` 307-315); `InferRequest.zdr` follows the plan; usage line, metric labels and the `planner_view` log line are counts and codes only; the action log is in-memory and never checkpointed; `external_content_at` is a timestamp derived from a tool name; a ZDR run never reaches memory tools (preflight refuses first, test pinned).
- Model proposes, Quarry executes: every verb is a proposal; execution-core admission and the risk gate only tighten, Quarry validates grant, domains, refs, budgets and may refuse, `policy_denied` and 403 are never retried or rephrased; `press` keys and `back` destinations are checked only in execution-core until the Ingestion companion lands (domain fence and post-action 403 remain); excluded verbs stay unreachable from the planner.

**Cross-session:** browser run parameters and the single model-gateway run-parameter helper: proposed owner this workstream S1/S2 with WS6 S4 `mint_budget` plugging in (Space must not build its own `tool_input`); single editor of the execution-core browser files (`browser_agent.rs`, `quarry_agent.rs`, `llm_planner.rs`, `tool_bridge/mod.rs`, `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/browser_run.rs`): one engineer from sibling (b); Quarry typed-error classification (`parse_typed_error`, `StepFailureClass`): S1/S3 here, others add arms; combined cost cap and cost-core writer: sibling (b) via OQ-14/X-7; delegated-bearer refresh (needed beyond about 240 s): WS1/sibling (b); approvals for a risky `press`/`select` reuse `gate_risky_action` (F-t2-033, sibling (b)); memory-taint promotion rule for Space threads (author versus Space owner) and the `done` answer destination: user must reconcile with sibling (a) (OD13).

**Slice WS12.S0 detail: rule module, golden, conformance harness**

Design rules (D12-1..D12-4): module in `quarry-core` (all four consumer crates already depend on it; `regex = "1"` is already in the lock through quarry-transform); two profiles: `Live` (applied to everything Quarry returns to any caller, including ZDR) and `Durable` (everything kept or emitted beyond the caller: receipts, checkpoints, events, JSON artifacts, logs, error text); `RULE_VERSION = "qr-redact/1"`; marker `[redacted:<kind>]` with kind in `password|otp|card|phone|secret|token|key|credential`; rule ids `field.password`, `field.otp`, `field.card`, `field.phone`, `field.label`, `field.luhn`, `shape.jwt`, `shape.pem`, `shape.aws`, `shape.github`, `shape.gitlab`, `shape.npm`, `shape.slack`, `shape.google`, `shape.openai`, `shape.stripe`, `shape.bearer`, `shape.basic`, `shape.userinfo`, `ctx.labelled_secret`, `ctx.otp_numeric`, `ctx.pan`, `url.query`, `url.fragment`. Live covers field-semantic values and high-confidence shapes; Durable adds contextual shapes (labelled secret assignment, numeric OTP beside an otp label, Luhn-valid PAN runs) and URL query/fragment secrets (keys `token`, `access_token`, `id_token`, `refresh_token`, `code`, `key`, `api_key`, `sig`, `signature`, `password`, `secret`, `session`, `sid`, `otp`, `jwt`, `x-amz-*`; fragment `access_token=`); `extraction_result` gets high-confidence shapes only (Live) so extraction keeps working. Regex engine is `regex` (linear time); a `RegexSet` pre-pass; JSON leaves capped at 64 KiB; budget 1 MiB of mixed text under 150 ms release. `Mode::{Enforce, Shadow, Off}` is process-wide (set once by the edge via `init_mode`, default `Enforce`, `ENVIRONMENT=production` accepts only `Enforce`); the library never reads env. Stamp `RedactionStamp {rule_version, profile, mode, values_masked: u32, by_rule: BTreeMap<String,u32>, probe: ok|partial|failed|skipped, probe_ms: u32, screenshot: none|masked|withheld}` carries no content, no lengths.

**Slice WS12.S1 detail: field-facts probe and AX/target masking**

Q10 recipe (D12-6, answers OQ-10) runs before S1 merges on the pinned Chromium (quarry-edge image): fixture `secrets-lab.html` with `<input id=pw type=password> (prefilled by the fixture script with a dummy value)`, `<input id=pw2 type=password>`, `<input id=cc autocomplete=cc-number value="4111111111111111">`, `<input id=tel type=tel value="+4799999999">`, `<input id=otp autocomplete=one-time-code>`, a `toggle` password input plus a button flipping its type to `text`, and `<input id=plain value="visible-text">`; raw CDP script (about 25 lines, `ws` or `chrome-remote-interface`, headless with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`): `Accessibility.enable`, type `s3cret-typed` into `pw2` with `Input.insertText`, click show, call `Accessibility.getFullAXTree{depth:8}` in the three states and print backend id, role, name, value, property names, plus `Browser.getVersion`; then `DOM.describeNode{backendNodeId}` without `DOM.enable` and record success or the error. **Slice WS12.S4 detail: Model Plane `mp-scrub`, planner and event scrub, stamp consumption**

Design basis (D12-9, D12-11): Quarry owns the canonical golden; the Model Plane vendors it byte-identical; the pattern set is shared by duplication plus conformance, not a cross-plane crate. Within the Model Plane `scrub.rs` is needed by execution-core and model-gateway (which does not depend on execution-core), so the copy moves into `apps/Model Plane/rust/crates/mp-scrub` [NEW]. The scrub is applied at the prompt and event boundary, never inside `observation_from_wire` (stop criteria match raw `extracted_text`, `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs` 349-356). The Live set requires a token-shaped body (at least 16 characters, at least one digit) so prose such as "bearer of the message" or "basic introduction" survives; the legacy `scrub_string` rules and tests do not move.

**Slice WS12.S5 detail: screenshot masking by element rectangle (fail closed)**

Design: a screenshot is captured on every observation (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/observation.rs` 517, 654) and feeds the artifact store, the vision sidecar (672-848), the UI-path VLM and the proof bundle; masking at the capture call masks every consumer without touching about 20 write sites. `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/sensitive_rects.rs` [NEW]: `scan_sensitive_rects(page, deadline) -> RectScan {rects, unresolved_visible, oopif_frames, scroll, dpr}` via one read-only `Runtime.evaluate` const script that walks `input,textarea,select,[contenteditable]`, recursing into open shadow roots and same-origin iframes (accumulating offset), returning facts (the Rust `classify_field` is authoritative) plus `getBoundingClientRect()`; padded rectangles (4 CSS px). `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/screenshot_mask.rs` [NEW]: `mask_png(png, rects, opts)` decodes with the `png` crate, fills solid `#1f2937`, re-encodes, refuses above 40 megapixels (withhold). Chromiumoxide `screenshot()` (2392): scan, capture, re-scan scroll (a scroll in between invalidates: re-scan once, else withhold), mask. New `BrowserDriver::screenshot_masked(&self, session, full_page) -> QuarryResult<MaskedScreenshot {bytes: Option<Bytes>, state, rects}>` with a default impl calling `screenshot` and reporting `none`. Rules: sensitive field visible and rect resolved -> masked; visible but unresolved (frame offset unknown, zero-size rect on a visible element, probe error) -> withheld (no artifact, `screenshot_artifact_id` omitted, sidecar and image artifact writes at 686-834 skipped, note `screenshot_withheld:sensitive_field_unresolved`); none present -> unmasked; hidden `display:none` password ignored; cross-origin iframe (`oopif_frames > 0`) not scannable [UNVERIFIED]: default `allow` with the count in the stamp, `QUARRY_BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_OOPIF=mask` blanks every cross-origin iframe rectangle; the explicit `Screenshot` action returns `ErrorCode::SecurityBlocked` (403, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/error.rs` 49) with the same reason when withheld; `AgentAction::Pdf` is withheld when any classified field has a non-empty value (`typed_field_kind` plus the same scan).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Ownership: the module lives in `quarry-core` and applies at Quarry's capture boundary with no other plane's database; the Model Plane gets its own copy (`mp-scrub`) shared by duplication plus golden precisely so no code or table crosses planes; no Control, Data, Application or Frontend change (the SPA has no AX consumer; the gateway forwards an already-masked observation and model-gateway scrubs again). `[RISK]` until F-t2-050: a secret displayed on a page can still reach a scrape artifact and a Data Plane document through `quarry-transform`.
- ZDR: masking is independent of the ZDR flag (Live profile masks ZDR observations that are returned though nothing persists; Durable covers events, logs, errors always and receipts, artifacts, checkpoints when written); boundaries not covered here and owned elsewhere: Quarry telemetry spans (WS10 S8), the gateway `last_observation` cache (WS4/WS9), the owner live frame stream and OOPIF credential fields in screenshots (both marked limits), scrape artifacts (F-t2-050).
- Model proposes, Quarry executes: Quarry's masking never calls a model; the model never receives a typed secret back and its own typed value is masked in the durable record by Quarry; stop-criteria and `done` decisions read the raw observation in memory only (`grpc.rs` 1015-1042 scrubs persistence); withheld screenshots and the future executor-side fill extend the rule.

**Cross-session:** masked live frames for Space members: Quarry owns the mask primitive (S5 rectangle scan), the Space session (a) decides whether members get a masked stream (later slice, per-frame cost or an SPA overlay from stamp `rects`) or receipts only (recommended, X-19; S2 in the cross-session table); receipts shown to members are masked on read, no migration needed before sharing; golden `secret-shapes.v1.json` canonical in Quarry, vendored by the Model Plane (sibling (b) must not edit the copy; changes go through Quarry with a `RULE_VERSION` bump); `mp-scrub` crate and the three prompt/event call sites: this workstream proposes, sibling (b) merges (rebase on WS1 and WS10; `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs` has in-flight hunks); flip of `EXECUTION_CORE_REQUIRE_QUARRY_REDACTION_STAMP` to 1: sibling (b) after S2 is deployed (refuses agent runs against an old Quarry image); chat transcript persistence of a password the user tells the model in chat is outside Quarry's reach (product decision, flagged not solved); no per-Space secret store (custody ADR).

**Capability matrix (the contract of this feature):** only `ChromiumoxideDriver` (`scrape_actions` and `capture_options` flags `true`, set in `capabilities()` 1873-1889). Browserbase: registered, no `configure_egress_policy`, re-renders `{url: current_url}` per call so a post-action capture would be wrong; flags `false`. Browserless: not registered, same pattern; `false`. Kernel: not registered, stateful but fails at the egress step; `false` until F-t2-059 proves a governed boundary. A request with `actions` or capture formats served by a driver whose flags are false answers 501 `UNSUPPORTED` (`details.reason = "browser_capability_unavailable"`, `details.driver`) and never falls back to a static fetch that would silently drop the actions; `FallbackDriver` is bypassed by planning `DriverPlan::browser_fetch` with an empty chain (`driver_plan.rs` 34-47).

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:**
- Ownership: everything that executes in a page, captures, validates or stores is Ingestion Plane (Quarry); the Frontend plane owns only the same-origin gateway route and UI; no new database, no Control or Model Plane state, `plane-service-principals.json` deliberately not edited; artifacts are Quarry objects read by the gateway only through Quarry's HTTP surface with the user's org token.
- ZDR: artifacts non-ZDR only (through `zdr::guard` in `persist_captures` and the defensive guard in `ActionRuntime`); ZDR (including the floor from the user token's org posture) returns inline `data_base64` and writes nothing (no artifact, cache, event content, scrape record); any request with actions, a capture format or a viewport is not cache-admissible on either the Quarry page cache or the gateway preview cache; `write.text` never logged, echoed or placed in errors; meter metadata counts only; durable paths (`scrape_stream`, `internal_run_page`, crawl, batch, schedules) reject actions and capture formats; safe mode disables ingest, local index, visual-RAG renderer, source registration and the Model title hop; gateway responses `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, ZDR orgs get `withheld`; one honest limit: a ZDR screenshot over the 6 MiB inline cap is omitted (data lost, not privacy).
- Model proposes, Quarry executes: Quarry validates every field, caps counts, waits, bytes and viewport, refuses the denied actions and runs the list itself, no raw script ever runs; deviation stated: the card says "grant-gated" but `/v1/scrape` carries no BrowserBroker grant or run, so the gate is flag plus principal kind plus the new `scrape:interact` scope (granted to nobody); a Model-originated action list is closed until the ADR-6 ruling and a grant story from sibling (b) (F-t2-033 approval for form-submitting clicks): for service principals by the absent `scrape:interact` scope, and for a Model list relayed by the BFF under the user's bearer by the tighten-only `initiated_by:"agent"` label, which the gateway sets on every Model-originated request and the edge turns into 403 (test `agent_labelled_user_token_cannot_send_actions`); a principal-kind gate alone could not tell that relay from a human list.

**Cross-session:** Model-originated scrape actions: Model Plane would own the proposal, Quarry validation and execution (this plan); opening needs ADR-6 (ratified 2026-10-28), the X-20 `on` gates (a verified Model caller, D2-012, and an approval gate), a principal with `scrape:interact` in `plane-service-principals.json` (Control Plane registry PR) and an approval story (sibling (b)); Evaluate: WS2/F-t2-002 owns the deny, one vocabulary rule (this wire enum has no `evaluate`, Model Plane's `quarry_agent.rs` contract does, they must not merge); agent-path `screenshot`/`pdf` artifact ids (slice 7b, field `artifact_ids.pdf`): sibling (b) agrees the field; model-gateway `BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_MAX_BYTES` (6 MiB) deliberately equals the capture inline cap, model-gateway ignores scrape screenshots today; scrape artifacts shown inside a Space: this plan serves them org-bound, sibling (a) decides where they appear and per-user or per-Space visibility (D18 (b) plus the resource taxonomy, ADR-8) before the Space UI embeds them; shared files `KnowledgeScrapePreview.tsx`, `knowledge-client.ts`, `browser-session.ts`: sequence by file with sibling (a) and WS5 slice 7; capture metadata (`{format, bytes, width, height, tiles}`) is safe for traces (keep the `capture_meter_metadata` names); a Space browser session uses `/v1/agent/*` and the broker, never scrape `actions`.

Wire contract (the shapes all later slices call): request `crawl: {v:1, kind:"crawl|batch", depth, max_depth (0 = unlimited), seed_hosts[], scope:{allow_subdomains, allow_external_links, crawl_entire_domain, include_paths[], exclude_paths[], deny_extensions (null = built-in list), legacy}, scope_mode:"enforce|observe", robots:"respect|ignore"}`; response `crawl: {v:1, scope_applied, mode, links_seen, links_allowed, links_denied, denials:{counts{code:n}, samples[{url,code,message,remedy,depth}] (at most 3 per code, 20 per page), robots[{url,code,user_agent,path}] (at most 50 per page)}, hosts_added[], crawl_delay_ms}`. Flags: none (nothing sends `crawl` until S3). Rollback: revert.

Tests: unit in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/crawl_filter.rs`: same host, `www.` equivalence both ways, trailing dot, uppercase, IDN (`bücher.example` vs `xn--bcher-kva.example`), userinfo trick `http://example.com@evil.test/`, port, subdomain on/off, external on/off, depth boundary, `mailto:`/`javascript:`/`tel:`/`data:`, fragment-only, extension denylist, `crawl_entire_domain:false` directory prefix, include miss, exclude hit, exclude beats include, duplicate collapse, sample and robots caps, 6,000-link page, pattern caps with exact error paths, catastrophic pattern `re:(a+)+$` against a 10,000-character path completes in under 250 ms, over-size regex is a field error not a panic, `hosts_added` only at depth 0. Differential: proptest that `CrawlFrontier::enqueue` and `evaluate` agree on host and pattern decisions. Edge: `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/tests/crawl_scope_robots.rs` [NEW] (harness `support::base_state` with `internal_signer`, runtime token env, `FixtureSiteDriver`): scoped links and counts, `observe` returns all links plus counts, depth-0 redirect adds the host, no-`crawl` golden response recorded from the unmodified handler, malformed `crawl` is 400. Commands: `cd "apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2" && cargo test -p quarry-core crawl_ && cargo test -p quarry-runtime crawl_filter crawl_frontier && cargo test -p quarry-edge --test crawl_scope_robots && cargo test --workspace` (CI `quarry-v2-ci.yml` 204-205; run in the `rust:1` container, the crates do not build on the Windows host). Definition of done: green; 5,000 links with 100 patterns under 250 ms in a debug build; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; golden test proves no change without `crawl`. Deployment evidence: rebuild the edge image (`make up`), overlay up; compute `X-Quarry-Run-Sig = hex(HMAC-SHA256(QUARRY_INTERNAL_SECRET, org_id + "\n" + url))` with `openssl`, call `POST /v1/internal/run_page` with the runtime bearer for `http://fixture-a.crawl.test/` and a `crawl` object (`scope_mode:"enforce"`, `robots:"respect"`, default scope); `jq` assertions: `.links` has exactly the fixture-a internal pages (no `fixture-b`, `docs.fixture-a`, `mailto:`, `.png`), `.crawl.denials.counts.external_host_disabled == 1`, `.crawl.denials.counts.out_of_scope == 1`, `.crawl.scope_applied == true`; the same call without `crawl` returns all links. Risks: link-dense CPU (capped and measured); `normalize_url` drops fragments and sets an empty path to `/` (only when `crawl` is present, documented); `rel` and link text unused (honouring `rel=nofollow` is a non-goal).

**Slice WS14.S4 detail: robots gate, guarded fetch, RFC 9309 semantics, `Crawl-delay` into the scheduler.** Goal: crawl and batch pages are checked against robots.txt at fetch time through the guarded driver chain, discovery filters against warm cache, `Crawl-delay` slows the existing scheduler, `/v1/map` shares the gate. Placement: authoritative at fetch time inside `PageRunner::run_inner` after `security.preflight` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs` [C] 305-321) and before DNS resolution and the scheduler slot (327-348), so a policy denial never reaches `record_bad` (the scheduler maps unknown error codes to `BadKind::Server`, pipeline.rs 371-377, and would halve the host's concurrency); at discovery time only against cached rules (`RobotsGate::peek`, never a network call).

Request table (D8): `url` required; `max_pages` (alias `limit`) default from WS6.A limits, `0` is treated as absent and takes that default in `lenient` mode and is a 400 `invalid_option` in `strict` mode (the WS6.A W1 semantics are kept until then); `max_depth` (alias `max_discovery_depth`); `include_paths`/`exclude_paths` (D3 grammar); `allow_subdomains` false; `allow_external_links` false (UI-only, never Model-visible); `crawl_entire_domain` true (opposite of Firecrawl, documented); `sitemap` only `skip` accepted; `ignore_query_parameters` reserved; `ignore_robots_txt` policy-gated (403 `policy_denied`); `scrape_options` 400 until WS5 slice 4 and then refs only (inline content must never enter Temporal history); `ingest`, `zdr` unchanged (`zdr` still refused). The edge refuses `ignore_robots_txt` for any service principal as a second line. Flag: `QUARRY_EDGE__CRAWL_REQUEST_VALIDATION=lenient|strict` (default `lenient`). Tests: Rust table-driven parsing (every field, alias, boundaries 100/101, 512/513, 8,192/8,193, reserved keys, `sitemap:"include"`, `scrape_options`, `ignore_robots_txt:true`, `crawl_request_zero_pages_is_default_in_lenient_and_400_in_strict`); end-to-end through the router with the orchestrator double (stamped params contain the full scope); gateway `model_surface_drops_external_and_robots_keys`, `ui_surface_forwards_scope_fields`, `crawl_site_action_goes_through_the_ssrf_normalizer`, `max_pages_is_clamped_on_the_action_path`; FE vitest for options and the schema guard. Commands: `cargo test -p quarry-edge crawl_request`; `cargo test --manifest-path apps/gateway/Cargo.toml --all-targets`; `cd "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3" && pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint`. Definition of done: a Model-proposed crawl cannot carry an external-links or robots key by any path; patterns are capped identically at gateway and edge (one shared constant table in `CRAWL_SCOPE_ROBOTS.md` and a test in each tree); OpenAPI and `CRAWL_SCOPE_ROBOTS.md` list every field. Deployment evidence (rebuilt edge, orchestrator, gateway, SPA; each asserted against fixture logs and job events): (a) `include_paths:["/docs/*"]` fetches only `/` and `/docs/a`; (b) `exclude_paths:["re:^/blog/"]` skips `/blog/b` with `exclude_pattern_hit` counted; (c) `include_paths:["re:(a+)+$"]` accepted and completes in normal time; (d) 101 patterns returns 400 `fields[100]`; (e) `ignore_robots_txt:true` returns 403 `policy_denied`; (f) `sitemap:"include"` returns 400 `unsupported_option`; (g) the `knowledge.crawl_site` action with `{url, allowExternalLinks:true, ignoreRobots:true}` yields job params containing neither key and fixture-b receives zero requests; (h) the SPA options produce the expected params. Risks: strict validation breaks clients sending stray keys (lenient first, warnings echoed); gateway/edge cap drift; overlap with F-t2-055 on `map_routes.rs` and WS5 on request types.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** (1) Ownership holds: scope, robots, denials, `Crawl-delay` and the batch check are Ingestion Plane; the override entitlement, ceiling, claim and audit sink are Control Plane (WS7, audit-core, one credential PR); no database crosses planes, denied URLs are never fetched so never ingested, no BrowserBroker grant is involved. (2) ZDR: crawl and batch stay refused before any new field is parsed (`refuse_durable_job_under_zdr` runs first, a test pins it; WS4 S-8 later adds `details.zdr_refusal` without changing status or text); the robots cache holds only public robots.txt keyed by origin, in memory, bypassed (`check_uncached`) for ZDR `/v1/map` callers, no robots log or metric carries a URL or host (counters `crawl_links_denied_total{code}`, `robots_decision_total{decision}`, `robots_would_deny_total`). (3) Model proposes, Quarry rejects: the Model-visible schema has no external-links or robots key, the gateway `Surface::Model` drops them, the edge refuses `ignore_robots_txt` for service principals and callers without the policy ability, and the 403 `details.denial.remedy` never suggests the override to the Model. Risk flagged, not solved here: `knowledge.crawl_site` has `requiresApproval:false`; approval belongs to sibling (b) (F-t2-033, F-t2-042).

**Cross-session:** Verevon Space: a Space restriction such as `crawl.external_links` enters only through WS7's tighten-only `RequestAsk` (propose catalogue v1.1, default allowed); no Space id is added to job params (owner stays org plus `params.user_id`); crawl telemetry is content-free counters; progress reaches a Space panel through the Application Plane projection, not quarry-control. Sibling (b): Model-visible crawl schema is the registry allowlist (`maxPages`, `maxDepth`, `includePaths`, `excludePaths`, `allowSubdomains`) and F-t2-042 must reuse `Surface::Model`; approval before a Model-proposed crawl is (b)'s call; `RobotsGate::check` is the API a future `validate_navigation` can call (agent navigation not exempt; human pane navigation exempt per OQ-11, default); no service principal may gain `crawl:write`. Proposed owners: WS14 owns the contract and code; the registry file `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/action-registry.ts` is the cross-session contract.

**State of the code (verified 2026-10-15, live tree):**
- The edge exposes only `POST /v1/crawl`, `POST /v1/batch` (handoff), a per-kind list `GET /v1/:kind/jobs` and `GET /v1/jobs/:id/events` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs` [M] 133-134, 192, 231-234; schedule routes 254-276). `list_job_events` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/resource_routes.rs` [C] 1057-1130) drains control once (limit 500, clamp 1000), emits no `id:` field, ignores `Last-Event-ID`, and silently truncates a crawl with more than 500 events [INF].
- Control job record `Job{ID, OrgID, Kind, Status, Policy, Params, ScheduleID, CreatedAt, RunID, IdempotencyKey}` has no origin, desired state, workflow id or terminal reason; JSON is hand-rolled in `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/store/store.go` [C] 174-300). `PUT /v1/jobs/{id}` is unscoped and takes only `status`, `run_id`, `policy` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/resources/resources.go` [C] 513-549). Pause, resume, cancel signals and `state`/`progress` queries exist only in `CrawlJobWF` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-orchestrator/internal/workflows/signals.go` [C] 87-146); nothing sends them: control's Temporal client is nil (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/cmd/control/main.go` [C] 192, `resources.MountScheduleAliases(r, db, nil)`, `NoopClient` returns nil where its doc promises `ErrNotConfigured`, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/temporal/client.go` [C] 84-109), the orchestrator is the only Temporal client.
- [CLAIM-FALSE] "Durable jobs, crawl, batch and schedules are refused under ZDR": `refuse_durable_job_under_zdr` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/routes.rs` 563-588, spot-checked) is called only from `crawl_handoff` and `batch_handoff`; `create_schedule` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/schedule_routes.rs` [C] 239-340) has no ZDR reference. A ZDR org can create schedules and change monitors today.
- [CLAIM-FALSE, security finding fixed first in S1] `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/SCHEDULES.md` claims an org-scoped `GET /v1/schedules` and soft delete. Control's `listSchedulesHandler` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/resources/resources.go` 63-76, spot-checked: reads only `limit` and `cursor`, `s.List(limit, cursor)`) lists every org's schedules including each `target_ref` URL; `get`, `delete`, `enable`, `disable`, `pause`, `unpause`, `trigger`, `backfill` take only an id with no org check; delete is a hard `DELETE FROM schedules` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/store/pg/resources.go` [C] 796-805).
- [CLAIM-FALSE] "failure notices go through notification-core by API": notification-core rejects the legacy `x-internal-api-key` and requires HMAC v2 delegation (`apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/delegation/verifier.go` [C] 80-165) and a closed caller and type allow-list (`apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/http/handlers.go` [C] 154-173, 199-217); control's `notify.HTTPSink` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/notify/sink.go` [C]) therefore cannot deliver today, so the existing change-detected notification is dead [INF; confirm with one signed call].
- [DRIFT] `/errors` from `page_failed` plus `page_blocked` would omit the commonest real failures: after retries are exhausted a retryable failure is recorded as `page_retried` while the crawl counts `pagesFailed++` (`workflows.go` 464-469). A workflow killed by the 30-minute `WorkflowExecutionTimeout` (`dispatcher.go:254`) emits nothing and the job stays `running`; `waitWhilePaused` sleeps in 5 s timer steps (`signals.go` 30, 140-146) so pausing consumes the 30 minutes. `emitEvent` idempotency parts for `run_paused`/`run_resumed` are `(runID, type)` (`workflows.go` 437-449, 542-552), so a second pause of one run is dropped as a replay.

Route-collision risk: `GET /v1/crawl/:id` must not shadow the list route `GET /v1/crawl/jobs` (register static `/v1/crawl/jobs`, `/v1/batch/jobs`, `/v1/crawl/ongoing`, `/v1/batch/ongoing`).

API: `DELETE /v1/crawl/:id` returns `{data:{job_id, status, phase:"cancelling", control{desired:"cancel", pending:true}}}`; 404 foreign or missing; 409 `Conflict` `details{status, reason}`. Events: `control_requested {action, actor, actor_type}`, `run_paused`/`run_resumed` (unique per pause), `run_cancelled {pages_visited, pages_failed, forced?}`, `run_timed_out {timeout_type, limit_s}`. Flags: `QUARRY_EDGE__JOB_CONTROL=1` (edge verbs, 501 off), `QUARRY_JOB_CONTROL_LOOP=1` (orchestrator loop); order: control and orchestrator first, then edge; rollback: flags off, pending rows harmless; in-flight workflows replay via the two `GetVersion` ids. Tests: workflows `TestBatchJobWF_CancelSignalEndsBatchEarly`, `TestBatchJobWF_PauseThenResumeCompletesAll`, `TestBatchJobWF_PauseTwiceEmitsTwoDistinctEvents`, `TestCrawlJobWF_PauseUsesAwaitNotTimers`, `TestCrawlJobWF_OldHistoryKeepsSleepPolling` (`env.OnGetVersion("lifecycle-v1", ...)` returns `workflow.DefaultVersion`), `TestRunPage_RetryableFailureIsFinalErrorEvent`; jobs (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-orchestrator/internal/jobs/control_test.go` [NEW], `httptest` control plus `go.temporal.io/sdk/mocks.Client`): `TestApplyPending_SignalsAndAcks`, `TestApplyPending_NotFoundCountsAsApplied`, `TestEscalate_TerminatesAfterGrace`, `TestSweep_TimedOutBecomesTypedTerminal`, `TestSweep_RepeatedPassIsNoop`, `TestMarkRunning_ConflictTerminatesStartedWorkflow`, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-orchestrator/internal/timeouts/timeouts_test.go` [NEW] `TestExecutionTimeoutPerKind`; control `TestControl_CancelAcceptedJobIsImmediateAndDispatchCannotOverwrite`, `TestControl_TerminalIs409`, `TestControl_PauseWrongStateIs409`, `TestControl_CrossOrgIs404`, `TestPendingControl_ReturnsOnlyUnapplied`, `TestFinalize_IsIdempotent`, `TestControl_ScrapeNotControllable`; edge `cancel_is_org_checked_and_409_on_terminal`, `verbs_forward_actor_from_claims`, `service_token_cannot_control`, `zdr_caller_can_cancel_but_not_read_errors`. Commands: `cd ".../quarry-orchestrator" && go test ./internal/workflows/ ./internal/jobs/ -count=1`; control `go test ./internal/resources/ ./internal/store/... -count=1`; edge `cargo test -p quarry-edge --test job_lifecycle`. Definition of done: a running 5000-page crawl can be paused, resumed and cancelled via the API; cancel stops within one page plus the 2 s loop; a workflow killed by timeout ends `timed_out` with an event; a cancel that beats the dispatcher never runs; old in-flight workflows replay. Deployment evidence (rebuild all three images; slow local site, 1 s per page, 200 pages): (1) start a crawl, wait for `counts.completed >= 5`; (2) `POST /v1/crawl/{id}/pause`: within about 10 s `phase` is `paused`, the counter stops for 30 s, exactly one new `run_paused` event; (3) resume then pause again: a second distinct `run_paused`; (4) resume then `DELETE`: within a page and 2 s `cancelled` with `run_cancelled.pages_visited`; (5) `DELETE` again answers 409; (6) a 20-URL batch cancelled after 3 ends `cancelled`; (7) set `QUARRY_JOB_TIMEOUT_CRAWL_S=20` in the last env file: after about 50 s the job is `timed_out` with `run_timed_out` (proves the sweep, the workflow emitted nothing); (8) `temporal workflow describe -w quarry-job-<id>` shows the matching closed state. Risks: Temporal non-determinism (two `GetVersion` ids and version tests); signal to a closed workflow (treated as applied, finalize sweep corrects); durable-frontier queue rows remain after cancel (no purge route, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/queue_routes.rs` 200-202; follow-up queue janitor, harmless because queue names are per run); the control HMAC is one shared secret between edge and orchestrator (pre-existing trust model).
