**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** (1) Ownership: job and schedule state stay Ingestion Plane (control is the record tier, the orchestrator the only Temporal client, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/temporal/client.go` deleted in S3); org posture is read over org-core HTTP with a service principal and entitlements through WS6.D's resolver, no database read; notification-core is reached by API with its owner's allow-list change; Model Plane is untouched (service tokens stay default-deny on every lifecycle route). Risk at the boundary: the posture read needs `org:retention:read:any` for a second holder (Control Plane decision; `observe` ships without it). (2) ZDR: creation refusal (observe, then WS4 S-8), fire-time posture re-check, a schedule of an org that later turns ZDR on pauses with `skipped_zdr`; for jobs that predate ZDR, counts and verbs stay available while `events`, `errors` URLs and `results` are refused for ZDR-floor callers; notifications are content-free; `schedule_requests` holds ids and times only and is covered by org erasure. Open leak flagged: the schedule reaper refuses to delete a Temporal schedule whose org has no remaining desired rows (`schedules.go` 188-194, fail closed), so Temporal schedule args (URLs) outlive a purged org; follow-up with WS4's tombstone work. (3) Model proposes, Quarry executes: `ingestions.*` actions run under the user's session, Quarry authorises and applies the state machine (409 on an illegal transition), `cancel_run` needs approval and is irreversible, a Model-proposed schedule is created disabled and waits for an approved enable (`ingestions.change_schedule_state` carries `requiresApproval: true` for unpause, trigger, backfill and delete; without that registry change the Model could unpause its own schedule through `ingestions.run_schedule_action`, which today has no approval).

**Cross-session:** Space: `origin.type/actor/ref` vocabulary is Quarry's (a user token's `origin.ref` is advisory and unverified; a verified Space id would need a gateway-signed claim that does not exist); who may pause or cancel a Space-started run is one function `authorize_control` (default org-wide, creator-only or role is a user ruling); status and `?follow=true` are the feeds Space should consume (metadata only, ZDR-safe); Space must not project `page_extracted` excerpts. Sibling (b): registry ids and approval flags live in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/action-registry.ts` (proposed owner the Frontend registry; Model Plane owns tool descriptors; F-t2-033 owns approval UX); budgets key on `origin.type = agent` and `x-verevon-run-id` is honoured on service tokens only; WS10 maps the new events through its allowlist; a service-token route to these verbs (F-t2-042) needs a new scope in `apps/Control Plane/config/plane-service-principals.json` and a `require_service_route_scope` entry; scheduled lane is acquisition-only (ADR-9) and a Model routine that starts Quarry browser runs on a cron breaks that ruling.

#### WS16. Structured extraction (`json`, `summary`, `question`, `highlights`) over a governed Model Plane lane  (Wave 2; owner: Ingestion Plane (quarry-runtime, quarry-edge) for the product, Model Plane model-gateway for the lane (accountable owner: sibling (b), per X-7 option O4 with O1 accountable), Control Plane registry co-signs; effort: L, 50 engineer-days (41 for slices S0 to S8, S9 is design-level and unscheduled); lane: L5 SCRAPE (Quarry halves S3 to S6), L8 PLANNER-MP (S1, S8), L9 CONTROL-PLANE (S2), L6 (S7))

Paths are written in full. Design D15. Slice ids are the design's own (`S0` to `S9`); memo ids WS16.A to WS16.J in the table.

**Resolves:** F-t2-019 (audit effort M, revised to L: the audit's "extend `ModelPlaneInvokeRequest` to the existing `/v1/invoke`, flip the grant, the Model Plane share is S" is wrong in four places, see state bullets). Supplies a shared lane to F-t2-030 phase 2 (monitor judge), F-t2-037 (OCR), F-t2-050 (PII hop), F-t2-062, F-t2-065 (each adds its own gateway route as a row to the golden-pinned `SERVICE_ROUTE_GRANTS` table and waits for the same grant ruling). **Depends on:** WS5.D (D5 slice 4: `ScrapeOptions`, custom `ScrapeFormat` deserializer, `run_with_inline`, `ScrapeResponse`, `FieldError`) before S6; WS5 slice 7 (inline `scrape_with_options` in model-gateway) for S8; S1 before S3 (the golden the fake reads); S3 before S4 before S5 before S6; S2 before S6 tier E2; S7 after S6; S9 after WS5 Epic E1 (`WS5.I`), WS15.D, WS6.A, WS6.D. **Gated by:** X-7 (DR-15.1, the Quarry-to-Model-Plane lane: grant shape G1, owner O4 with the Model Plane gateway owner accountable; OQ-14) for S2 and every production use of the Quarry path; an ADR-4 amendment (a new ruling, not just the E2 proof) for `AI_FORMATS_ZDR=allow`; X-3 (commit the in-flight `http_routes.rs`, `grpc.rs`, `zdr_posture.rs`, `zdr_features.rs`, `model_plane_gate.rs` hunks first); D15 questions 2 (pricing, gates `USAGE_LLM_METRICS=on`) and 4 (org safety policy and redaction ordering with F-t2-050, gates production enablement). S0, S1 (needs an owner slot), S3, S4, S5, S7 and S8 behind its flag proceed without a ruling; S6 ships dark behind `QUARRY_EDGE__AI_FORMATS=0`.

API: `POST /v1/scrape {"url", "formats":["markdown", {"type":"json","schema":{...},"prompt":"prices in NOK"}, {"type":"highlights","query":"delivery","max_highlights":3}]}` returns 200 `{"data":{"markdown", "json", "highlights":[{"text","start","end"}], "ai":{"json":{"status","model","schema_valid","repair","prefilled","truncated_input","usage":{input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd}}, "highlights":{"status","dropped","untrusted_source"}}}, "meta", "error":null}`. Partial failure keeps 200 (`"ai":{"json":{"status":"error","code":"ZDR_UNAVAILABLE","details":{"reason":"zdr_unavailable"}}}`); field error is 400 `details.fields[]` with `schema_ref_not_supported` and similar so a Model that proposed a bad schema can retry; a service principal without `extract:ai` gets 403 `FORBIDDEN` with `details.field:"formats[i]"`; D5's `unsupported_format` `supported` list is now dynamic. Budgets (`AiBudget`): `max_input_chars` 60,000 (ceiling 80,000), `max_output_tokens` json 2048, summary 1024, question 512, highlights 1024 (ceiling 8192), `max_calls` 8, `max_total_tokens` 200,000, `max_cost_usd` only when the gateway returns `cost_usd`; on exhaustion remaining pages return `ai.<fmt>.status:"skipped", code:"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED"` with WS6's `dimension` (`llm_tokens`, `llm_calls`, `llm_cost`) and the request still returns its pages; `402 BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` only when spent before the first call; concurrency 4 per request, 16 per edge process. Metering: one `quarry.extract.llm` event per successful format, closed attributes (`kind`, `repair`, `zdr`, token counts, no content), id `quarry:<request_id>:<url_hash16>:<kind>`, content-free under ZDR; Quarry keeps guards, not a ledger (matrix rule 16); the ledger of record is cost-core fed by the gateway (S1); under ZDR the Model Plane records nothing, so ZDR spend is visible only as Quarry's content-free counters. Flags: `QUARRY_EDGE__AI_FORMATS` (exists, default 0), `QUARRY_EDGE__AI_FORMATS_ZDR=refuse|allow` (default `refuse`; stays `refuse` until the owner records an ADR-4 amendment that allows ZDR extraction, because ADR-4 as published says refuse AI formats under ZDR behind a flag; the E2 ZDR proof is a precondition of that amendment, not a switch; review K3-13; today `ai_formats.rs:306` `let _ = zdr;` makes the current ZDR handling a no-op, so the proof is about the lane, not the policy), `..._HARVEST`, `..._REPAIR` (default 1), `..._MODEL_JSON`, `..._MODEL_JSON_COMPLEX`, `..._MODEL_TEXT`, `..._MAX_INPUT_CHARS`, `..._MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, `..._MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS`, `..._CONCURRENCY`, `QUARRY_EDGE__USAGE_LLM_METRICS=off|shadow|on` (default off; same tri-state and anchor pattern as WS6.C's `USAGE_BROWSER_METRICS` but a separate switch). Rollout: land dark; enable on a dev stack at E1 (dev bypass, real gateway, no grant: proves the engine only); enable on the shared stack after S2 is live; flip ZDR to `allow` only after the E2 ZDR proof and a recorded ADR-4 amendment. Rollback: `QUARRY_EDGE_AI_FORMATS=0` (formats answer `unsupported_format`, `/v1/extract` with `schema` answers 501 as today). Migrations: none.

A page whose AI hop is skipped still crawls and says so. Not started until preconditions land.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** (1) Ownership: Control Plane owns the grant (registry file and specs only; Auth Core audits every mint with `model_service_token_issued`); Quarry owns the format contract, harvest, verbatim verification and budgets (matrix rows 61-62: Quarry does "bridge/output validation", the Model Plane owns inference, provider routing, model choice and cost; prompt templates live in Quarry and are flagged to the Model Plane owner); no Quarry second cost ledger (rule 16, cost-core fed by the gateway); Data Plane untouched; no cross-plane database access. Rules at risk: ownership split of prompt templates (confirm with the Model Plane owner), G1 gives `quarry-edge` `inference:invoke` on `inference-core` (bypass of the gateway if the network allows: mitigated by `tenant` binding, network policy [verify in compose], rate class, retrieval-engine precedent), org `injection_defense` and required PII redaction do not apply on `ai_chat` (until F-t2-050 or a gateway change), a directory-bound principal can mint for any real org. (2) ZDR per boundary: token `tenant` (60 s, no body field accepted by Auth Core); request `zdr:true` whenever `claims.effective_zdr_mode(req.zdr)` and typed 412 honoured (`ModelHopError::ZdrRefused`, never a silent non-ZDR fallback); gateway side `ai_chat` is non-persisting with no envelope and the inference-core cache skips ZDR (`cache.rs` 105); Quarry writes no artifact, scrape record, page-cache entry, extraction cache, event content or log of schema, prompt, page or output; no cost-core row for ZDR turns by Model Plane doctrine; crawl, batch and schedules stay refused so S9 never sees ZDR; `AI_FORMATS_ZDR=refuse` is the shipped default and stays so until an ADR-4 amendment is recorded (the E2 ZDR proof is a precondition of it). (3) Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects: the Model may propose a schema, question or prompt, Quarry validates every field (limits, `$ref` policy, scopes) and rejects with field-level 400s; a format reaches no browser action, script, header, proxy or URL; a service principal cannot request an AI format without `extract:ai` (default deny, so a Model-driven `fetch_url` cannot spend model money outside the run's budget); in the interim route the Model proposes, model-gateway runs the inference step it owns and Quarry only fetches.

**Cross-session:** Space: ZDR-safe telemetry rule (names, kinds, counts, tokens; never schema, prompt, page, output, URL) and the content-free `quarry.extract.llm` attributes are reused by any Space extraction telemetry (owner WS4 for the rule, this plan for the call sites); extraction in Space chat goes through the S8 tool inside the Model Plane run until the Quarry path is live and never takes a Space-scoped Quarry token; results are returned inline and persisted nowhere (sharing needs the resource-taxonomy ADR); product copy for `ZDR_UNAVAILABLE` and `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` goes in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/i18n/errors.ts` [M]. Sibling (b): the service lane of model-gateway (`/v1/ai/chat`, `SERVICE_ROUTE_GRANTS` and its golden, service rate bucket, metering) is proposed to be owned by sibling (b), who also owns S8 and who accepts rows from F-t2-037 and F-t2-050; any service calling `ai_chat` must present `x-inference-authorization` (document it); approvals do not gate extraction (cost is bounded by budgets); run budgets see interim-route spend inside the run but not Quarry-side AI-format spend (attributed to the service), which is why `extract:ai` is default-deny. User must reconcile: owner slot for DR-15.1 (O1/O4), who commits the in-flight `http_routes.rs`, `grpc.rs`, `zdr_posture.rs`, `zdr_features.rs` hunks before S1 and S8 edit the same functions, whether the route table row should name `service:quarry-edge` (tightening; today any service holding `models:invoke` passes), whether a content-free ZDR usage envelope is wanted.

Contract: `GET /v1/profiles/:id` returns `{data:{profile_id, name, scope, saved_at, rev, snapshot_version, cookies:[{name, domain, path, secure, http_only, same_site, session, expires, value_len, value:null}], origins:[{origin, local_keys, session_keys, idb_databases}], locale, timezone, has_user_agent, has_viewport, truncated}}`: structure without any secret or storage value (breaking for raw readers; only tests and the runbook read raw values). New refusals: 403 for service principals and ZDR callers, 413 on import over cap. No raw read route exists at all; a "show my cookies" feature is a separate audited DSAR export. Flags: ZDR enforcement behind `QUARRY_EDGE__ZDR_REFUSE_DURABLE_RESOURCES` (observe first); service-principal refusal and redaction ship on (security fix, no live caller). Rollback: revert, or the flag. Tests: unit `service_principal_is_refused_for_every_op`, `zdr_user_is_refused_except_list_and_delete_when_flag_on`, `zdr_flag_off_only_logs`, `import_requires_scope`, `redact_never_emits_a_cookie_value`, `restorable_is_false_when_all_cookies_expired`; integration (`profile_guard.rs`) `get_profile_returns_value_null_and_value_len`, `canary_cookie_value_never_appears_in_any_profile_response`, `service_token_gets_403_on_all_profile_routes`, `zdr_org_user_cannot_create_or_probe_but_can_delete`, `import_over_cap_is_413`; must stay green: `zdr_claim_floor.rs::a_zdr_org_users_agent_run_cannot_take_a_persistent_profile`, `zdr_behavior.rs` (4 tests at 67, 95, 132, 179). Commands: `cargo test -p quarry-edge --test profile_roundtrip --test zdr_behavior --test profile_guard`; `cargo test --manifest-path apps/gateway/Cargo.toml --all-targets` from `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3` for the list-shape fix. Definition of done: no `/v1/profiles` response contains a cookie value; service tokens cannot reach the routes; ZDR-org users are refused on durable operations with the flag on; the gateway list shows real profiles. Deployment evidence (rebuild the `quarry-edge` image and the gateway image): (1) with a standard-org user token create a profile via `POST /v1/profiles/create`, run a persistent agent run that sets a cookie whose value is the canary `CANARY-d16-p0`, close it; `curl -s .../v1/profiles/<id> | grep -c CANARY-d16-p0` returns 0 and the body shows `"value":null,"value_len":<n>`; (2) `docker logs quarry-edge 2>&1 | grep -c CANARY-d16-p0` returns 0; (3) the execution-core service token gets 403; (4) with the flag on a ZDR-org user token (org ZDR through org-core, claim stamped by auth-core) gets 403 on `POST /v1/profiles/create` and 200/204 on `DELETE`; (5) `GET /api/ingestions/profiles` through the gateway lists the profile (before the fix it returns an empty list). Risks: redaction breaks any undiscovered raw reader (grep of three repos done; announce in the changelog); ZDR enforcement could surprise a ZDR customer with legacy profiles (observe-first, delete stays open).

Output: a result table appended to C1 before C1 starts (or the test's doc comment); C1 picks "frame-less CDP" or "journal/flush". Risk: Chromium unavailable in CI (WS3.B provides the live lane first). Effort S, 1.5 d, no deployment evidence.

**Slice WS17.E1 detail: envelope layer below the cache, blob-store split, interim `env` key provider (migration 0016).** Goal: Postgres rows and Redis values hold ciphertext, without waiting for the Control Plane. Design: `EnvelopeProfileStore` (implements `ProfileStore`, owns codec and key provider) over `CachedBlobStore` (Redis, opaque envelope bytes) over `PostgresProfileBlobStore`; cache semantics change from write-through to cache-aside with invalidate-on-write; new key prefix `quarry:profile:v2:{org}:{profile}` (the one-off backfill also `UNLINK`s old `quarry:profile:{org}:*` keys); cipher `ring::aead::AES_256_GCM` (`LessSafeKey::seal_in_place_append_tag`, `ring` 0.17.14 already in the lock file through rustls, no new crypto crate), one 96-bit random nonce per seal from `ring::rand::SystemRandom`, one DEK per profile rotated every 256th save (`rev % 256 == 0`) and when none exists (random-nonce collision bound irrelevant by construction), gzip (`flate2`) above 4 KiB; envelope JSON `{"enc_v":1,"alg":"A256GCM","key_id":"env:v1"|"oc:3","wrapped_dek":"<b64>","snapshot_id":"snap_<ulid>","z":"gzip|none","nonce":"<b64 12B>","ct":"<b64>"}` with the AAD not stored but rebuilt as `"quarry-profile\0v1\0" || len32(org_id) || org_id || len32(profile_id) || profile_id || len32(snapshot_id) || snapshot_id || enc_v` (binds ciphertext to org and profile; `key_id` and `wrapped_dek` outside the AAD so a KEK rotation can rewrap the header); DEKs in `zeroize::Zeroizing<[u8;32]>`, never logged.

Flags: `QUARRY_EDGE__PROFILE_ENCRYPTION=off|compat|on` (`off`: today's plaintext; `compat`: read envelope or plaintext, write plaintext, safe for a mixed fleet; `on`: read both, write envelope only, plaintext column nulled, lazy re-seal), `QUARRY_EDGE__PROFILE_ENCRYPTION_REQUIRED=1` (boot refuses anything below `on`, set in the production overlay after backfill), `QUARRY_EDGE__PROFILE_KEY_PROVIDER=env|org_core`. Rollout: ship code with `off`, then `compat`, then `on` after all pods run the new code, then `REQUIRED` after E3's backfill reports zero plaintext rows, one step per release or fully rolled-out deploy. Rollback from `on`: set `compat` (envelope rows stay readable by new pods; old pods cannot read NULL-plaintext rows, which is why `on` waits for a fully new fleet). Tests: unit `seal_open_roundtrip`, `tampered_ciphertext_fails`, `aad_binds_org_profile_and_snapshot`, `nonces_are_unique_across_10000_seals`, `empty_and_max_size_snapshots`, `gzip_threshold`, `aad_is_length_prefixed_not_separator_ambiguous` (org `a|b` vs `a`,`b|`), `known_answer_vector` (fixed key and nonce, pinned ciphertext); `env_provider_wrap_unwrap`, `unwrap_with_wrong_org_fails`, `key_cache_ttl_and_org_eviction`; store `plaintext_row_is_resealed_lazily_with_cas`, `compat_mode_writes_plaintext`, `on_mode_nulls_plaintext`, `cache_holds_envelope_bytes_and_never_cookie_values` (Redis-gated: canary absent, JSON parses as `EnvelopeV1`), `key_unavailable_is_not_start_fresh` (provider errors: load returns `RuntimeNotReady`, row unchanged), `old_plaintext_cache_keys_are_ignored`; all `postgres_profile_store` and `cached_profile_store` tests ported and green. Commands: `cargo test -p quarry-runtime profile`; the Postgres lane; Redis lane (`REDIS_URL=redis://... cargo test -p quarry-runtime cached_profile_store`); `cargo audit --deny warnings --ignore ...` as CI. Definition of done: with `on`, no cookie value is readable in `quarry_profiles` or Redis; restore still works; boot refuses weak configuration in production. Deployment evidence (rebuild the edge image with `--features postgres-queue,browser-agent`, set `QUARRY_EDGE__PROFILE_ENCRYPTION=on` and a generated master key, recreate `quarry-edge`): (1) a persistent run against `https://httpbin.org/response-headers?Set-Cookie=quarry_e2e%3DCANARY-d16-e1%3B%20Max-Age%3D86400%3B%20Path%3D%2F`, closed; (2) `docker exec ingestion-postgres psql -U ingestion_user -d quarry_edge -At -c "select enc_v, key_id, snapshot is null, length(envelope) from quarry_profiles where profile_id='<id>'"` returns `1|env:v1|t|<n>` and `psql -At -c "select encode(envelope,'escape') from quarry_profiles" | grep -c CANARY-d16-e1` returns 0; (3) Dragonfly keys under `quarry:profile:v2:<org>:*` exist (`redis-cli -a $INGESTION_DRAGONFLY_PASSWORD -n 6 --scan --pattern 'quarry:profile:v2:*'`) and `GET <key> | grep -c CANARY-d16-e1` returns 0; (4) a second run on the same profile navigating to `https://httpbin.org/cookies` shows `quarry_e2e` (restore through decrypt; pass criterion: restore latency p95 under 1.5x the pre-slice p95 measured the same way on the same profile, over at least 20 restores; review K3-18); (5) a throwaway edge with a wrong `QUARRY_PROFILE_MASTER_KEYS`: run start returns 503 `details.reason="profile_key_unavailable"` and `select rev from quarry_profiles` is unchanged. Risks: new cryptographic code (mitigated by `ring`, per-profile DEK with at most 256 messages, a known-answer test, and an external review of `profile_crypto.rs` and `envelope_profile_store.rs` before `REQUIRED` goes on in production, review not in the 8 days); the trait split touches every `ProfileStore` implementer (keep `ProfileStore` signatures stable after P1); master-key loss (E2 section); restore latency measured in evidence step 4.

**Slice WS17.P2 detail: owner and ACL enforcement (builds on P1's `owner_user_id`).** Goal: `user_private` means owner only, at every `/v1/profiles*` route and at run attach. Model (D16-7): `owner_user_id` set only on INSERT, value `Claims::actor_id()` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/auth.rs` [C] 144-146); `user_private`: only the owner may list, attach, probe, rename, rescope or delete; `org_shared`: any org member may list, attach and probe, only the owner may rename, rescope or delete; `run_scoped`: owner only; non-owners get 404 (list filtered), not 403, to avoid an existence oracle; service principals never use `/v1/profiles*`; a Space must never widen the ACL (a future Space-shared profile is an explicit Quarry-side ACL row written by the owner through a gateway action, never a header or a Space-service call). Legacy rows (owner NULL) follow the precedent of `0008_step_receipt_actor_scope.sql`: `user_private` legacy rows fail closed (hidden, not deleted), `org_shared` legacy rows stay org-visible; rescue is an operator SQL runbook (`UPDATE quarry_profiles SET owner_user_id = ..`).

**Slice WS17.C1 detail: complete snapshot capture in quarry-browser (Track B).** Goal: capture the whole context jar with expiry and SameSite, web storage and IndexedDB for every visited origin, bounded and ordered, behind a flag. Strategy (D16-12, final choice after S0): cookies by `Storage.getCookies { browserContextId }` through `Browser::execute` for the session's own context (whole jar, with `expires`, `session`, SameSite, partition key; works even with no tab open); web storage and IndexedDB by an origin journal: visited origins tracked per session (`visited_origins: BTreeSet<String>`, cap 64, http/https only); at capture every LIVE tab runs the in-page serializer; origins no longer live use records flushed while alive through `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` installing a `pagehide` handler that calls a `Runtime.addBinding` function (`__quarryProfileFlush`) with a capped JSON payload (or the frame-less `IndexedDB` CDP domain if S0 says it works); cookies first so an IndexedDB timeout never loses authentication; budget 10 s (cookies 2 s, storage 4 s, IndexedDB 4 s), partial results flagged `truncated`; empty-capture guard (no cookies and no origins while the loaded snapshot had some: skip the save and emit `profile_capture_empty_skipped`).

**Slice WS17.E2 detail: Control Plane key API in org-core and the `org_core` key provider (org-core migration 024; gated by X-8).** Goal: per-org KEKs owned by the Control Plane, DEK wrap/unwrap/rewrap over an authenticated API, crypto-shredding by the existing org hard delete (`gdpr_hard_delete_organization`, `apps/Control Plane/org-core/migrations/003_gdpr_hard_delete.up.sql`; the FK cascade deletes the key rows; soft delete with its 30-day grace does NOT shred). Hierarchy: master key (env now, KMS later) to per-org KEK (wrapped at rest in org-core) to per-profile DEK (wrapped by the KEK, stored in the Quarry envelope); Quarry never holds a KEK. Org-core owns it behind an interface (`internal/orgkeys` with `MasterKeyProvider` and `Store`) so a later `key-core` extraction is mechanical; the ownership docs list no key responsibility today and must be updated, which makes this a user-ratified ownership decision.

Master-key loss destroys every profile of every org (and every wrapped KEK); mitigations are part of the slice: the key is generated once by the bootstrap and stored in the secrets ledger (`.env.generated-secrets`, the bootstrap guard refuses to regenerate), an offline two-person escrow runbook before production, the boot canary, and a restore drill (restore the org-core and Quarry databases from backup into a scratch stack, unwrap and decrypt one profile). Limits stated to counsel: a point-in-time restore of org-core older than an org's KEK creation orphans that org's profiles; shredding is effective once backups age out. The interim `env` provider (E1) cannot crypto-shred and may run in production only as an explicit, logged interim. Flags: `ORG_CORE_KEYS_ENABLED=0|1` (dark by default), `QUARRY_EDGE__PROFILE_KEY_PROVIDER=org_core`. Rollback: back to `env` only while no row is `oc:`-sealed; afterwards `org_core` must stay; disabling `ORG_CORE_KEYS_ENABLED` makes every `oc:` row unreadable (503) so it is an outage switch, not a rollback. Tests: org-core (Go) `generate_unwrap_roundtrip`, `unwrap_with_wrong_org_or_profile_context_fails`, `scopes_gate_each_route` (gateway credential gets 403), `destroy_makes_unwrap_410`, `hard_delete_cascades_key_rows` (Postgres, `TEST_DATABASE_URL`), `rotate_then_rewrap_keeps_dek`, `canary_failure_returns_503`, `no_dek_or_wrapped_dek_in_logs`, `migration_is_idempotent`, compose contract test; Quarry `org_core_provider_maps_statuses` (wiremock 503/410/403/200), `provider_never_logs_bodies`, `router_unwraps_env_and_oc_rows`. Commands: `cd "apps/Control Plane/org-core" && go test -v -p 1 ./...` (Postgres 16 container, `REQUIRE_CONTRACT=1`, `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, per `org-service.yml`); Quarry lanes as E1. Definition of done: `oc:`-sealed rows restore through org-core; destroying an org's KEK makes its profiles unreadable; org hard delete shreds automatically; custody and loss runbook exist and the restore drill ran. Deployment evidence (rebuild org-core with `bash scripts/run-control-plane.sh build org-core` then `up -d --no-deps org-core`, and the edge image): (1) with the quarry credential `curl -s -X POST http://org-core:8080/internal/orgs/<org>/keys/data-keys -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARRY_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN" -d '{"purpose":"quarry.profile","context":{"profile_id":"prof_x"}}'` returns 201 with `key_id":"oc:1"`, the gateway credential 403; (2) repeat the E1 persistent-run flow: `select key_id from quarry_profiles` returns `oc:1` and `psql -d org_core -c "select org_id, kek_version, state from org_key_encryption_keys"` shows one active row; (3) stop the org-core container: a restore returns 503 `profile_key_unavailable`, `rev` unchanged, and works again after start; (4) operator `DELETE /internal/orgs/<org>/keys`: the next run with that profile id restores no cookies and the edge logs `profile_key_destroyed`; (5) restore drill with `pg_dump` of both databases into a scratch stack, one profile decrypted; a wrong master key answers 503 from the canary. Risks: availability coupling (org-core down blocks restores and saves, content untouched, per-process DEK cache 300 s covers blips); a new Control Plane responsibility; credential drift between the Control Plane secrets file and the Ingestion mirror (evidence step 1 doubles as the check).

**Slice WS17.E3 detail: backfill, erasure hop, tombstone and cache purge, then plaintext removal (migration 0017).** Goal: no plaintext profile rows remain; org erasure reaches `quarry_profiles`, tombstones and Redis. Recommended erasure transport (D16-5 option A): quarry-control's existing durable consumer calls a new quarry-edge internal route (no second consumer on `control-shared-nats`, no cross-database delete).

**Slice WS17.S7 detail (optional, only if usage shows concurrent use): single-writer profile lease for shared profiles.** First acquirer is the writer, others restore read-only. Files if built: `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs` [C] attach path (Redis `SET quarry:profile-lock:{org}:{profile} <lease> NX PX <ttl>` renewed with the run; a second attach sets `persist_profile=false` effective and returns `profile_read_only: true`); `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs` needs no change (`persist_profile` already gates saves at 676). Tests: `second_attach_is_read_only`, `lock_expires_with_the_lease`. Evidence: two runs on one profile, only the first run's cookies persist. Effort S-M, 3 d.

**Plane ownership / ZDR / Model-proposes-Quarry-executes check:** (1) Ownership: profile data stays in the Ingestion Plane under Quarry's own database; the only Control Plane addition is key management in org-core (a new responsibility needing the ownership docs updated and user ratification, X-8); Quarry never reads a Control Plane table (HTTP with a registered credential); quarry-control reaches `quarry_edge` data only through an edge internal route; Data Plane never sees profile content; the Model Plane never sees cookie or storage values (service principals refused on all `/v1/profiles*`, the read route returns structure only, snapshots never enter observations, receipts or events; residual path `AgentAction::Evaluate` reading `document.cookie` is closed by WS2.A, and P0's canary test asserts a seeded value never appears in any `/v1/*` response or `docker logs`). (2) ZDR per boundary: run start refused (existing); `/v1/profiles*` refused for ZDR callers except list and delete (P0, observe-first, shared flag with WS4); Redis holds ciphertext only (v2 prefix, invalidate-on-write); Postgres rows sealed and ZDR callers cannot create rows; tombstones hold ids and a timestamp, deleted with the org, cannot exist for ZDR; the key API carries org id, purpose and profile id never content, DEK material never in logs or errors; restore and capture reports are counts only, no cookie names, domains or origins at INFO; no new spans. Rules at risk: ZDR on `/v1/profiles*` is observe-only until the flag is on, the interim `env` provider cannot crypto-shred, other `quarry_edge` tables are not erased on org erasure. (3) Model proposes, Quarry rejects: a Model-driven run may propose a `profile_id`; the P2 attach check rejects another user's profile inside Quarry; restore applies stored state to the session's own isolated context only and never navigates or widens egress.

**Cross-session:** Space: profile ownership and sharing is Quarry's (`quarry_profiles.owner_user_id` plus `scope`, enforced in `profile_guard`); a Space must never widen the ACL (a Space-shared profile would be an explicit owner-written ACL row `principal_kind`, `principal_id` read by Quarry, never a trusted `space_id`); agent browser inside a Space (WS8 shared-jar attach) uses the session's context not the profile, restore stays first-tab-of-context only, saves happen at release by the run owner; capture and restore reports are counts only and safe for Space activity feeds (origins and cookie names are not); to reconcile: whether Space members may use an `org_shared` profile (yes today) or need Space-scoped sharing first. Sibling (b): the owner check needs the user identity at run start, so WS1's delegated bearer must carry `user_id` for Model-driven runs (an autonomous service run owns its profile as `service:<id>` and should use `run_scoped`); BrowserBroker grants are unaffected (profiles are not grant material); execution-core and model-gateway must not call `/v1/profiles*` or forward a `profile_id` they did not receive from the user's request; the `browser_profile` feature key is an X-16 follow-up in the Model Plane catalogue; the `profile_restore` summary in the chat browser UI is WS9's. Frontend gateway: the profile list-shape fix (P0) is the one hunk, owned by the browser-UI workstream; `browser.rs` profile proxies need no change.

Source: `.plan-work/plan-parts/D-w4-w5-epics.md`; paths written in full, tags as in 3.3 (`[?]` would mean on disk but not listed by git, none used here). Each epic ends with a recommendation: **build**, **build after ADR**, **park** or **delete**. Reconciliation applied: the migrations for E4.2 and E4.6 follow R-4 and do not share a number (session-core 0046 WS10, 0047 WS11, `0048` E4.6 research runs; E4.2's store is a capability-core migration `0017_procedures`, with `0016` kept for WS7 outcome B, and a session-core `0049` only if the owner picks a session-core table; all `[provisional]`, allocated at merge by the migration arbiter); principal-registry rows (`map:read`, `cap.web.*` scopes) ride the R-13 Control Plane PRs; execution-core browser files have one editor (R-27); the event name is `agent.expired` (R-11).

**Verdict.** Wave 4 is not one wave. Three of its sixteen items are already inside Wave 1-2 designs (F-t2-054 in WS8, F-t2-060 step 1 in WS3, the OpenAPI half of F-t2-064 in WS5 slice 8), one (F-t2-053 part a) is WS15 slice S2, and six wait on an ADR or owner ruling. Wave 5 is polish plus parked bets; only F-t2-067 slice 1, 068 clear-data, 069 step 1, 071 slice a and 074 are worth scheduling before an ADR.

Two corrections the epics rely on. **[CLAIM partly false] F-t2-052 premise:** the only per-page data stored today is `PageExtraction` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/output.rs:81-104` [C]: url, title, 300-char excerpt, word_count, lang, driver), with no artifact id and no structured fields, so a result set built from `page_extracted` events is a page index, not a dataset; a real dataset needs crawl and batch to embed scrape options with the `json` format (WS5 Epic E1 plus WS16). - **Items / owner / effort.** F-t2-052, F-t2-053. Ingestion (quarry-edge Rust routes, quarry-control Go sources and schedules), Frontend (Ingestions page, gateway proxy). F-t2-052 M (about 11 days); F-t2-053 shrinks from L to M (about 6 days). Epic about 17 days.

- **Scope.** (1) `run_id` on `ArtifactSummary` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/resources.rs:83-97` [C]) and a `run_id` filter on `list_artifacts` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/resource_routes.rs` [C], route `routes.rs:178` [M]). (2) `GET /v1/runs/{id}/items` (alias under `/v1/jobs`) in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/run_items_routes.rs` [NEW], reading `page_extracted` events through WS15's `jobResults` method (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/resources/jobs_lifecycle.go` [NEW], `ForJobTypes(['page_extracted'], after_seq, 100)`), joined to artifact refs, streamed `csv` and `jsonl`, field projection, D14b's 100-item and 10 MiB cap; rows gain a `json` column once crawl embeds the format. (3) Gateway proxy `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/ingestions/runs.rs` [C], action contract in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/action-registry.ts` [C] first, then a table view with an explicit "Ingest selected" in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/ingestions/components/VerevonIngestionsPage.tsx` [C]. (4) A saved definition is a `Source` (`resources.rs:27-43` [C], free-form JSONB `config`) with a typed, versioned options object validated by the D5/D14a validators; schedules point at it through `target_ref`. (5) `GET /v1/presets` is control-only (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/cmd/control/main.go:174` [C]); do not proxy it until D7's `JobPolicy` and the `robots.max_mode` ceiling enforce it, because the `fast` preset sets `RobotsIgnore` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/resources/presets.go:60-75` [C]); otherwise delete the Go presets and rename the overloaded word to "saved job".

#### E4.2 Procedure store and run-as-procedure

- **Items / owner / effort.** F-t2-051. Ingestion (postconditions, canonicalisation), Model Plane (store in capability-core, runner in execution-core), Frontend via WS9 slice 4c. XL, about 30 days (postconditions 6, canonicalisation 6, store and runner 18).
- **Dependencies.** WS1 (replay needs a run grant); WS6 (budgets per replay); WS11 (the runner is a planner mode); WS3 S10 (trusted input so outcomes verify); WS12 (typed-text redaction). ADR 6 (stored actions are declarative) and ADR 3 adjacent; needs a ledger entry for the store owner.
- **Scope.** Keep the shipped compiler (`compile_procedure`, `compare_replay`, `assess_quality`, `analyze_impact`: `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/browser_procedure.rs:61, 114, 153, 188` [C]) behind `POST /v1/agent/runs/{id}/procedure` (`compile_run_procedure`, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs` near 2466 [C]); version is hard-coded to 1 and the compiler rejects any receipt not `Verified` (`browser_procedure.rs:85-96`). Step 1, postconditions: `outcome_for_action` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/observation.rs:217-266` [C]) returns `Unknown("postcondition_required")` for click, type, press, scroll, select, evaluate, back, forward; add an optional step-level `expect` (URL pattern, element present or absent by ref, text in a region) on the action request in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/contracts.rs` [C]; the Model proposes, Quarry evaluates. Step 2, canonicalisation: map `snapshot_id`/`generation`/`ref_id` (`contracts.rs:650-654`) to `ClickSemantic`/`TypeSemantic` locators or an `ElementFingerprint`, fail closed with `TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED` on ambiguity, typed text becomes a named slot bound at replay. Step 3: `apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/procedures` [NEW] with a capability-core migration (`0017_procedures` `[provisional]`; capability-core owns its migrations, applied by its `docker-entrypoint.sh`; `0016` stays reserved for WS7 outcome B; allocated at merge by the migration arbiter), immutable versioned builds with tags; the runner is a deterministic planner mode in `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs` and `quarry_agent.rs` [C] that proposes each stored step under a fresh grant, runs `compare_replay` first, and hands back to the planner or user on mismatch. Naming: call the artifact a "saved recipe" (WS11's `browser_agent/procedure.rs` [NEW] and `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_PROCEDURE` mean the prompt procedure `browse/1`); keep `BrowserProcedure` as the wire type.
- **First slice.** `expect` postconditions behind a flag, surfaced in receipts (M), or the store-owner ledger entry.
- **Risks.** Never reuse a stored sensitive approval; human-recorded receipts lose observations (D8 `HUMAN_RECEIPT_MODE=full` for recording only); stale recipes (`analyze_impact` quarantines).
- **ZDR check.** ZDR runs write no receipts and cannot be saved; the store holds actions and locators only; rollout state lives in Model Plane, Quarry still executes or rejects every step.
- **Recommendation: build after ADR-lite (store owner), staged.**

- **Items / owner / effort.** F-t2-058. Ingestion (edge, browser, runtime) with Control Plane (tier cap entitlement, metering). XL, about 30 days: emulation M 6, profile pinning and cache key M 6, tiers L 15, SessionPool parked.

Emulation: extend WS3 S2's `apply_page_hygiene` in `open_tab_page` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs` near 371-557 [C]) to set `Emulation.setLocaleOverride`, `setTimezoneOverride`, `setGeolocationOverride` and a UA plus `Accept-Language` override from a validated country table (none set today, `chromiumoxide.rs:1851-1860`). Profile pinning: route `profile_id` through `ProfileStore` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/session.rs` [C]) with D16's owner guard; a profile-bound scrape is personalised and bypasses the cache; every cached entry gains an org prefix (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/cache.rs:1-36` [C]; this is WS4.K). Tiers: `EgressBroker::plan` (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/egress_broker.rs:102-163` [C]) is a processor-gated pool rotating on 401/403/407/429/503; add `tier` (none, pool, country), org ceiling, one escalation after a strong challenge. The Chromium path has no upstream proxy chaining (`apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/browser_egress_proxy.rs:1-8` [C]; loopback-only `PinnedEgressProxyEndpoint`, `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:331-360` [C]), so design a pinned chain or sidecar before any browser tier ships.

- **Recommendation: build** slices a and b; **build after ADR 5 and ADR 10** for tiers; **park** SessionPool.

## 4. Sequencing and parallelism

This section is the operating manual for running 15 lanes at once without colliding. It condenses the sequencing memo (arch-B) and applies the architecture memo's reconciliation list (arch-A section 2, cited as R-n); where R-n changes a design or arch-B, the row says so in one clause.

Paths are written in full. Tags `[C]`/`[M]`/`[U]`/`[NEW]` come from `tools/provenance.sh` run on the live tree on 2026-10-15. Line ranges are the designs' live-tree ranges and drift as earlier slices land: re-read before editing. Slice letters are the catalogue ids (`WS3.D` is design D3's S3).

**Position 0 (process, before any lane merges): PRE-1, decision X-3.** About 324 uncommitted entries sit under the files nearly every slice edits, including 28 untracked golden and fixture files and 6 untracked gate files that `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` [M] and CI need, and session-core migrations `0044` and `0045` [U]. Commit or branch them as a baseline first. Until then every lane's append to a shared file conflicts and the gates pass only on the owner's machine. Only slices that touch no uncommitted hunk (WS4.A, WS3.B, WS3.E, WS2.E, WS1.A1; WS2.A and WS4.K with one hand-staged hunk each) may merge before position 0 completes; every slice that edits an [M] file (WS3.A, WS5.A, WS5.B, WS6.A, WS1.A0, WS1.A2, PRE-2) waits for it (X-3).

### 4.1 Lanes (worktrees) and what runs concurrently

A lane is a team's worktree and branch family. A lane never waits for another lane's PR to be written, only to be merged. Every one of the 166 slices belongs to exactly one lane. Labels: `(g)` gated by a named decision, `(opt)` optional, `(unsched)` design-level only and not in any total.

**Rules that bind every lane.**
- *Primary editor, not owner.* The third column names the lane that edits a file most; other lanes edit the same files only in the order of 4.2 (for example `step_receipts.rs`, `observation.rs` and `agent_routes/*` appear under L2, L3, L10 and L14, and `domains/browser.rs` is edited by WS1.B (L1) and WS2.C (L2) although L6 edits it most).
- *Test layout.* New Rust integration tests live in `crates/<crate>/tests/`, never in `src/tests/`: `cargo test -p <crate> --test <name>` resolves only `tests/<name>.rs` (or a `[[test]]` entry), and the shared harness is `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/tests/support/mod.rs` [M]. No `src/tests` directory exists in quarry-edge, quarry-runtime or quarry-browser.
- *`AppState` fields.* A new field names every full literal: four in `quarry-edge` and six in the gateway (listed in 4.2); other `quarry-edge` sites use struct update. Such PRs merge in the order of 4.2.

**What runs concurrently.**
- **Day 0 in W1:** L1 (WS1.A1, WS1.A0), L2 (WS2.A), L3 (WS3.A, B, E), L4 (WS4.A, B, K), L5 (WS5.A) and L7 (WS6.A) start together on hunk-disjoint code. Several of them edit the same [M] files, so hunks are staged by hand and merge in the per-file order above; the slices that edit an [M] file wait for position 0. W1 is sized for 6.5 engineers: L1 x2, L2, L3 x1.5, L4, L5.
- **W2 foundations during W1:** the file-disjoint foundation set (section 4.3 position 13) starts as soon as a lane is free; none needs a W1 merge except WS10.A (codemod), WS3.B (for WS17.A) and the shared `agent_routes` split.
- **Single editors:** one engineer owns the execution-core browser files and `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/browser_run.rs` (R-27); one owns `agent_routes.rs` through the split; one Control Plane owner makes both registry PRs (R-13); one editor at a time on the broker's `grant.go`, `server.go`, `authz.go`.
- **Second engineer needed:** L7 (crawl versus jobs), L8 (planner versus trace persistence), L3 (WS12.B/F, WS13.C/G, WS8.E share the driver with WS3), L5 (WS5 and WS13 versus WS16), L6 (SPA versus gateway halves).
- **Lanes that hand off:** at W1 close L4 and L2 engineers move to L10 and L12; at 12 engineers L13 and L14 share one person and L9 and L15 share one (section 4.4).

### 4.2 File-conflict matrix and required merge order per hot file

Shared rules for every row. Slices are listed in the order they must merge; "queue" means one serial merge queue and every later PR rebases. Generated files and goldens are regenerated on rebase, never hand-merged. A PR adds at most one `mod` line and one `AppState` field (there are four full `AppState {..}` literals in `quarry-edge` and six in the gateway, so a field without a shared builder breaks every test build; `quarry-edge`: `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/main.rs:1426`, `.../src/test_support.rs:96`, `.../tests/support/mod.rs:41` and `.../src/routes.rs:1301`, every other site uses struct update; gateway, under `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/`: `config.rs:146`, `main.rs:313`, `domains/browser.rs:4915`, `domains/chat/shared.rs:745`, `domains/orchestration.rs:632` and `onboarding/crawl_preview/stream_e2e.rs:110`; re-grep before use). Announced freezes: WS2.B two working days on `agent_routes.rs`, WS3.D one day on `chromiumoxide.rs`, WS10.A one day on every route file. **R-7 admission gate order inside `step` (one chain, one test).** 1 closed (404 `run_not_live`); 2 `resolve_caller` (owner or attach delegate); 3 control and takeover gate (cheap, local: `USER_TOOK_OVER`); 4 grant revalidation; 5 driver capabilities; 6 ephemeral tier; 7 raw-script deny; 8 web policy (WS7); 9 budget (WS6); 10 sensitive approval (the only gate that consumes state); 11 navigation domain; 12 navigation security. Principle: side-effect-free gates first, the consuming gate last, so a refusal never burns a single-use approval. WS2 owns the pin test `admission_order_is_pinned`; WS6's `enforce_budget` is step 9.

### 4.3 Whole-plan merge order (numbered, W1 then W2, with reasons) and critical path

Each position is a merge train. PRs inside a position may merge in any order unless the text says otherwise (they are hunk-disjoint or append-only; where two edit the same [M] file, the per-file table in 4.1 fixes the order). A position starts when its stated prerequisites are merged, not when the previous position finishes. W1 is positions 1 to 11 and W2 positions 12 to 27. Hot-file rules from 4.2 apply on top.

**W1 exit gate (after position 11).** Merged and deployed on the rebuilt local stack: PRE-1 and PRE-2; WS1.A0, WS1.A1, WS1.A2, WS1.B and WS1.C with `BROWSER_GRANT_ENFORCEMENT=strict` on the production-overlay stack (the real `docker-compose.yml` plus `docker-compose.production.yml`; the test-only contract overlay may set env and volumes only and never removes a production hardening key; WS3.A is a dependency of that L2 run, and the PR records `ps` on the same stack with zero `--no-sandbox` and a `navigate` step returning 200); WS2.A to WS2.E; WS3.A to WS3.F, WS3.H, WS3.J; WS4.A to WS4.G and WS4.K with the purge recorded; WS5.A to WS5.H, including WS5.C (moved from optional to gated: it is the X-14 Q1 gate for the production default `DOC_ROUTING=on`); WS6.A (crawl bounds, counted in the W1 total). Gated or optional items (WS4.H, WS4.I, WS4.J, WS3.I, WS3.G, WS2.F) may trail without blocking W2, except that WS4.A must be deployed before `VITE_BROWSER_OMNIBOX_SEARCH` is on in production.

**Critical path.** `WS1.A1 (10 d) -> WS1.B (10 d) -> WS8.F (12 d) -> WS8.H (6 d) -> WS8.I (7 d) -> WS8.J (5 d)` = 50 engineer-days, the shared browser. With D1's two-engineer split on WS1.A1/B it is 46 to 48; risk-adjusted 13 to 18 weeks. WS1.A2 (6 d) and WS1.A0 (1.5 d) are off the path because WS1.B depends on WS1.A1 only; the L2 legs B and C of WS1.B go green only with WS1.A2 merged, which needs X-1, so a late sign-off delays the evidence of WS1.B and not its code. WS2.A is not on the path: it is the entry condition of WS2.B, which the WS1.A2 Quarry validator stream waits for.

| Step | Start (eng-day) | Finish |
|---|---|---|
| WS1.A1 broker issues kind, zdr, TTL and cap-bound grants on the `Repository`; proto; model-gateway grant routes; L1 core (the prod-mode L2 harness is WS1.A2, off the path) | 0 | 10 |
| WS1.B `DeriveRunGrant`, model-gateway `POST/DELETE /v1/browser/grants`, gateway enforcement | 10 | 20 |
| WS8.F Quarry attach core: tab ledger, caller resolution, per-tab control | 20 | 32 |
| WS8.H execution lanes: human and agent actions run concurrently (GA gate) | 32 | 38 |

| WS8.J phase 3: deliverable and handoff marks, turn-scoped release, orphan sweep | 45 | 50 |

Other chains, all starting on day 0 in parallel: WS16.B to WS16.H 30 d; WS10.C to WS10.I 28 d; WS1.A1, WS1.B, WS7.K 26.5 d; WS5.A, WS5.B, WS5.D, WS13.E, WS13.F, WS13.I 26 d; WS14.C, WS14.D, WS14.E, WS14.I 18 d; WS15.B, WS15.E, WS15.I, WS15.J 17.5 d; WS17.C, WS17.D, WS17.I 17 d; WS15.B, WS6.H 9.5 d. Two chains end in a decision or epic, so the graph understates them: **planner default-on** (WS11.F stage 3) needs WS1.A1, WS1.A2, WS1.B, WS6.B, WS6.E, WS12.A to WS12.E, F-t2-044 Tier B and OD13; plan on engineer-day 31 at best, 37 to 43 realistically, plus the live-success floor. **Scheduled crawls** (WS15.J) are 17.5 d on the graph plus the one-week soak of WS15.I, about 22.5 d; WS14.I needs its own soak.

**Success criteria each exit closes** (the full table is in 1.2; a criterion that cannot be proved whole at the W1 exit is split, never claimed whole). **W1 exit** closes SC1 (L2 on the real production overlay plus the env-and-volumes contract overlay), SC2a (`raw_script_denied`; 409 `USER_TOOK_OVER` for a user token labelled agent with `QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT=1` on the evidence stack, the flag value named in the PR, the shipped default staying `0`), SC3 (sweeper, caps, RSS runs with `QUARRY_BROWSER_MAX_SESSIONS=48` in the test env), SC4, SC5 (including the Quarry `PageCache` cross-org probe of WS4.K), SC6 (WS5.A to WS5.H including WS5.C; screenshot and PDF formats and the strict-date 400 are W2 or later) and the crawl-bound clause of SC7 (WS6.A: finite default, `clamped_by:["default"]`). **W2 exit** closes SC2b (the Model Plane run pauses, WS11.D, after which the takeover flag defaults to `1`), the rest of SC7 (WS6.B to WS6.E, the token cap, billing codes), SC8, SC9, SC10, SC11 and SC12; SC9 rests on SC1 and SC2a.

### 4.4 Effort roll-up

Assumptions. Days are the designs' own engineer-days after the review's re-estimates (midpoints for ranges: WS2.D 6.5, WS9.J 9, WS5.I 13.5, WS16.J 9); engineer-weeks = days / 5. Columns: core = scheduled and unconditional; gated = blocked by a named decision but scheduled once it lands; opt = optional; unsched = design-level only and in no total. Calendar weeks assume 80% focus. WS6.A (3.5 d) is pulled into W1 as a hotfix and WS3.K (8 d) counts in W2. Sibling-owned days outside the Quarry figure (about 5.5 d: WS6.B +1.5 Model Plane, WS6.E +2 Model Plane and +2 execution-core) are not in the totals. Risk multipliers: W1 x1.15 to x1.5 (small, file-level, mostly verified); W2 x1.3 to x1.8 (cross-plane review, rebases on uncommitted diffs, ADR waits, migration renumbering). The audit's efforts were raised for 33 items after verification, and several designs say the audit understated (D2 S3 S to M, D11 M to L, D14a step 1 S to 10 d, D15 M to L, D10 L to XL). The review corrected the first-draft W1 figure of 113.75 core days to 132.25: WS1.A 10 to 16 d (WS1.A1 10 d and WS1.A2 6 d) plus the new WS1.A0 (1.5 d), WS2.C 5.5 to 10 d, WS3.F 6 to 10 d, WS6.A 1.5 to 3.5 d, the new WS4.K (0.5 d); WS5.C (4 d) moved from optional to gated; WS14.S0b (0.5 d) joins W2. The skeptic put W1 core at about 140 d; the 7.75 d difference is the remaining uncertainty on WS1.A and WS2.C and sits in the risk band, not in a slice. Where an estimate is still light, plan with this band on top of the multipliers: design slices WS15 L2 7 to 12 d, WS16 S6 8 to 14 d, WS17 E2 8 to 14 d.

| Wave | core d | gated d | opt d | unsched d | core+gated d | eng-weeks | risk-adjusted eng-weeks | calendar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | 132.25 | 16 | 6 | 13.5 | 148.25 | 29.7 | 34 to 44 | 6.5 engineers: 6.6 to 8.6 weeks |
| W2 | 447.5 | 63 | 19.5 | 9 | 510.5 | 102.1 | 133 to 184 | 8 eng 21 to 29 wk; 12 eng 14 to 19 wk; 16 eng 10 to 14 wk |
| W1+W2 | 579.75 | 79 | 25.5 | 22.5 | 658.75 | 131.8 | 167 to 228 | about 5 to 7 months end to end |

The critical path (50 d, 13 to 18 weeks risk-adjusted) is a floor, not the estimate. W1 is throughput-bound (about 6.6 to 8.6 weeks at 6.5 engineers). W2 at 12 engineers is about 14 to 19 weeks, where throughput and critical path meet; beyond about 14 engineers the critical path binds and extra people do not shorten W2.

The sibling days above add about 5.5 d to W2.

### 4.5 Feature flags and rollout table

Every behaviour change ships behind a default-off or observe-mode flag, and production defaults flip only after a recorded L2 run (6.2). Prefixes: edge `QUARRY_EDGE__*` (separator `__`; compose anchors drop the prefix, for example `USAGE_BROWSER_METRICS`), driver `QUARRY_BROWSER_*`, Go services `QUARRY_*`, Model Plane `<SERVICE>_*`, gateway unprefixed, SPA `VITE_*`. New flags use only the `QUARRY_EDGE__` form (the raw single-underscore `QUARRY_EDGE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` and `QUARRY_EDGE_ARTIFACT_BACKEND` are read case-sensitively by the production refusals: PRE-2). An unparsable value aborts boot in every new reader; the old `EdgeConfig` loader silently falls back to defaults (S9 `config.rs:334-341`) and must not be copied. Vocabularies differ by design (`off|observe|enforce` in WS7, WS14, WS17; `off|shadow|on` in WS6; `off|shadow|skip|on` in WS5; `lenient|strict` in WS5 and WS14); semantics are common: `observe` equals `shadow`.

| `GATEWAY_RESULT_CACHE_CONTENT` | `on` (`off` disables the two content caches only) | WS4.A | keep (emergency lever; the only safe rollback posture is `GATEWAY_CACHE_REDIS_URL` unset) |
| `QUARRY_ZDR_LOG_FILTER` | on | WS4.E | folds into the WS10.H span processor |
| `QUARRY_EDGE__ZDR_REFUSE_DURABLE_RESOURCES` | observe first, then on | WS4.H (WS15.S1, WS17.B call it; R-25) | after one release at on and customer notice; keep as rollback until then |
| `QUARRY_EDGE__ZDR_TOMBSTONE`, `QUARRY_ZDR_TOMBSTONE_RETENTION_DAYS`, `QUARRY_ZDR_TOMBSTONE_DRY_RUN` | off | WS4.J | enable per environment after contract and legal review; keep the retention knob |

Rollout rules that cut across the table (resolutions R-23, R-26, R-28, R-29 of section 2.3).
- **One logical switch per feature, one per layer.** Human browsing is on only when broker `BROWSER_BROKER_HUMAN_BROWSE_ENABLED`, model-gateway, `QUARRY_EDGE__HUMAN_BROWSE`, gateway `BROWSER_HUMAN_BROWSE` and the SPA `VITE_*` flags are all on; attach likewise (`QUARRY_EDGE__ATTACH`, `BROWSER_ATTACH`). Deploy order: broker, model-gateway, Quarry, gateway. Production stays off everywhere until X-13 and ADR-3 are answered, and the gateway `BROWSER_HUMAN_BROWSE` and `BROWSER_ATTACH` default to `0` in every environment, dev included, until those answers exist; the rollout matrix lives in the WS8 runbook.
- **Planner.** W1 and W2 evidence recipes leave `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM` and `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_PLANNER_MODE` unset (deterministic planner); a recipe that sets planner mode names it.
- **Capacity.** `QUARRY_BROWSER_MAX_SESSIONS` (40) must exceed `QUARRY_EDGE__MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` (32) plus the scrape and heavy-lane budget (1); the three numbers are placeholders pending the RSS runs, which set 48 sessions in their test env; the driver reaper (idle 3600 s, max age 21600 s) sits above every run-sweeper number and the human-browse absolute grant TTL (4 h) equals the interactive backstop (14400 s); a boot check asserts the ordering, WARN-only until the RSS runs are recorded (SC3) and a refusal to boot afterwards.
- **Receipt text.** `QUARRY_EDGE__HUMAN_RECEIPT_MODE` and `QUARRY_EDGE__RECEIPT_TEXT_MODE` stay separate flags over one builder, `redacted_for_record`; the stricter wins for human steps.
- **Mirrored defaults.** The live `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml` [M] defaults `QUARRY_EDGE__AUTOPROMPT` and `SEMANTIC_RERANK` to 0, the committed one to 1, and the untracked switch test asserts 0: never commit one without the other.

**Per-wave deployment-evidence recipe.** Rebuilt local images, a running stack, and a verified end-to-end flow with a stated observable assertion (6.2 defines the standard).

Wave 1 exit evidence, on the rebuilt local stack:
1. WS4.A two-org Redis flow and ZDR bypass counters, WS4.B purge record; WS6.A 7-page crawl; WS2.A `evaluate` answered 403 then `get_content` returns `Example Domain`; WS4.K org B sending org A's fingerprint as `prev_fingerprint` gets a miss; PRE-2 `QUARRY_EDGE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=True` with `ENVIRONMENT=production` refuses to boot (PR 1 with PR 1b, PR 2, PR 3 and PR 4 of 7.2).
2. WS2.C/D: with `QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT=1` on the evidence stack (the PR names the value; the shipped default stays `0`) a user token labelled `initiated_by:"agent"` gets 409 `USER_TOOK_OVER` on the next step during a takeover and succeeds after give back (SC2a; the service-principal refusal is proved by the claims-injecting integration test, and the Model Plane run pause is SC2b in W2); a viewer-less interactive run expires only after 900 s idle (dry-run logs first); a 33rd run returns 429 `org_run_cap` or `global_run_cap` with `Retry-After`.
3. WS3.A/C: `ps` shows zero `--no-sandbox` processes while a browser step succeeds, in dev and the production overlay; two sessions with different viewports do not relaunch Chromium (process start time unchanged). WS3.F: with `QUARRY_BROWSER_MAX_SESSIONS=12` set in the test env file the 13th session returns 429 `browser_session_cap` (the shipped default is 40, and the SC3 RSS runs at 8, 16 and 32 contexts set 48); `pkill chromium` then a new run succeeds; `/ready` carries `browser`.
4. WS1.A0 to WS1.C: the production overlay (WS1.A0: durable artifact backend and `QUARRY_EDGE__DURABLE_EVENT_HISTORY=1`) boots quarry-edge with `ENVIRONMENT=production` and the validator URL set (`/ready` 200) on `docker-compose.yml` plus `docker-compose.production.yml` plus the env-and-volumes contract overlay, and `ps` on that stack shows zero `--no-sandbox` while a `navigate` step returns 200 (WS3.A); an AI browser run end to end through the gateway with `BROWSER_GRANT_ENFORCEMENT=strict`; a broker restart keeps an issued grant valid; `bash scripts/tests/browser-grant-prod-contract.sh` [NEW] green with legs B and C turned from expected-fail to green.
5. WS5.B/C/D: with `DOC_ROUTING=on` on the evidence stack (the production default `on` follows WS5.C) a PDF through `/v1/scrape` returns text with `metadata.content_kind`; an inline ZDR scrape returns markdown and writes no artifact row.
6. Contract gates: `bash scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` and `--self-test`, `node --test scripts/tests/zdr-contract-schema.test.mjs`.

Wave 2 exit evidence:
1. Shared browser (WS8, WS9): a human session opens, the agent attaches in an agent-flagged tab, the user takes over (409 on the agent's next step), gives back and stops; the same run is visible in the dock with the evidence panels.
2. Planner (WS11): stage 1 `allowlist` on a dev org; stage 2 `org_opt_in` production-overlay run with a grant; a budget exhaustion yields 402 `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` and an honest completion; a takeover pauses the Model Plane run with its checkpoint (SC2b), after which `QUARRY_EDGE__TAKEOVER_ENFORCEMENT` defaults to `1`.
3. Crawl and jobs (WS14, WS15): the fixture-site crawl denies off-site and robots-disallowed URLs with typed denials; cancel, pause, resume; a schedule fires on its cron and a posture-violating fire shows `schedule_skipped` (`QUARRY_SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENABLED=1` only after WS14.I).

5. Profiles (WS17): saved and restored across a Quarry restart; envelope rows unreadable without the key; erasure removes them.

Trace, metrics, redaction, policy (WS10, WS6, WS12, WS7): `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/trace` after an AI run; `/metrics` on the internal listener; graceful drain with a live stream; a typed password never appears in receipts, events, artifacts or the planner prompt; a `ResolvedPolicy` denial shows `policy.denied` with `decision_source`.

## 5. Cross-session interfaces

Two sibling planning sessions share pieces of this plan. Sibling (a) is Verevon Space (agent PC and browser inside Spaces, Space grants that must never widen an owner-plane ACL, ZDR-safe telemetry and projections). Sibling (b) is Model Plane plus chat and agents (BrowserBroker grants, agent browser path, delegated bearer, approvals, the `browser.*` tool schema, the execution-core planner, model-gateway `browser_run`, cost-core). Source audits: `01-verevon-space-audit.md` (F-t1-020 room-scoped agent browser, F-t1-021 agent computer confinement, ADR 6) and `03-model-plane-chat-and-agents-audit.md` (F-t3-008 agent browser on real broker grants, F-t3-006 approvals v2, F-t3-002 durable loop, F-t3-018 scheduled runs). "Owner" is the proposed owner of the code; the contract owner is named in the contract column. Every row ends in a question only the user can settle, marked FOR USER TO RECONCILE.

**Rule that governs every row.** Space access can only narrow an owner-plane decision (`apps/master-ownership-matrix.md` rule 10, line 166: projections only narrow access): grants are minted from the owner's bearer, Quarry compares `grant.owner_id` with the run owner, policy meets only tighten, projections hold ids and counters. A Space feature that needs a member to act on or read a browser owned by another member is a new design (a shared-session ACL), out of scope here.

## 6. Verification and regression plan

### 6.1 Per-lane test commands and CI gates

Commands run from the repo root `C:/dev/CoresSystem` unless a `cd` is shown. Evidence tags: `[CI]` stated by a workflow, `[RUN]` executed read-only by the sweeps, `[MEM]` project memory note, not re-verified, `[UNVERIFIED]` needs a real run. ### 6.2 Deployment evidence standard

The repo counts a deployment claim only after rebuilt local images, a running stack and a verified end-to-end flow with a stated observable assertion. No slice, wave exit or production flag flip is called done on a green unit test alone.

Every PR description records: (1) the rebuilt image ids and `SOURCE_REVISION` (the production overlay needs `SOURCE_REVISION` and `BUILD_DATE`; `GET /version` shows the revision); (2) `docker ps` showing the service healthy in the intended mode (for example quarry-edge `ENVIRONMENT=production`); (3) a transcript of the end-to-end flow with its observable assertion; (4) where the slice fixes a defect, a pre-fix capture on the old image; (5) a log scan for the hop (no URL, host, title, query, grant domain, secret canary); (6) rollback notes, including any one-way door (the gateway cache fix must roll back with `GATEWAY_CACHE_REDIS_URL` unset, never set); (7) the stale doc corrected and a line in `apps/STALE_DOC_DELETION_REGISTER.md` [C] (OQ-15).

Evidence types used in the success criteria: **CI** hermetic test in CI; **L2** live prod-overlay stack run recorded in the PR; **LOG** log or artifact scan with a canary; **PROBE** scripted adversarial request. L2 is a pre-merge evidence run on a developer or self-hosted host, not a GitHub-hosted job (it needs outbound HTTPS to `example.com`: the broker requires dotted non-IP hostnames and Quarry's SSRF guard blocks private targets, so a local fixture site cannot stand in). L2 runs on the real production overlay (`docker-compose.yml` plus `docker-compose.production.yml`) plus a contract overlay that may only set env and volumes and never removes a production hardening key (SC1).

**Stack recipes (project memory and S9, not re-verified in this pass).**
- Ingestion Plane: `cd "apps/Ingestion Plane" && make up` passes only two env files; the memory recipe passes a longer env-file chain (Control and Application `.env.generated-secrets`, `Quarry-v2/.env`, the core `.env` files, `apps/Ingestion Plane/.env.generated-secrets` last) because required interpolations such as `QUARRY_CONTROL_API_KEY` may be unset `[UNVERIFIED]`. Override the macOS `CORE_SYSTEM_CACHE_ROOT` and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` defaults on Windows. The edge is at `127.0.0.1:8082` here and `127.0.0.1:38080` in the standalone compose; `make test-endpoints` checks edge `:8082/health`, imports `:3025/ready`, integration `:3026/health`.
- Gateway and SPA: image swap with `swap_gateway_image.py`, then restart the frontend. `:5173` is the main checkout's container over a Windows bind mount, so HMR never sees host edits: restart the container (the browser also caches `global.css`); a worktree needs its own dev server.
- Model Plane: `bash "apps/Model Plane/scripts/compose.sh" up -d --no-deps --build <service>` (needs `MODEL_PLANE_RUNTIME_ENV_FILE` as an absolute, canonical, regular, non-symlink file). Control Plane: `bash "apps/Control Plane/scripts/run-control-plane.sh" build <svc>` then `up -d --no-deps --build <svc>` (a bare `docker compose build` exits 0 and builds nothing). Convex: `docker restart convex-gateway`, wait for "Convex functions ready!".

### 6.4 Cross-plane contract tests

**A. The production-mode browser contract test (WS1.A1 for L1, WS1.A2 for L2, design D1 slice 1a).** Every "fails in production" statement in the audit is inference; this test turns it into a recorded result and then a regression gate. Two layers, deliberately outside any single plane (precedent: `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`, `quarry-model-plane-switches.test.mjs`):
- **L1, hermetic, CI-gated:** `scripts/tests/browser-grant-contract.test.mjs` [NEW] (`node:test`, reads files, no network), run by `.github/workflows/browser-grant-contract.yml` [NEW] together with `bash scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`. Assertions: (1) `quarry-edge` holds `browser-broker`/`browser:read` and no principal holds `browser:write` on `browser-broker`; (2) manifest row `browser-grant-validate` is `granted:true` and byte-identical in auth-core's vendored copy (sha256 match); (3) proto field numbers pinned (`AcquireGrantRequest` 1-10, `ValidateGrantResponse` 1-12, `DeriveRunGrantRequest` 1-6 after WS1.B, none reused or renamed); (4) gateway `chat/shared.rs` contains the literal `x-browser-authorization`, `browser.rs` calls `required_browser_token` and contains no `format!("session:` (after WS1.B); (5) single minting path: the only non-test source hits for `acquire_grant(` in `apps/Model Plane/rust`, the gateway source and `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates` are `model-gateway/src/browser_grants.rs` and, until WS1.B deletes it, the zero-caller `GrpcGrantValidator::acquire`; (6) compose: the broker block lists `inter-plane-bus`, the production overlay requires the validator URL, the contract overlay only sets env and volumes and removes no production hardening key; (7) after WS1.C the grants migration has no `zdr` column.
- **L2, live prod-mode stack:** `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/tests/e2e/browser-grants-prod-contract.spec.ts` [NEW] (Playwright API `request` fixture, no rendering; reuses `tests/e2e/auth.setup.ts` storage state and the `local` project) and wrapper `scripts/tests/browser-grant-prod-contract.sh` [NEW], which with `--boot` runs the repo's own recipes in order: auth-core rebuild through `apps/Control Plane/scripts/run-control-plane.sh` [C], `BROWSER_BROKER_GRANT_TTL_SECONDS=45` broker and model-gateway through `compose.sh`, quarry-edge on `docker-compose.yml` plus `docker-compose.production.yml` (bootable after WS1.A0: durable artifact backend and `QUARRY_EDGE__DURABLE_EVENT_HISTORY: "1"`) with the longer env-file chain plus the test-only overlay `apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.grant-contract.yml` [NEW], which may only set env and volumes and never removes a production hardening key (`ENVIRONMENT: production`, both dev bypasses `0`, the artifact root on a named volume, `QUARRY_EDGE__BROWSER_GRANT_VALIDATOR_GRPC_URL: http://browser-broker:9095`), then the gateway image swap. Posture is proved, not read: a user-token `POST /v1/agent/runs` straight to Quarry without `grant_id` must return 403 `browser grant_id is required` (`agent_routes.rs` 1377-1383, confirmed in the live tree); a 200 aborts the run as "not prod mode". WS1.A0 closes every boot bail of `main.rs` 132-241 and the durable gate 694-708 (a 0.5-day spike records each one first), and the PR records the WS3.A proof on the same stack: `ps` shows zero `--no-sandbox` and a `navigate` step returns 200.
- **Legs.** A (green at the end of WS1.A2): A1 `GET /api/browser-broker/token` and `/api/model-plane/token` return 200; A2 model-gateway `POST /v1/browser/grants {allowed_domains:["example.com"]}` returns a 32-hex `grant_id` and `kind=="session"`; A3 a Quarry start with a grant and a hostile client `constraints.allowed_domains` returns a `run_id`; A4 `/step` navigate to `https://example.com` is 200 and to `https://evil.example` is FORBIDDEN (domains came from the broker); A5 negatives: no `grant_id` 403, forged id 403, revoke then `/step` 403 (not 5xx, the G6 fix), after the 45 s TTL 403; A6 another user's grant 403 or 404; A7 no domain strings in broker, model-gateway or gateway logs. B (gateway session) and C (AI run through the gateway; the run-event replay must contain `BrowserActionDispatched` and `BrowserObservationReceived` and no `401|403|PermissionDenied|Unauthenticated|not authorized`) are expected-fail in WS1.A2 and green in WS1.B; they are written with Playwright `test.fail()` so an unexpected pass fails the suite and WS1.B cannot forget to remove them. The deterministic planner (no `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM`) keeps it LLM-free.
- **Per-hop log scan** after the happy legs and before the negative controls: `docker logs --since <T0>` for gateway, model-gateway, execution-core, quarry-edge and browser-broker, grepped for `\b40[13]\b`, `PermissionDenied`, `Unauthenticated`, `browser grant is not authorized`, `browser grant_id is required`; any hit fails the run and names the hop.
- **Quarry crate tests** `quarry-edge/tests/browser_grants_prod.rs` [NEW] (the first tests ever with `require_browser_grants: true`): `prod_start_run_without_grant_is_403`, `prod_start_run_with_active_grant_overrides_client_domains`, `prod_step_with_revoked_grant_is_403_not_5xx`, `prod_validator_mints_org_scoped_browser_broker_token`, `prod_boot_refuses_http_only_validator`, `prod_boot_refuses_grpc_validator_without_service_tokens`, plus the `token_request_contract` row test.

**B. Fixtures and sha256 gates.** The mechanism (`scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` [M], lines 48-419): (a) every GOLDENS row digest matches its pin and any sibling `.sha256` agrees; (b) every VENDORED copy is byte-identical to its golden; (c) the strict loader `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-schema.mjs` [M] accepts the ZDR goldens and the refusal catalogue; (d) every CONSUMERS row has a vendored copy in its tree, else "pending" (fails only under `REQUIRE_CONTRACT`, deliberately unset in CI, so four posture-matrix consumers stay pending). Rust-side pins: `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/token_request_contract.rs` [M], `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/tests/dp_retrieve_contract.rs` [U], `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/tests/dp_rerank_contract.rs` [U].

The claims golden `quarry-token-claims.golden.json` exists in three trees (`apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/fixtures/` [C], `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/tests/fixtures/auth-core/` [C], `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/tests/fixtures/auth-core/` [U]) and changes together in one PR (R-13). **C. The ZDR matrix and canary tests (WS4.G, D4 S-7 and S-9).** `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-core/src/zdr_matrix.rs` [NEW] holds `Treatment { Honored, InlineOnly, Degraded{warning}, Refused{code, feature}, Inert{reason} }`, `Row { id, routes, treatment, enforcement, status: Enforced | Gap{issue}, log: Canary{test} | LogUnverified }` and `ROWS`; the golden `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/contracts/zdr-feature-matrix.json` [NEW] is generated from it and its shape is `{contract: "quarry.zdr-feature-matrix", version: 1, catalogue: {contract: "model-plane.zdr-refusals"}, treatments, rows: [{id, routes, treatment, code?, feature?, http?, enforcement, status, issue?}], out_of_catalogue: ["ZDR_REQUIRED"]}`. Quarry refusals keep Quarry's envelope, HTTP status and message text (existing tests assert the message contains "ZDR", `zdr_claim_floor.rs` 842-870) and add `details.zdr_refusal = {code, feature?, action}` with a Model Plane catalogue code (`zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden`, `zdr_feature_not_supported`, `zdr_decision_unavailable`). Tests in `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/tests/zdr_feature_matrix.rs` [NEW]:
- `every_registered_route_has_a_matrix_row` (scans `routes.rs`, `fleet_routes.rs`, `queue_routes.rs` and `agent_routes.rs` or `agent_routes/router.rs`, whichever exists, under `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/`, with `\.route\(\s*"([^"]+)"` after cutting any `#[cfg(test)] mod` block (the test-only routes in `auth.rs` would add 8), normalising `:id` to `{id}`; the extracted set must equal the 85 routes at the time of the PR, and a changed count fails unless `ROUTE_BASELINE_UPDATE=1`) and `every_row_matches_a_registered_route` (stale rows fail), with `route_scan_ignores_cfg_test_modules`, `route_scan_follows_the_agent_routes_split` and `every_row_has_a_log_canary_or_is_marked_log_unverified`;
- `the_golden_and_markdown_are_what_the_table_generates`;
- `every_code_and_feature_the_matrix_names_is_in_the_closed_catalogue_list` (local list of 10 codes and 30 feature keys; WS4.I replaces it with the vendored `zdr-refusals.json`);
- `enforced_refusals_hold` (golden ZDR-org token gets the row's status and a message containing "ZDR"; a standard-org token does not: crawl, batch, persistent profile at agent start, resume);
- `a_service_principal_is_refused_durable_jobs_by_the_scope_gate` and `a_service_principal_with_body_zdr_gets_the_same_persistent_profile_refusal` (built by `264832dd` as the split of the old `a_service_principal_with_body_zdr_gets_the_same_refusals`: both golden service tokens with body `zdr:true` get the route scope gate's 403 on `/v1/crawl` and `/v1/batch`, and `service_execution_core` with `zdr:true` is refused a persistent profile like a ZDR user; the service `zdr` claim is ignored by design);
- `gap_rows_currently_violate` (pins today's behaviour so a fix must flip the row: ZDR-org `POST /v1/schedules {preset:"hourly", target_ref}` returns 200; `/v1/profiles` create and `GET` succeed; `POST /v1/change/snapshot` and `/v1/change/refresh` are not refused). WS4.H inverts these to `zdr_org_cannot_create_a_schedule`, `..._monitor`, `..._profile`, `..._snapshot` with `details.zdr_refusal.code == "zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden"`, wind-down routes (list and delete for schedules, monitors and profiles) still 200 (`zdr_org_can_list_and_delete_profiles`), and `a_refused_request_never_reaches_the_control_plane`.
- **Canary tests.** `quarry-edge/tests/zdr_log_capture.rs` [NEW] (own test binary so a global capturing subscriber is safe): `a_zdr_scrape_logs_no_url_and_no_title_at_the_default_level` (JSON subscriber at `EnvFilter("info")`, probe URL `https://example.com/zdr-probe-<uuid>`; fails on the current tree at `apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs` 821, which is the point), the control `a_non_zdr_scrape_still_logs_page_extracted_with_the_url`, `scrape_meter_metadata_under_zdr_has_no_url_or_fingerprint`; `serp.rs` unit test `search_provider_errors_do_not_embed_the_query`; gateway `tests/cache_admission_only.rs` (source scan: `cache.lookup(` and `cache.store(` forbidden under `src/domains/**`) and `log_field_discipline.rs`. WS12 adds a seeded-secret canary, WS4.B/WS1.A2 log scans use the same pattern.
- **Never-loosen rule.** A test fails if an existing refusal row changes to a weaker treatment; the published ZDR matrix is generated from the Rust `ROWS` table (axum has no route attributes), never hand-edited, and its completeness against the registered routes is enforced by the CI route scan above; the zero-log-lines claim is proved per route family by one canary, or the row says `log-unverified`.

**D. Other cross-plane gates a lane must keep green.** `bash scripts/tests/principal-registry-parity.test.sh` and the auth-core contract specs for any registry edit (R-13); the docs contract for any prod-check or principal change; `quarry-core/tests/contracts.rs` 40-60 and the Go `TestErrorCodeStatusMirror` for any wire code (R-10); the gate-order pin `admission_order_is_pinned` for any `step` edit (R-7); the Temporal replay test for any `GetVersion`.

The user said "you decide the optimal build"; the coordinating session decided the open questions of `W3-estimate.md` and they are ratified defaults from now on, recorded as "owner-delegated, decided 2026-10-23":

1. ADR-2: the split is ratified. Build 2a (OTP-only handoff). 2b (secrets) stays unbuilt and gated until the key ceremony and counsel.
2. knowledge.crawl_site (E3.7.9): approval is required above 50 pages; at or below 50 it proceeds under the run budget. The threshold is a tighten-only config, default 50.
3. Office hybrid path (E3.6-6): approved.
4. Fail-closed PII (E3.6-4): approved. A page that fails redaction is dropped with a typed per-page failure; the crawl or batch continues; a partial or unredacted page is never emitted.
5. D9: the approval card renders inline in the transcript and the @tab token renders as an inline chip; no dock is needed (unblocks the swap in W3-B1-06 and E3.3-c).
6. OD13 (E3.2-e1): the consent pattern language is approved as drafted and ships flag-off until counsel reviews the wording; it is not enabled.
7. Migration 021 carries E3.5-1 and the E3.5-6 tag column in one migration; 025 is not used.

Build rules of the same date: one wave at a time, wave mode (no review-fix loops, no per-slice docker rebuilds or live proofs, one light test pass at the end of the wave), Haiku 5.5 for mechanical slices and Sonnet 5.5 high for authority, audit, ZDR, money and data-loss slices, no Opus, at most 3 agents at a time, usage checked between batches.
